chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Sulayman's understanding is described as something God gave, and the same verse says that to each God gave judgment and knowledge [c2]. A reader may notice that the verse does not set one of them against the other [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what each of them judged, or which judgment is meant by it in 21:79.
- Not established: whose field or whose sheep, what damage was done, or whether the matter was brought to both of them together.
- Not established: Sulayman's age at the time; the Quran does not give it.

chapters.title_en: The wind and those who served him

claims.statement_en: For Sulayman God made the wind strong, running by his command to the land that God had blessed.
God says that He subjected the wind to him, running by his command softly to where he directed.
The ayah says that its morning was a month and its evening a month.

God made the spring of qitr flow for him, and some of the jinn worked before him by the permission of his Lord; whoever of them turned from God's command, God would make him taste the punishment of the blaze.

Some of the shayatin, the Arabic plural of shaytan, dived for him and did other work besides, and God was guarding them; the shayatin are also described as every builder and diver, and others bound together in chains.
They made for him whatever he wished of mihrabs, likenesses, basins like great water-troughs, and fixed cooking-pots.
The family of Dawud are told to work in thanks, and God says that few of His servants are thankful.
God told Sulayman that this was His gift, so he could give or withhold without reckoning, and that he has nearness with God and a good place of return.

chapters.summary_md: God made the wind run by Sulayman's command, and some of the jinn and the shayatin worked for him, by God's permission and under God's guarding [c1][c2][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md: For Sulayman God made the wind strong, running by his command to the land that God had blessed [c1]. God says that He subjected the wind to him, running by his command softly to where he directed [c2]. The ayah says that its morning was a month and its evening a month [c3]. God made the spring of qitr flow for him, and some of the jinn worked before him by the permission of his Lord; whoever of them turned from God's command, God would make him taste the punishment of the blaze [c4]. Some of the shayatin, the Arabic plural of shaytan, dived for him and did other work besides, and God was guarding them; the shayatin are also described as every builder and diver, and others bound together in chains [c5]. They made for him whatever he wished of mihrabs, likenesses, basins like great water-troughs, and fixed cooking-pots [c6]. The family of Dawud are told to work in thanks, and God says that few of His servants are thankful [c7]. God told Sulayman that this was His gift, so he could give or withhold without reckoning, and that he has nearness with God and a good place of return [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The wind is called strong in 21:81 and soft in 38:36; the ayat give both words and do not join them [c1][c2]. The ayah on the month does not say what was measured in a month, a journey or a time [c3]. Every service in these ayat is placed under God: by God's permission, with God guarding, and as God's gift [c4][c5][c8]. The words for the things made, mihrabs and likenesses, are left without further description [c6].
chapters.kids_md: God made the wind obey Sulayman, going where he directed [c1][c2]. Some of the jinn and others worked for him, by God's permission [c4][c5]. God told the family of Dawud to give thanks [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Every power described in these ayat is placed under God: the wind runs by his command, the jinn work by God's permission, and the shayatin are guarded by God [c1][c4][c5]. The ayat close this passage with a call to thanks and the remark that few are thankful [c7]. The gift is spoken of as a gift to give or withhold, with a promise of nearness stated for Sulayman [c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how the wind carried him or what it carried, where the land that God blessed was, or whether it is the same land in each place.
- Not established: what the month refers to; the Arabic gives only its morning a month and its evening a month.
- Not established: what qitr is; the word is often read as molten copper or metal, but the ayah does not say so.
- Not established: how the jinn and the shayatin looked or how they worked; this draft describes neither and says only what the ayat say.
- Not established: who the others bound in chains were, or what the chains were; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: what the likenesses were, or whether the same people who made the mihrabs made them.

claims.statement_en: His forces of the jinn, of humankind and of the birds were gathered for Sulayman, and were held in ranks.
When they came to the valley of the ants, an ant said to the ants to enter their dwellings, so that Sulayman and his forces would not crush them while they did not perceive.

He smiled, laughing at her words, and asked his Lord to inspire him to be thankful for the favour on him and on his parents and to do righteous work that pleases God, and to admit him by God's mercy among His righteous servants.

chapters.summary_md: Sulayman's forces were gathered, an ant warned the ants in a valley, and Sulayman smiled and asked God to help him be thankful [c1][c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: His forces of the jinn, of humankind and of the birds were gathered for Sulayman, and were held in ranks [c1]. When they came to the valley of the ants, an ant said to the ants to enter their dwellings, so that Sulayman and his forces would not crush them while they did not perceive [c2]. He smiled, laughing at her words, and asked his Lord to inspire him to be thankful for the favour on him and on his parents and to do righteous work that pleases God, and to admit him by God's mercy among His righteous servants [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ant speaks as one of the ants and says they do not perceive; the ayah gives her words and nothing else about her [c2]. Sulayman's response is a smile and a prayer, not a command [c3]. The prayer names thanks, righteous work and admission among the righteous [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman's forces were gathered, and they came to a valley of ants [c1][c2]. An ant told the other ants to go into their homes [c2]. Sulayman smiled and asked God to help him be thankful [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Sulayman answers what he hears with a smile and a prayer for thankfulness [c3]. A reader may notice that his prayer includes his parents among those who received favour [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the valley of the ants was, or how Sulayman understood the ant; the ayah says that he laughed at her words.
- Not established: the size or make-up of the forces beyond the groups named, or what ranks means in practice.
- Not established: who his parents were beyond what other ayat say; this ayah gives no names.

claims.statement_en: Sulayman looked for the birds and asked why he did not see the hoopoe, or whether it was among the absent.
He said that he would punish it severely or slaughter it, unless it brought him clear authority.
It did not stay away long, and said that it had learned what he had not, and had come to him from Saba with sure news.
It said that it had found a woman who ruled them, who had been given of everything and had a great throne.

It said that it had found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, that Satan had made their deeds seem fair to them and turned them from the way, so that they were not guided and did not prostrate to God, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what they conceal and what they declare; the Arabic wording can also be read as a call to prostrate to God.
The ayah says that God, there is no god but He, is the Lord of the great throne.
Sulayman said that they would see whether it had spoken the truth or was among the liars, and told it to go with his letter, cast it to them, then turn away from them and see what they returned.

chapters.summary_md: Sulayman missed the hoopoe, which returned with news from Saba, and he sent it with a letter to see what they would answer [c1][c3][c7].
chapters.body_md: Sulayman looked for the birds and asked why he did not see the hoopoe, or whether it was among the absent [c1]. He said that he would punish it severely or slaughter it, unless it brought him clear authority [c2]. It did not stay away long, and said that it had learned what he had not, and had come to him from Saba with sure news [c3]. It said that it had found a woman who ruled them, who had been given of everything and had a great throne [c4]. It said that it had found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, that Satan had made their deeds seem fair to them and turned them from the way, so that they were not guided and did not prostrate to God, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what they conceal and what they declare; the Arabic wording can also be read as a call to prostrate to God [c5]. The ayah says that God, there is no god but He, is the Lord of the great throne [c6]. Sulayman said that they would see whether it had spoken the truth or was among the liars, and told it to go with his letter, cast it to them, then turn away from them and see what they returned [c7].
chapters.deep_md: Sulayman asks about the hoopoe and states a threat that depends on clear authority [c1][c2]. The hoopoe answers with a claim of knowledge and a report [c3][c4][c5]. The ayat do not mark where the hoopoe's words end, and the Arabic of 27:25 can be read as a report or as a call; 27:25-26 can be read as its words or as a comment [c5][c6]. Sulayman's reply is to test the report and to send a letter [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman could not see the hoopoe, and asked where it was [c1]. The hoopoe came back with news from Saba [c3]. Sulayman said that he would see if it was telling the truth, and sent it with a letter [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Sulayman asks for clear authority and then checks the report before acting [c2][c7]. The report names prostration to God, who knows what is hidden and what is declared, as what they were turned away from [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where Saba was beyond its name; the ayah gives the name only.
- Not established: where the hoopoe's own words end, whether at 27:25 or 27:26; the Arabic does not mark it.
- Not established: how the hoopoe spoke or how Sulayman understood it; the ayat give its words and say nothing about the manner.
- Not established: whether Sulayman carried out the threat of 27:21; the ayat go on without saying.
- Not established: the name of the woman who ruled, which the ayat do not give; she has her own entry elsewhere in the inventory.

claims.statement_en: The woman told her chiefs that a noble letter had been cast to her, that it was from Sulayman, and that it began with the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
The letter told them not to exalt themselves against him and to come to him submitting.
She asked her chiefs to advise her in her matter, saying she never decided a matter until they were present.
They said that they had strength and fierce might, and that the matter was hers, so she should see what to command.
She said that kings, when they enter a town, ruin it and make its mighty ones humble, and that this is what they do.
She said that she would send them a gift and wait to see with what the messengers returned.

When the messenger came to Sulayman, he asked whether they would help him with wealth, said that what God had given him was better than what He had given them, and said that they rejoiced in their gift.
He told the messenger to return to them, and said that he would come to them with forces they could not face, and would drive them out from there humbled and small.

chapters.summary_md: A letter from Sulayman reached a woman who ruled; she took counsel, sent a gift, and Sulayman answered that what God had given him was better [c1][c3][c6][c7].
chapters.body_md: The woman told her chiefs that a noble letter had been cast to her, that it was from Sulayman, and that it began with the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate [c1]. The letter told them not to exalt themselves against him and to come to him submitting [c2]. She asked her chiefs to advise her in her matter, saying she never decided a matter until they were present [c3]. They said that they had strength and fierce might, and that the matter was hers, so she should see what to command [c4]. She said that kings, when they enter a town, ruin it and make its mighty ones humble, and that this is what they do [c5]. She said that she would send them a gift and wait to see with what the messengers returned [c6]. When the messenger came to Sulayman, he asked whether they would help him with wealth, said that what God had given him was better than what He had given them, and said that they rejoiced in their gift [c7]. He told the messenger to return to them, and said that he would come to them with forces they could not face, and would drive them out from there humbled and small [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The letter is described in the ayat only by its opening and its request [c1][c2]. The woman consults her chiefs and sets out her own view before sending a gift [c3][c4][c5][c6]. Sulayman's reply is about what God has given, and the ayat do not say what the gift was [c7]. The word rendered submitting in 27:31 is muslimin, and its sense here is for the reviewer [c2].
chapters.kids_md: A letter from Sulayman came to the woman who ruled [c1]. She asked her chiefs for advice and sent a gift [c3][c6]. Sulayman said that what God had given him was better than their gift [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The woman is shown taking counsel before she acts [c3][c5]. Sulayman answers a gift by pointing to what God had given him [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the woman's name, her people's number, or the place of her rule beyond the name in 27:22; the ayat do not give them.
- Not established: what the gift was, who carried it, or how many messengers there were; 27:35 has the plural and 27:36 the singular.
- Not established: how the letter was cast to her or how she knew it was from Sulayman.
- Not established: whether the forces threatened in 27:37 were ever sent; the ayat go on to another matter.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: a personal name for this woman is given in later works; it is not used here, and her own entry is elsewhere in the inventory.

claims.statement_en: Sulayman asked his chiefs which of them would bring him her throne before they came to him submitting.
An ifrit of the jinn said that he would bring it before Sulayman rose from his place, and that he was strong and trustworthy for it.

One who had knowledge from the Book said that he would bring it before Sulayman's glance returned to him; when Sulayman saw it settled by him, he said that this was from the bounty of his Lord, to test whether he would give thanks or be ungrateful, and that whoever gives thanks does so for himself, and whoever is ungrateful, his Lord is self-sufficient and generous.
He said to disguise her throne for her, to see whether she was guided or among those not guided.
When she came, she was asked whether her throne was like this, and she said that it seemed to be it, and that they had been given knowledge before her and had been submitting.
What she used to worship other than God had kept her back, for she was of a people who disbelieved.
She was told to enter the sarh, and when she saw it she took it for a pool of water; he said that it was a sarh made smooth, of glass.
She said, my Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds.

chapters.summary_md: Sulayman asked who would bring her throne; it was brought, he gave thanks to his Lord, and when she came she said that she submitted with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds [c1][c3][c8].
chapters.body_md: Sulayman asked his chiefs which of them would bring him her throne before they came to him submitting [c1]. An ifrit of the jinn said that he would bring it before Sulayman rose from his place, and that he was strong and trustworthy for it [c2]. One who had knowledge from the Book said that he would bring it before Sulayman's glance returned to him; when Sulayman saw it settled by him, he said that this was from the bounty of his Lord, to test whether he would give thanks or be ungrateful, and that whoever gives thanks does so for himself, and whoever is ungrateful, his Lord is self-sufficient and generous [c3]. He said to disguise her throne for her, to see whether she was guided or among those not guided [c4]. When she came, she was asked whether her throne was like this, and she said that it seemed to be it, and that they had been given knowledge before her and had been submitting [c5]. What she used to worship other than God had kept her back, for she was of a people who disbelieved [c6]. She was told to enter the sarh, and when she saw it she took it for a pool of water; he said that it was a sarh made smooth, of glass [c7]. She said, my Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds [c8].
chapters.deep_md: In the ayat an ifrit of the jinn makes one offer and a person with knowledge from the Book makes another; the ayat describe neither [c2][c3]. Sulayman's words on seeing the throne are about thanks and about test [c3]. The ayat leave the speaker of the sentence that she was kept back in 27:43 as the narration [c6]. The final words are hers and are a prayer and a statement of submission [c8].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman asked who could bring her throne [c1]. It was brought, and Sulayman said that it was a gift from his Lord, to see if he would give thanks [c3]. Then she said that she submitted to God, Lord of the worlds [c8].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Sulayman receives what is brought to him as a test of thanks and not as pride [c3]. The woman ends with an admission that she had wronged herself and a statement of submission to God [c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the throne was brought from, how it was brought, or what it was made of; the ayat give no description of it.
- Not established: who the one with knowledge from the Book was; the ayah does not name him or say what the knowledge was.
- Not established: what the sarh was, where it was, or its size; the ayah says only that it was made smooth, of glass.
- Not established: who said it was a sarh made smooth, of glass; the verb is he said, and this draft reads it as Sulayman.
- Not established: whom the pronoun in given knowledge before her points to, and whose knowledge it is; the Arabic is open, and 27:43 can be read in more than one way.
- Not established: how the disguising of the throne was done, or what she knew; the ayat give only her answer.
- Not established: the order of these events in relation to the others in this story; the draft follows the order of the ayat for reading only.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: a name is given in later works to the one with knowledge from the Book, and the woman has a personal name there; neither is used here.

claims.statement_en: In the evening there were presented to him the standing and swift ones, a phrase in which the Arabic does not name the animal.
He said that he had loved the love of good things in place of the remembrance of his Lord, until it was hidden behind the veil.
He said to bring them back to him, and he began to pass over the legs and the necks, a verb that the Arabic readers take in more than one way.
God says that He tested Sulayman and cast a body upon his throne, and that he then turned back.
He said, my Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that is not fitting for anyone after me; you are the giver.

chapters.summary_md: Sulayman spoke of his love of good things in place of remembering his Lord, God tested him, and he turned back and asked forgiveness and a kingdom for no one after him [c2][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md: In the evening there were presented to him the standing and swift ones, a phrase in which the Arabic does not name the animal [c1]. He said that he had loved the love of good things in place of the remembrance of his Lord, until it was hidden behind the veil [c2]. He said to bring them back to him, and he began to pass over the legs and the necks, a verb that the Arabic readers take in more than one way [c3]. God says that He tested Sulayman and cast a body upon his throne, and that he then turned back [c4]. He said, my Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that is not fitting for anyone after me; you are the giver [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not say what it refers to in until it was hidden behind the veil [c2]. The test is stated in the words of God, and the ayah says no more than that a body was cast upon his throne [c4]. The Arabic word for his throne here is kursi, a different word from the arsh used of the great throne in the account of the woman who ruled [c4]. His prayer asks for forgiveness and for a kingdom of a particular kind [c5].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman said that he had loved good things so much that he forgot to remember his Lord [c2]. Then God tested him, and he turned back and asked God to forgive him [c4][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Sulayman's turning back is joined to a prayer for forgiveness [c4][c5]. A reader may notice that he names his own loving of good things as something that took him from remembering God [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the standing and swift ones were; the Arabic does not name them, though they are commonly read as horses.
- Not established: what it refers to in the veil clause, whether the sun or the animals; the Arabic does not say.
- Not established: what Sulayman did to the legs and necks, which reading of the verb is meant, or why he did it.
- Not established: what the body upon his throne was, or how the test happened; the ayah gives no more, and this draft adds no account.
- Not established: how long the test lasted or what his love of good things had caused him to miss.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: accounts that identify the body or give details of the test; none is used here and none is vouched for.

claims.statement_en: When God decreed death upon Sulayman, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff.
When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.

chapters.summary_md: When God decreed death upon Sulayman, a creature of the earth eating his staff was what showed his death, and when he fell the jinn saw that they did not know the unseen [c1][c2].
chapters.body_md: When God decreed death upon Sulayman, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name Sulayman in its own words; the pronoun looks back to the verses before it [c1]. It does not say how he was placed when he died, only that he fell [c1][c2]. The point made about the jinn is about knowledge of the unseen [c2].
chapters.kids_md: When Sulayman died, a creature of the earth eating his staff was what showed it [c1]. Then the jinn saw that they did not know the unseen [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayah ends with a statement about the jinn and the unseen: that if they had known it, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment [c2]. A reader may take from this that knowledge of the unseen is not possessed by the jinn [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how long Sulayman was dead before he fell, how he was placed, or what he was doing; the ayah says none of this.
- Not established: what the staff was like, or what the creature of the earth was; the Arabic names it only as a creature of the earth.
- Not established: what work or punishment the jinn were in; the ayah says only the humiliating punishment.
- Not established: how the jinn learned of his death, beyond that it became clear to them when he fell.

chapters.title_en: What was followed about his kingdom

claims.statement_en: The ayah says that they followed what the shayatin recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman; the Arabic word for concerning can also mean over or in the time of.
It says that Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the shayatin disbelieved, teaching people magic.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah says that Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the shayatin disbelieved, teaching people magic, and that they followed what the shayatin recited concerning his kingdom [c1][c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah says that they followed what the shayatin recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman; the Arabic word for concerning can also mean over or in the time of [c1]. It says that Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the shayatin disbelieved, teaching people magic [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The passage separates Sulayman from the teaching of the shayatin by saying plainly that he did not disbelieve [c2]. The people who followed are not named, only referred to by they [c1].
chapters.kids_md: Some people followed what the shayatin said about Sulayman's kingdom [c1]. The ayah says that Sulayman did not disbelieve [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayah clears Sulayman of disbelief in plain words [c2]. A reader may notice that it places the teaching of magic with the shayatin [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who they are in this ayah, what exactly the shayatin recited, or how it concerned his kingdom.
- Not established: what the magic was or how it was taught; this draft says nothing about it beyond the words of the ayah.
- Not established here: the rest of 2:102, which speaks of a revelation to angels in a place named there; it has its own entry and is not used in this draft.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Sulayman, the jinn and the birds. None is used in this draft.

Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: a personal name for the woman who ruled Saba, a name for the one with knowledge from the Book, and details of the test of the body and of the death. None is used in the story texts.

A scholar should check these wordings first: the month of 34:12, qitr, the standing and swift ones and the verb for the legs and the necks in 38:31-33, the reading of the veil clause, the body upon the throne in 38:34, the sarh and the glass in 27:44, who speaks the last clause of 27:44 before her own words, and the sense of concerning in 2:102.

The chapters follow a reading order (knowledge and thanks, the field, the wind and those who served him, the ants, the hoopoe, the letter, the throne, the test, the death, the claim about his kingdom). The Quran does not give a chronology across these surahs.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: Ilyas is among the messengers.
He asked his people whether they would not be mindful of God.
He asked whether they called on Baal and abandoned the best of creators, God, their Lord and the Lord of their forefathers of old.
They called him a liar, and so they will be brought forward, except the devoted servants of God.
God left something upon him among those who came later; the Arabic does not state what.
Peace is pronounced upon Ilyasin.
God says that thus He rewards those who do good, and that Ilyas was among His believing servants.

chapters.summary_md: Ilyas is among the messengers and asked his people whether they would not be mindful of God [c1][c2]. They called him a liar [c4]. He is among God's believing servants [c7].
chapters.body_md:
Ilyas is among the messengers [c1]. He asked his people whether they would not be mindful of God [c2]. He asked whether they called on Baal and abandoned the best of creators, God, their Lord and the Lord of their forefathers of old [c3].

They called him a liar, and so they will be brought forward, except the devoted servants of God [c4]. God left something upon him among those who came later [c5]. Peace is pronounced upon Ilyasin [c6]. God says that thus He rewards those who do good, and that Ilyas was among His believing servants [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passage opens with Ilyas's place among the messengers [c1] and gives his message as questions [c2][c3]. The people's answer is that they called him a liar, and the verse speaks of their being brought forward, with an exception for the devoted servants of God [c4]. The rest of the passage speaks of what God left upon him, peace, reward for those who do good, and his place among the believing servants [c5][c6][c7].
chapters.kids_md: Ilyas was a messenger of God [c1]. He asked his people whether they would not be mindful of God, and whether they called on Baal and left the best of creators [c2][c3]. They said he was not telling the truth [c4]. God counted Ilyas among His believing servants [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Ilyas's message was a question put to his own people about whom they called on [c2][c3]. Another is that the passage separates the response of the people from the verdict God gives on his servant [c4][c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where Ilyas lived, how long he preached, or how many followed him.
- Not established: what Baal is in this verse. The word can also mean 'lord' or 'master', and the verse does not say whether a person, a statue or something else is meant.
- Not established: what being 'brought forward' means, and who the 'devoted servants' who are excepted are.
- Not established: what God left upon him among those who came later.
- Not established: whether Ilyasin, in the verse of peace, is another form of the name Ilyas, as is often assumed, or names his family or followers; the spelling in this text divides the word into separate parts, and this draft does not decide.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later writers identify Ilyas with a figure known from earlier scriptures as Elijah; none of that is used here.

claims.statement_en: Ilyas is named in a list with other figures, and each of those named is described as one of the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: Ilyas is named in a list of figures, each of them one of the righteous [c1].
chapters.body_md: Ilyas is named in a list with other figures, and each of those named is described as one of the righteous [c1].
chapters.deep_md: The verse is a list: Ilyas is one entry, and the description one of the righteous covers every entry [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God named Ilyas as one of the righteous [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran can honour a person simply by naming him among the righteous [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the other names in the list are not told in this draft; they belong to the stories of those figures.
- Not established: any act of Ilyas in this verse.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.

37:125: the Arabic word ba'l can mean a lord or master, a husband, or a name of a deity; the draft writes 'Baal' and says in the unknowns that the verse does not define it. A scholar should decide how the page should word it.

37:127-128: the verb rendered 'will be brought forward' has no object or place in the verse, and the exception ('except the devoted servants of God') is read in more than one way; the draft keeps both open.
37:129: the object of the verb is omitted in the Arabic and the draft leaves it so.
37:130: the Quran text spells the name in the peace-verse as separate words; the draft writes 'Ilyasin' and does not say whether it is the same person.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Ilyas is identified by later writers with Elijah and given a biography; none of this is used.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

chapters.title_en: Named among the favoured and the best

claims.statement_en: Alyasa is named in a list with Ismail and others, and God says that He favoured each of those named over the worlds.
Alyasa is named again, with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the best.

chapters.summary_md: Alyasa is named in a list with Ismail and others, each of whom God favoured over the worlds [c1]. He is named again with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl as one of the best [c2].
chapters.body_md:
Alyasa is named in a list with Ismail and others, and God says that He favoured each of those named over the worlds [c1].

Alyasa is named again, with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the best [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The Quran names Alyasa in lists [c1][c2]. One list gives a statement of favour over the worlds [c1]. The other gives a short description, among the best [c2].
chapters.kids_md: God named Alyasa with Ismail and others and said He favoured each of them [c1]. In another place God named Alyasa with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl and said each was among the best [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran can honour a person with a brief mention and no story, and that the honour is stated by God [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: anything Alyasa did or said, where or when he lived, or to whom he was sent.
- Not established: whether the Quran calls him a prophet or a messenger in these verses; the lists describe him as favoured and among the best.
- Not established: what 'favoured over the worlds' covers.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later writers identify Alyasa with a figure known from earlier scriptures as Elisha and as the successor of Ilyas; none of that is used here.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.
6:86: 'favoured over the worlds' is a statement about each of those named; a scholar should check whether the draft's wording is strong enough, too strong, or fits the word 'worlds'.
6:87 follows the list and describes those chosen and guided, but it is outside Alyasa's inventory range and is not used.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Alyasa is identified by later writers with Elisha, the successor of Ilyas; none of that is used.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

chapters.title_en: The messenger and the loaded ship

claims.statement_en: God says that Yunus was among the messengers.
He fled to the laden ship.
There was a casting of lots, using a verb with no named subject, and he was among the losers.

chapters.summary_md: Yunus was among the messengers; he fled to the laden ship, and in the casting of lots he was among the losers [c1][c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: God says that Yunus was among the messengers [c1]. He fled to the laden ship [c2]. There was a casting of lots, using a verb with no named subject, and he was among the losers [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The Arabic verb for fled, abaqa, is the verb used for one who runs away; the ayah does not say from what [c2]. The verb for the lots, sahama, has no named subject, and the word for the losers, mudhadin, means those who were overcome [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Yunus was one of God's messengers [c1]. He went away on a ship that was full [c2]. There was a casting of lots, and he was one of those who lost [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat state that Yunus was among the messengers and state in the next words that he fled [c1][c2]. A reader may notice that both are said plainly, side by side [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what he fled from, where the ship was going, or who else was aboard; the ayat say only that it was laden.
- Not established: who cast the lots, how, or why; the verb has no named subject.
- Not established: whether this came before or after the sending to his people in 37:147; the order of the ayat is not an order of time.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: names for the city of his people and for the sea; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The one called dhu al-nun, the one of the fish, whom this draft reads as Yunus, went off angry and thought that God would not have power over him; the Arabic verb can also be read as that God would not restrict him.
He called out in the darknesses, "There is no god but You, glory be to You, I was among the wrongdoers".
God answered him and saved him from the distress, and said that in this way He saves the believers.

chapters.summary_md: The one of the fish went off angry, called out in the darknesses, and God answered him and saved him from the distress [c1][c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: The one called dhu al-nun, the one of the fish, whom this draft reads as Yunus, went off angry and thought that God would not have power over him; the Arabic verb can also be read as that God would not restrict him [c1]. He called out in the darknesses, "There is no god but You, glory be to You, I was among the wrongdoers" [c2]. God answered him and saved him from the distress, and said that in this way He saves the believers [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the title dhu al-nun and does not use the name Yunus; reading it as Yunus is an inference from the accounts of the fish elsewhere [c1]. The word for the darknesses is plural, and the ayah does not say what they were or where [c2]. His call has parts: that there is no god but God, that God is glorified, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c2]. The ayah ends by speaking of the believers in general [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The one of the fish went away angry [c1]. He called out to God in the darknesses, and God answered him and saved him [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The call in the darknesses begins with the oneness of God and glorifying Him before it says anything about himself [c2]. The ayah then links God's saving of him to God's saving of the believers [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the darknesses were, or where; the ayah does not say that they were in the belly of the fish, and this draft does not say so either.
- Not established: what he was angry about, or with whom.
- Not established: the sense of the Arabic verb for power, whether to have power over him or to restrict him; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: what the distress was, beyond that God saved him from it.

chapters.title_en: The fish and the bare land

claims.statement_en: The fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.
Had he not been one of those who glorify God, he would have stayed in its belly until the day they are raised.
God cast him on the bare land while he was sick.
God caused a plant of the kind called yaqtin to grow over him.

chapters.summary_md: The fish swallowed him, God cast him on the bare land, and caused a plant to grow over him [c1][c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: The fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy [c1]. Had he not been one of those who glorify God, he would have stayed in its belly until the day they are raised [c2]. God cast him on the bare land while he was sick [c3]. God caused a plant of the kind called yaqtin to grow over him [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat join his being swallowed with his being blameworthy, and then name glorifying as what changed the outcome [c1][c2]. The bare land is named as the place where God cast him [c3]. The plant is given by the name of its kind, yaqtin, and nothing more is said of it [c4].
chapters.kids_md: A fish swallowed him [c1]. He glorified God, and God cast him on the bare land [c2][c3]. God made a plant grow over him [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat say that glorifying God made the difference to how he fared in the belly of the fish [c2]. A reader may notice that after the rescue he is described as sick and is given a plant over him [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how long he was in the belly, or how he was cast out; the ayat give no duration and no further account.
- Not established: where the bare land was, or what kind of land it was beyond the word for bare.
- Not established: what a plant of the yaqtin kind is exactly; later readers have taken it as a gourd, but the ayah says only the name of the kind.
- Not established: what blameworthy points to, or how he was sick; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: how this chapter relates in time to the darknesses of the chapter on his call; the ayat do not say.

claims.statement_en: The one addressed is told to be patient for the decision of his Lord and not to be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was choked with grief.
Had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been thrown on the bare land while he was blamed.
His Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: The companion of the fish called out choked with grief; a favour from his Lord reached him, and his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous [c1][c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: The one addressed is told to be patient for the decision of his Lord and not to be like the companion of the fish, when he called out while he was choked with grief [c1]. Had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been thrown on the bare land while he was blamed [c2]. His Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat use the title companion of the fish, and reading it as Yunus is an inference from the account of the fish elsewhere [c1]. The ayat name a favour from his Lord as what changed his outcome [c2]. They end by saying that his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God tells the one addressed to be patient and not to be like the companion of the fish [c1]. A favour from his Lord reached him, and his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat give the story of the companion of the fish as a lesson in patience for the one addressed [c1]. They name his Lord's favour and his Lord's choosing as what stands at the end of it [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the one addressed is; the ayat do not name him.
- Not established: what he called out, or when; the ayat say only that he called out while choked with grief.
- Not established: what the favour from his Lord was, or how it reached him; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: how these ayat relate in time to 21:87-88 and 37:139-148; they are read together here only because they speak of the same companion of the fish.

claims.statement_en: God sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
They believed, and God let them enjoy life for a while.

The ayah asks why no town believed so that its belief benefited it, except the people of Yunus; when they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and let them enjoy life for a while.

chapters.summary_md: God sent Yunus to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed; God removed the punishment of disgrace from them and let them enjoy life for a while [c1][c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: God sent him to a hundred thousand or more [c1]. They believed, and God let them enjoy life for a while [c2]. The ayah asks why no town believed so that its belief benefited it, except the people of Yunus; when they believed, God removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and let them enjoy life for a while [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The number in 37:147 is a hundred thousand with the words or more, and the ayah says no more of how many [c1]. Both ayat use the same expression for the while for which they were allowed to enjoy life [c2][c3]. The ayah at 10:98 sets the people of Yunus apart from the towns whose belief came too late to benefit them [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God sent Yunus to a great many people, a hundred thousand or more [c1]. They believed, and God let them enjoy life for a while [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat present the belief of the people of Yunus as unlike the belief of other towns, since it benefited them [c3]. A reader may notice that their belief is followed by the removal of a punishment and by a time of enjoying life [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether the sending in 37:147 was before or after the fish; the verse carries no word of time, and the order of the ayat is not an order of time.
- Not established: the name or place of the town, what the punishment of disgrace was, or how it was removed.
- Not established: how long the while was, or what became of them after it.
- Not established: whether the hundred thousand or more are all of his people, or how they were counted.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Yunus, the fish and the supplication of 21:87. None is used in this draft.
The titles dhu al-nun (21:87) and companion of the fish (68:48) are read as Yunus by an inference from 37:139-142; a scholar should confirm that wording.
The ayat do not say what the darknesses of 21:87 were or where; this draft does not join them to the belly of the fish.
The order of the chapters is a reading order; the sending to his people (37:147-148, 10:98) is not placed before or after the fish.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: names for the city, the sea and the length of his time away. None is used.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: Zakariyya was made guardian of Maryam, whom her Lord had accepted with a good acceptance and caused to grow well.
Whenever Zakariyya went in to her in the mihrab, he found provision with her, and he asked her where she had this from.
She said that it is from God, and that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya was made guardian of Maryam, and whenever he went in to her in the mihrab he found provision with her, which she said was from God [c1][c2][c3].
chapters.body_md: Zakariyya was made guardian of Maryam, whom her Lord had accepted with a good acceptance and caused to grow well [c1]. Whenever Zakariyya went in to her in the mihrab, he found provision with her, and he asked her where she had this from [c2]. She said that it is from God, and that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah names Zakariyya as her guardian and as the one who went in to her [c1][c2]. The question about the provision is his, and the answer is hers [c2][c3]. This draft states only what concerns Zakariyya here; the rest of Maryam's account is in her own entry [c1].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya looked after Maryam [c1]. When he went in to her, he found food and drink with her, and she told him it was from God [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Maryam's answer places her provision with God, who gives to whom He wills [c3]. A reader may notice that Zakariyya asks about what he finds and receives an answer that points to God [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the provision was, or how it came; the ayah says only provision.
- Not established: how Zakariyya was related to Maryam, or how long he was her guardian; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: whether the Arabic wording makes God or Zakariyya the one acting in kaffalaha; this draft says that Zakariyya was made her guardian, and the reviewer checks the recitation.
- Not established: where the mihrab was or what it was.

claims.statement_en: There Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking for good offspring from Him, and said that God hears supplication.
The ayah is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya, when he called on his Lord with a hidden call.
He said that his bone had grown weak and his head had flared with white, and that he had never been unfortunate in calling on his Lord.

He said that he feared the kinsfolk who would come after him, and that his wife was barren, and asked God for an heir from Himself who would inherit from him and from the family of Yaqub, and to make him pleasing.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya called on his Lord in a hidden call for good offspring, speaking of his weakness, his fear for what would come after him, and his wife's barrenness [c1][c2][c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: There Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking for good offspring from Him, and said that God hears supplication [c1]. The ayah is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya, when he called on his Lord with a hidden call [c2]. He said that his bone had grown weak and his head had flared with white, and that he had never been unfortunate in calling on his Lord [c3]. He said that he feared the kinsfolk who would come after him, and that his wife was barren, and asked God for an heir from Himself who would inherit from him and from the family of Yaqub, and to make him pleasing [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give the prayer in different forms: a short request for good offspring (3:38) and a longer one that speaks of his weakness, his fear and his wife (19:4-6) [c1][c3][c4]. The longer form is introduced as a mention of the mercy of his Lord to His servant [c2]. The word for his hidden call means a call made quietly [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya called quietly to his Lord and asked for a child to come after him [c1][c2][c4]. He said that he had never been unhappy when he called on his Lord [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The prayer begins with the speaker's weakness and his history of calling on God, before he asks for anything [c3]. A reader may notice that the prayer is described as a hidden call and as a mercy [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Zakariyya's age, or the age or name of his wife, or how long she had been barren; the ayat give none of these.
- Not established: who the kinsfolk are or what he feared from them.
- Not established: what the heir was to inherit, whether property, prophethood or knowledge; the ayah says only from him and from the family of Yaqub.
- Not established: where or when he prayed beyond the setting of the preceding verse; the ayat give no further detail.

claims.statement_en: The angels called to him while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous.
He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren; the answer was that in this way God does what He wills.
He was addressed by name as Zakariyya and told that God gives him good news of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom God had not made a namesake before.
He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached the extreme of old age.
The answer was that it is so, that his Lord says it is easy for Him, and that He had created him before when he was nothing.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya was given good news of a boy named Yahya, and asked how this could be when old age had reached him and his wife was barren; the answer was that God does what He wills [c2][c3][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md: The angels called to him while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren; the answer was that in this way God does what He wills [c2]. He was addressed by name as Zakariyya and told that God gives him good news of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom God had not made a namesake before [c3]. He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached the extreme of old age [c4]. The answer was that it is so, that his Lord says it is easy for Him, and that He had created him before when he was nothing [c5].
chapters.deep_md: Both passages give good news, a question from Zakariyya, and an answer from God [c1][c2][c3][c4][c5]. In 3:39 the good news comes from the angels, in 19:7 it is given in the voice of God; the ayat do not say whether this is the same moment [c1][c3]. The question is the same in each place and refers to old age and to his wife being barren [c2][c4]. The answers are that God does what He wills, and that creating him from nothing was easy for God [c2][c5].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya was told that he would have a boy named Yahya [c1][c3]. He asked how this could be, since he was old and his wife could not have a child [c2][c4]. He was told that God does what He wills and that it is easy for Him [c2][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The question about how it can be is answered by pointing to God's will and to God's earlier creation of the questioner [c2][c5]. A reader may notice that the question is asked plainly and that the answer is also given plainly [c2][c4][c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who speaks the answers in 3:40 and 19:9; the verb is he said with no named speaker.
- Not established: whether 3:39 and 19:7 describe the same moment, or whether the angels of 3:39 are the voice of 19:7.
- Not established: Zakariyya's age, or how old his wife was; the ayat say old age and barren, nothing more.
- Not established: the sense of the word for one who holds back, or of the word for namesake, which can also read as equal; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an identification of the word from God in 3:39 with a person; it is not used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: Zakariyya said, my Lord, make a sign for me; the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and that he should remember his Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning.
He said, my Lord, make a sign for me; the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three nights, sawiyyan, a word whose sense is left open here.
He went out to his people from the mihrab and signalled to them to glorify God in the morning and the evening.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya asked for a sign and was told that for three days he would not speak to people except by gesture; he went out from the mihrab and signalled to his people to glorify God morning and evening [c1][c3].
chapters.body_md: Zakariyya said, my Lord, make a sign for me; the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and that he should remember his Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning [c1]. In the other passage the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three nights, sawiyyan, a word whose sense is left open here [c2]. He went out to his people from the mihrab and signalled to them to glorify God in the morning and the evening [c3].
chapters.deep_md: One passage names days and the other names nights, and the ayat do not say how they relate [c1][c2]. In the first passage the sign comes with an instruction to remember God much and to glorify Him [c1]. The signal to his people in the last ayah is a call to glorify God [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya asked God for a sign [c1]. For three days he would not speak to people, except by gesture [c1]. He went out and signalled to his people to glorify God morning and evening [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The sign of silence is joined to a command to remember and glorify God much [c1]. A reader may notice that when he comes out to his people, his gesture calls them to glorify God as well [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: why the sign took this form, or whether it was a limit on his speech or an inability; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: whether the three days of 3:41 and the three nights of 19:10 are the same period; the ayat do not join them.
- Not established: how he signalled, or whether he could still speak to God or glorify; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the sense of sawiyyan; it is read as sound, whole or unbroken, and the reviewer decides the wording.

chapters.title_en: Answered, and named among the righteous

claims.statement_en: Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking not to be left alone, and said that God is the best of inheritors.
God answered him, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him.
The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him.
Zakariyya and Yahya are named, with others, each described as being among the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya called on his Lord not to leave him alone, and God answered him, gave him Yahya and put his wife right for him [c1][c2].
chapters.body_md: Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking not to be left alone, and said that God is the best of inheritors [c1]. God answered him, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him [c2]. The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him [c3]. Zakariyya and Yahya are named, with others, each described as being among the righteous [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The call in 21:89 is brief and ends by naming God as the best of inheritors [c1]. The answer has parts: the gift of Yahya and the putting right of his wife [c2]. The description in the plural that follows does not say who is included [c3]. In 6:85 Zakariyya and Yahya are named among those each described as righteous [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya asked God not to leave him alone [c1]. God answered him and gave him Yahya [c2]. Zakariyya and Yahya are named among the righteous [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat show a prayer made in need and an answer that gives what was asked [c1][c2]. They also describe those spoken of as hastening to good, calling on God in hope and fear, and humble before Him [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what put his wife right means, or whether it refers to her barrenness; the ayah does not say how.
- Not established: who they are in 21:90, whether Zakariyya, his wife and Yahya or others; the plural is not explained.
- Not established: the time between his call and the answer, or how long the answer took.
- Not established: why the others named in 6:85 are grouped with them; this draft states only the part that concerns Zakariyya and Yahya.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Zakariyya, his trade and his death. None is used in this draft.

The age and barrenness details (3:40, 19:4-5, 19:8) are given only as the ayat say them: old age has reached him, his bone has grown weak and his head has flared with white, his wife is barren. A scholar should decide whether the self-description in 19:4 is worded with enough care.
The passages with the glad tidings and the sign (3:39-41 and 19:7-11) are not joined into one scene; the ayat speak of three days in one place and three nights in the other.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Zakariyya's wife, his kinship to Maryam, the trade attributed to him and his death. None is used.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: The angels called to Zakariyya while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous.
God told Zakariyya of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom He had not made a namesake before.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya was given good news of Yahya, a boy with that name for whom God had made no namesake before, a leader and a prophet from among the righteous [c1][c2].
chapters.body_md: The angels called to Zakariyya while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. God told Zakariyya of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom He had not made a namesake before [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The good news in 3:39 describes Yahya in a series of ways: as confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. The good news in 19:7 gives his name and says that the name had no namesake before [c2]. The ayat do not say whether this is the same moment [c1][c2].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya was told that he would have a boy named Yahya [c1][c2]. Yahya would be a leader and a prophet from among the righteous [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The good news gives the name first and the qualities after it [c1][c2]. A reader may notice that being a prophet is joined with being from among the righteous [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the sense of the Arabic hasur, one who holds back, or of sayyid, a leader; the ayah gives the words and the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: what the word from God is; the ayah says only that Yahya confirms it.
- Not established: the sense of the word for namesake, which can also read as equal; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: Yahya's birth, parents' ages or the place of his birth beyond what the ayat of Zakariyya's account say.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an identification of the word from God with a person; it is not used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgment as a child.
God gave him tenderness from Himself, and purity, and he was one who feared God.
He was dutiful to his parents, and was not a tyrant or disobedient.
Peace is on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.

chapters.summary_md: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength; God gave him judgment, tenderness and purity, he feared God and was dutiful to his parents, and peace is on him [c1][c2][c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgment as a child [c1]. God gave him tenderness from Himself, and purity, and he was one who feared God [c2]. He was dutiful to his parents, and was not a tyrant or disobedient [c3]. Peace is on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The first words are a command addressed to him by name [c1]. The following ayat describe him as a description, by what God gave him and by what he was [c2][c3]. The last ayah is a statement of peace on the day of his birth, the day of his death and the day he is raised [c4]. The words tenderness (hanan) and purity (zakah) are given without further explanation [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Yahya was told to hold on firmly to the Book [c1]. He was kind to his parents and was not harsh [c3]. Peace is on him [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The description joins duty to God with duty to parents [c2][c3]. A reader may notice that the ayat on Yahya end with peace upon him on the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which Book Yahya was told to take, or what it contained; the ayah says only the Book.
- Not established: what judgment as a child consisted of, or how old he was; the ayah says child and no more.
- Not established: the exact senses of hanan (tenderness) and zakah (purity) here; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: how he died, or when; the ayah says only the day he dies.
- Not established: whether the peace on him is a greeting or a statement; the ayah has the word alone.

chapters.title_en: Given, and named among the righteous

claims.statement_en: God answered Zakariyya, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him.
The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him.
Yahya is named, with Zakariyya and others, each described as being among the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: God gave Yahya to Zakariyya in answer to his call, and Yahya is named among those each described as righteous [c1][c3].
chapters.body_md: God answered Zakariyya, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him [c1]. The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him [c2]. Yahya is named, with Zakariyya and others, each described as being among the righteous [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah on the gift of Yahya is brief and speaks of the answer to Zakariyya's call [c1]. The description that follows is in the plural and does not say who is included [c2]. In 6:85 Yahya is named in a list, and each in the list is described as righteous [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God answered Zakariyya and gave him Yahya [c1]. Yahya is named among the righteous [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Yahya is spoken of first as a gift from God and then as one of the righteous [c1][c3]. The ayah describes those it speaks of as hastening to good deeds and humble before God [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who they are in 21:90, whether Zakariyya, his wife and Yahya or others; the plural is not explained.
- Not established: what put his wife right means, or whether it refers to her barrenness.
- Not established: why the others named in 6:85 are listed with Yahya; this draft states only the part that concerns Yahya and Zakariyya.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Yahya and his death. None is used in this draft.
The words hasur (3:39), sayyid, hanan and zakah (19:13), the sense of the word for namesake (19:7), and judgment as a child (19:12) are left open; a scholar should decide how the page words each.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the word from God in 3:39 with a person, and accounts of Yahya's life and death. None is used in the story texts.
The Quran gives the glad tidings of Yahya, his description, and the peace upon him; it does not give a story of his life, so the chapters are short.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

chapters.title_en: The wife of Imran and Maryam

claims.statement_en: The wife of Imran said “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated; so accept it from me; indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”

When she gave birth she said “My Lord, I have given birth to a female,” and God knew best what she had given birth to, “and the male is not like the female; I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed.”
Her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and made her grow in a good growth, and made Zakariyya her guardian.

Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab he found provision with her; he said “Maryam, from where is this for you?” and she said “It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without account.”

God tells the listener that this is of the news of the unseen which He reveals, and that the listener was not with those who cast their pens to decide which of them would take charge of Maryam, nor with them when they disputed.

chapters.summary_md: The wife of Imran vowed the child in her womb [c1]. She gave birth to a girl and named her Maryam [c2]. God accepted Maryam, and Zakariyya became her guardian [c3]; he found provision with her [c4]. God says this is news of the unseen [c5].
chapters.body_md: The wife of Imran said she had vowed to her Lord what was in her womb, dedicated, and asked Him to accept it [c1]. When she gave birth she said she had delivered a female, that the male is not like the female, that she had named her Maryam, and that she sought refuge for her and her offspring with God from Satan, the accursed [c2]. Her Lord accepted her with good acceptance, made her grow in a good growth, and made Zakariyya her guardian [c3]. Whenever he came upon her in the mihrab he found provision with her, and she told him it was from God, who provides for whom He wills without account [c4]. God adds that this is news of the unseen, and that the listener was not with those who cast their pens over who would take charge of Maryam [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage makes statements about Maryam in a single sequence: her mother's vow and prayer [c1][c2], God's acceptance [c3], Zakariyya's finding of provision [c4], and the casting of pens over her care [c5]. The text does not say that these are consecutive in time, and the ayat give no length of time between them [c3][c4][c5]. Maryam's own words in this chapter are a single sentence [c4]. The words dedicated and acceptance frame the passage [c1][c3].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Imran asked God to accept the child she carried [c1]. When her baby was born, she named her Maryam and asked God to protect her [c2]. God accepted Maryam, and Zakariyya took care of her [c3]. When he found food with her, she told him it was from God [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the chapter links a mother's prayer [c2], a guardian's care [c3] and a young woman's answer that her provision is from God [c4]. It may prompt reflection on dedication and trust [c1][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established in the ayat: the name of Imran's wife, the dates, how the casting of pens was done, what kind of provision Zakariyya found, and what the mihrab was (the ayat use the word without describing a place).
- Whether this Imran is the same as the father of anyone else in the Quran is not stated. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of this Imran with the father of Musa and Harun.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the personal name of Maryam's mother, and the place of her upbringing.

claims.statement_en: The angels said “Maryam, God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds,” and “Maryam, be devout to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow.”
The angels said “Maryam, God gives you glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near.”
He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and is of the righteous.
She said “My Lord, how can I have a child when no human has touched me?” and was told “Thus God creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter He only says to it ‘be,’ and it is.”
In another passage, she withdrew from her family to an eastern place and took a screen from them; God sent to her Our Spirit.
She said “I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are mindful of Him.” He said “I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.”

She said “How can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I have not been unchaste?” He said “So it is. Your Lord says: It is easy for Me; and so that We make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us; and it is a matter decreed.”

chapters.summary_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen and purified her [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a word from Him whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam [c2], who would speak in the cradle and in maturity [c3]. She asked how she could have a child [c4][c7], and was told it is easy for God [c7]. Another passage tells it with God's Spirit sent to her [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md:
The angels said to Maryam that God had chosen her, purified her and chosen her over the women of the worlds, and told her to be devout, to prostrate and to bow with those who bow [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a word from God whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [c2]. He would speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and be of the righteous [c3]. She asked how she could have a child when no human had touched her, and was told that God creates what He wills, and when He decrees a matter He says to it be, and it is [c4].

Another passage tells that she withdrew from her family to an eastern place and took a screen from them, and God sent to her Our Spirit [c5]. She said she sought refuge in the Most Merciful if the one who came was mindful of Him; he said he was only a messenger of her Lord, to give her a pure boy [c6]. She asked how she could have a boy when no human had touched her and she had not been unchaste, and he said it was so, that it was easy for her Lord, that He would make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passages tell the announcement with a different speaker: the angels in the first [c1][c2] and Our Spirit, who calls himself a messenger of her Lord, in the other [c5][c6]. The question of the mother is the same in both and is answered in similar terms [c4][c7]. The name and titles are given in the first passage: a word from Him, the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam [c2]. The phrase a sign for the people and a mercy from Us is given in the other [c7]. The cradle speech is announced here [c3] and told in a later chapter.
chapters.kids_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her [c1]. They gave her good news of a baby called Isa [c2]. Maryam asked how she could have a baby, and she was told that God creates whatever He wants [c4]. God said it is easy for Him [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the ayat show a young woman asking a sincere question and being answered directly [c4][c7]; they begin with being told to be devout [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established in the ayat: the place in the east, the date, and how the screen was set.
- The ayat say Our Spirit and a messenger of your Lord. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the angel (Jibril).
- The meaning of a word from Him is read in more than one way by interpreters; this draft gives the words only.
- The ayat do not describe the form in which the messenger came, and the draft does not describe it.

claims.statement_en: She conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place.
The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree; she said “If only I had died before this and had been something forgotten and lost.”
She was called from beneath her: “Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a sariyy.”

She was told “Shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink and be comforted. If you see any human, say ‘I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak today to any human.’”
In another passage, God says that He breathed into the one who guarded her chastity of His spirit, and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
A further passage says that God made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign, and gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of rest and of flowing water.
Maryam, daughter of Imran, guarded her chastity, and God breathed into it of His spirit; she believed in the words of her Lord and His books, and was of the devout.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam conceived and withdrew to a remote place [c1]. In labour she came to the trunk of a palm tree and said she wished she had died before this [c2]. She was called not to grieve, told of a sariyy beneath her [c3], and told to shake the palm tree, eat and drink, and say she had vowed a fast [c4]. Other passages call her and her son a sign [c5][c6][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Maryam conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place [c1]. The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree, and she said she wished she had died before this and been something forgotten and lost [c2]. She was called from beneath her not to grieve, because her Lord had placed beneath her a sariyy [c3]. She was told to shake the trunk of the palm tree toward her so that fresh ripe dates would fall, to eat and drink and be comforted, and if she saw any human, to say that she had vowed a fast to the Most Merciful and would not speak that day to any human [c4].

Other passages speak of the same woman [c5][c6][c7]. One says God breathed into her of His spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds [c5]. Another says that God made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign and gave them refuge on a high ground with rest and flowing water [c6]. A further passage names Maryam, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity and was breathed into of God's spirit; she believed in the words of her Lord and His books and was of the devout [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The other passages summarise the same event in one sentence each [c5][c6][c7], and all use the word sign or an equivalent for her and her son, except the last, which gives her belief and devotion [c7]. In the main account, the narrative moves from her grief [c2] to a series of instructions [c3][c4]. The ayat do not say who called her from beneath her [c3], and they do not say what the word sariyy refers to (a stream or a noble one are both discussed by interpreters) [c3]. The high ground of 23:50 is not stated to be the place of 19:22 [c1][c6].
chapters.kids_md: Maryam went to a quiet place, and when the baby was about to be born she came to a palm tree [c1][c2]. She was told not to be sad, and to shake the palm tree so that dates would fall for her to eat [c3][c4]. God says that she and her son are a sign for everyone [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the account records a woman in distress being given food and drink and told not to grieve [c3][c4]. The passages also record that she believed in the words of her Lord and was devout [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established in the ayat: the place, the date, who called to her from beneath her (19:24), what the word sariyy means here, what the remote place and the high ground refer to, and the length of time.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the places given in tradition for the birth.
- The details of her fast of silence beyond the sentence in 19:26 are not given.

claims.statement_en: She came to her people carrying him; they said “Maryam, you have done a monstrous thing. Sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil and your mother was not unchaste.”
She pointed to him; they said “How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?”
He said “I am the servant of God; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.”
