Ibrahim answered with a word of peace, said that he would ask his Lord to forgive his father, since his Lord was gracious to him, and said that he would withdraw from them and from what they call on besides God and would call on his Lord, hoping not to be unfortunate in calling on his Lord.

chapters.summary_md: Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, why he took idols as gods [c1]. He asked him to follow the knowledge that had come to him and warned him about Satan [c4][c5]. His father threatened to stone him and told him to keep away, and Ibrahim answered with peace and said he would ask his Lord to forgive his father [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md: Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, whether he took idols as gods, and said that he saw him and his people in clear error [c1]. The Quran tells the listener to mention Ibrahim in the Book, as one who was truthful, a prophet [c2]. He asked his father why he worshipped what neither hears nor sees nor helps him in any way [c3]. He told his father that knowledge had come to him that had not come to the father, and asked him to follow him so that he would guide him to a level path [c4]. He told his father not to worship Satan, who was disobedient to the Merciful, and said that he feared that a punishment from the Merciful would touch him, so that he would become a friend of Satan [c5]. His father asked whether he was turning away from his gods, said that if he did not stop he would stone him, and told him to keep away from him for a long time [c6]. Ibrahim answered with a word of peace, said that he would ask his Lord to forgive his father, since his Lord was gracious to him, and said that he would withdraw from them and from what they call on besides God and would call on his Lord, hoping not to be unfortunate in calling on his Lord [c7].
chapters.deep_md: One passage gives the father's name as Azar [c1]. The other passages say only his father [c3][c6].
chapters.kids_md: Ibrahim asked his father why he worshipped what cannot hear or see [c3]. His father told him to keep away [c6]. Ibrahim answered with peace and said he would ask his Lord to forgive his father [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Ibrahim answered a threat with a word of peace and a prayer for his father [c6][c7]. Another is that he offered what he had learned and invited his father to follow it [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether Azar is the father's personal name, a title, or the name of another relative; the ayah gives the name beside the word father, and readers have differed.
- Not established: where this happened, or when.
- Not established: what the father said or did after the threat.

claims.statement_en: Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.
When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him.
Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing.

chapters.summary_md: Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father only because of a promise [c1]. When it became clear that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him [c2].
chapters.body_md: Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him [c1]. When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him [c2]. Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah names Ibrahim's father only as his father and does not give a name [c1]. It describes Ibrahim with the Arabic words awwah and halim, usually rendered tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Ibrahim had promised to ask forgiveness for his father [c1]. When he saw that his father was an enemy of God, he turned away from him [c2]. The Quran says that Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah separates a promise that was made from what follows when the truth becomes clear [c1][c2]. Another is that it describes Ibrahim as tender-hearted and forbearing even while he disowns his father [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when it became clear to Ibrahim, or how.
- Not established: whether the father was still living at that time.
- Not established: whether the promise in this ayah is the one recorded in the passage where Ibrahim says he will ask forgiveness; connecting them is an inference.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later genealogies give Ibrahim's father a different personal name, and some works treat Azar as a title or as the name of another relative.
Hadith to add later: reports about Ibrahim and his father on the last day, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: The man who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord

claims.statement_en: The Quran asks whether the listener has seen the one to whom God had given the kingdom and who argued with another man about that man's Lord.
The other man said that his Lord is the One who gives life and causes death.
The first man answered that he gives life and causes death.
The other man said that God brings the sun from the east, so the first man should bring it from the west, and the one who disbelieved was confounded.
God does not guide the wrongdoing people.

chapters.summary_md: A man to whom God had given the kingdom argued with another man about that man's Lord [c1]. The other man said that his Lord gives life and causes death, and the first man answered that he did too [c2][c3]. The other man then said that God brings the sun from the east and told him to bring it from the west, and the one who disbelieved was confounded [c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran asks whether the listener has seen the one to whom God had given the kingdom and who argued with another man about that man's Lord [c1]. The other man said that his Lord is the One who gives life and causes death [c2]. The first man answered that he gives life and causes death [c3]. The other man said that God brings the sun from the east, so the first man should bring it from the west, and the one who disbelieved was confounded [c4]. God does not guide the wrongdoing people [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah links the argument to the kingdom that God had given the first man, and the Arabic can be read as because God had given it or after God had given it [c1]. It does not say what the first man meant by giving life and causing death [c3].
chapters.kids_md: A man who had a kingdom argued with another man about his Lord [c1]. The other man said that his Lord gives life and causes death [c2]. He said that God brings the sun from the east and told the first man to bring it from the west [c4]. The man who did not believe had no answer [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the argument ends by pointing to what only God does [c4]. Another is that the ayah closes by saying that God does not guide wrongdoing people [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name of the man who had the kingdom, his land or his time; the ayah describes him only as the one who argued.
- Not established: what the first man meant by giving life and causing death.
- Not established: whether the first man was a king in the full sense or ruled a smaller territory; the ayah says only that God had given him the kingdom.
- Not established: what the first man did or said after he was confounded.

uncertainties_en: The ayah names the other man, in a spelling that this draft's name check does not recognise, so the chapter texts refer to him without his name; the anchor fixture should be widened and the name restored.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man who had the kingdom is called Nimrod (Namrud), and later works add details of his kingdom and his end.
Hadith to add later: reports about the argument and the man's end, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: The wife of Imran and the dedication of her child

claims.statement_en: The wife of Imran said to her Lord that she had vowed to Him what was in her womb, as one dedicated to Him, and asked Him to accept it from her, for He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
When she gave birth, she said to her Lord that she had given birth to a female.
The ayah says that God knew best what she had given birth to, and that the male is not like the female.
She said that she had named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan, the accursed.

chapters.summary_md: The wife of Imran told her Lord that she had vowed to Him what was in her womb [c1]. When she gave birth to a female, she named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan [c2][c4].
chapters.body_md: The wife of Imran said to her Lord that she had vowed to Him what was in her womb, as one dedicated to Him, and asked Him to accept it from her, for He is the Hearing, the Knowing [c1]. When she gave birth, she said to her Lord that she had given birth to a female [c2]. The ayah says that God knew best what she had given birth to, and that the male is not like the female [c3]. She said that she had named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan, the accursed [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah records the words of the vow and of the naming [c1][c4]. The text does not mark whether the sentences that God knew best what she had given birth to, and that the male is not like the female, are her words or a remark added in the ayah, and readers have taken it both ways [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Imran asked God to accept what she had vowed to Him [c1]. She gave birth to a baby girl and named her Maryam [c2][c4]. She asked God to protect her and her children from Satan [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that she brought her vow and her newborn to God in prayer and placed her under His protection [c1][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: her name, her age or where she lived; the ayah calls her the wife of Imran.
- Not established: what the vow of dedication involved, beyond the word the ayah uses for dedicated.
- Not established: whether the words that God knew best, and that the male is not like the female, are hers or an added remark.
- Not established: how the Imran of this ayah is related to other people of that name, or when he lived.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: her name is given as Hannah, and later works describe the lineage and the age of Imran's family at length.
Hadith to add later: reports about Maryam's birth and her mother's prayer, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: Her mother named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan.
Her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and made her grow with a good growth.
Zakariyya became her guardian.
Whenever Zakariyya came in to her in the mihrab he found provision with her, and when he asked how she came by it, she said it was from God, who gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning.

God told the listener that the account of the casting of their pens over which of them would take Maryam in his care is part of the news of the unseen that He reveals, and that the listener was not with them when they cast their pens or when they disputed.

chapters.summary_md: Her mother named her Maryam and placed her in God's protection from Satan [c1]. Her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance, and Zakariyya became her guardian [c2][c3]. When he found provision with her and asked about it, she said it was from God [c4].
chapters.body_md: Her mother named her Maryam and placed her and her offspring in God's protection from Satan [c1]. Her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and made her grow with a good growth [c2]. Zakariyya became her guardian [c3]. Whenever Zakariyya came in to her in the mihrab he found provision with her, and when he asked how she came by it, she said it was from God, who gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning [c4]. God told the listener that the account of the casting of their pens over which of them would take Maryam in his care is part of the news of the unseen that He reveals, and that the listener was not with them when they cast their pens or when they disputed [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat tell of her guardian but not of her age or her home [c3]. The verb for making Zakariyya her guardian is read in more than one way in the recitations, and the draft says only that he became her guardian [c3]. The account of the casting of pens is given as news of the unseen [c5].
chapters.kids_md: Her mother named her Maryam and asked God to protect her [c1]. Her Lord accepted her well, and Zakariyya took care of her [c2][c3]. When he found provision with her and asked where it came from, she said it was from God [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that her answer to Zakariyya looks to God as the one who gives provision without reckoning [c4]. Another is that the passage presents her upbringing as God's acceptance and growth [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Maryam's age when she was cared for, or where she lived.
- Not established: what the mihrab was, or what the provision was; the ayah says only that Zakariyya found provision with her.
- Not established: how the casting of pens decided the matter, or who took part in it.
- Not established: whether the Lord or Zakariyya is the subject of the verb for making him her guardian; the recitations differ.

claims.statement_en: The angels said that God had chosen her and purified her and chosen her above the women of the worlds.
They told her to be devoutly obedient to her Lord, to prostrate and to bow with those who bow.
The angels said that God gave her good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam, honoured in this world and in the Hereafter and among those brought near.
The angels said that he would speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and be among the righteous.

She asked how she could have a child when no human being had touched her, and the answer was that God creates what He wills, and when He decides a matter He says to it only that it should be, and it is.

chapters.summary_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen and purified her [c1]. They gave her good news of a word from God whose name is the Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam [c3]. She asked how she could have a child when no human being had touched her, and was told that God creates what He wills [c5].
chapters.body_md: The angels said that God had chosen her and purified her and chosen her above the women of the worlds [c1]. They told her to be devoutly obedient to her Lord, to prostrate and to bow with those who bow [c2]. The angels said that God gave her good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam, honoured in this world and in the Hereafter and among those brought near [c3]. The angels said that he would speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and be among the righteous [c4]. She asked how she could have a child when no human being had touched her, and the answer was that God creates what He wills, and when He decides a matter He says to it only that it should be, and it is [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The angels' words are given in parts: a choosing and a command to worship [c1][c2], and the news of the child [c3][c4]. The ayat call the child a word from God and give his name and title [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her [c1]. They gave her good news of a child, Isa, son of Maryam [c3]. She asked how she could have a child, and was told that God creates what He wills [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins the choosing of Maryam to a call to worship [c1][c2]. Another is that her question is answered by pointing to what God wills [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how the angels spoke to her, or how many came.
- Not established: the sense in which she was chosen above the women of the worlds; the ayah says only that God chose her.
- Not established: how old the child would be at maturity; the ayah uses a word for the age of full maturity and gives no number.
- Not established: how the answer to her question was given, or when.

claims.statement_en: The Quran tells the listener to mention Maryam in the Book, when she withdrew from her family to an eastern place.
She placed a screen between herself and them, and God sent His spirit to her, which appeared to her as a human being.
She said that she sought refuge from him with the Merciful, if he was mindful of God.
He said that he was only a messenger of her Lord, sent to give her a pure boy.
She asked how she could have a boy when no human being had touched her and she had not been unchaste.
He said that it would be so, that her Lord had said it was easy for Him, that He would make the boy a sign for the people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam withdrew from her family to an eastern place and placed a screen between herself and them [c1][c2]. God sent His spirit to her, and she sought refuge with the Merciful [c2][c3]. He said that he was a messenger of her Lord, sent to give her a pure boy, and that it was easy for God [c4][c6].
chapters.body_md: The Quran tells the listener to mention Maryam in the Book, when she withdrew from her family to an eastern place [c1]. She placed a screen between herself and them, and God sent His spirit to her, which appeared to her as a human being [c2]. She said that she sought refuge from him with the Merciful, if he was mindful of God [c3]. He said that he was only a messenger of her Lord, sent to give her a pure boy [c4]. She asked how she could have a boy when no human being had touched her and she had not been unchaste [c5]. He said that it would be so, that her Lord had said it was easy for Him, that He would make the boy a sign for the people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat say that God sent His spirit and that it appeared to her as a human being, and they add no description beyond that [c2]. The speaker is called a messenger of her Lord and is not named in these ayat [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Maryam went away from her family to an eastern place [c1]. God sent His spirit to her [c2]. He told her that he was a messenger of her Lord, sent to give her a pure boy [c4]. He said that this was easy for God [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Maryam first sought refuge with the Merciful, then asked how it could be [c3][c5]. Another is that the answer given to her is that the matter is easy for God [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the eastern place was, or why she withdrew.
- Not established: what the spirit that was sent is. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the spirit is identified as Jibril.
- Not established: anything about the way the spirit appeared beyond the words of the ayah.
- Not established: Maryam's age at this time.

claims.statement_en: Maryam conceived him and withdrew with him to a far place.
The pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree, and she said that she wished she had died before this and had become something forgotten and out of mind.
A voice called to her from below her, telling her not to grieve, for her Lord had placed beneath her a sariyy, a word commonly read as a stream.
It told her to shake the trunk of the palm toward her so that fresh ripe dates would fall on her, and to eat, to drink and to be content.
It told her that if she saw any human being she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak that day to any person.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam conceived and withdrew to a far place [c1]. The pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of a palm tree, and she wished she had died before this [c2]. A voice told her not to grieve and told her to shake the palm so that dates would fall, and to eat and drink [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: Maryam conceived him and withdrew with him to a far place [c1]. The pains of childbirth brought her to the trunk of the palm tree, and she said that she wished she had died before this and had become something forgotten and out of mind [c2]. A voice called to her from below her, telling her not to grieve, for her Lord had placed beneath her a sariyy, a word commonly read as a stream [c3]. It told her to shake the trunk of the palm toward her so that fresh ripe dates would fall on her, and to eat, to drink and to be content [c4]. It told her that if she saw any human being she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak that day to any person [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not say who called to her from below, and the word sariyy is read as a stream or as a noble person [c3]. The instruction about the fast says that she would not speak that day to any person [c5].
chapters.kids_md: Maryam went to a far place [c1]. She came to the trunk of a palm tree [c2]. A voice told her not to be sad, and told her to shake the palm so that fresh dates would fall on her, and to eat and drink [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places her wish to have died beside a voice that tells her not to grieve and gives her food and drink [c2][c3][c4]. Another is that the instruction to say she had vowed a fast to the Merciful gives her words for anyone she meets [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the far place was, how far it was, or how long the labour lasted.
- Not established: who called to her from below; the ayah does not name the caller, and the recitations read the words in more than one way.
- Not established: whether sariyy means a stream or a noble person; the word can bear either sense.
- Not established: the kind of fast, or how long she kept it; the ayah says only that she would not speak to any person that day.

claims.statement_en: She came to her people carrying him, and they said that she had done something grave, and called her sister of Harun, and said that her father was not a man of evil and her mother was not unchaste.
She pointed to him, and they asked how they could speak to one who was a child in the cradle.

He said that he was a servant of God, that God had given him the Book and made him a prophet, had made him blessed wherever he might be, had enjoined on him prayer and almsgiving as long as he lived, had made him dutiful to his mother, and had not made him a wretched tyrant, and that peace was upon him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
The Quran says that this is Isa, son of Maryam, a statement of the truth about which they are in doubt.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam came to her people carrying the child, and they said that she had done something grave [c1]. She pointed to him, and they asked how they could speak to a child in the cradle [c2]. He said that he was a servant of God, who had given him the Book and made him a prophet [c3]. The Quran says that this is Isa, son of Maryam [c4].
chapters.body_md: She came to her people carrying him, and they said that she had done something grave, and called her sister of Harun, and said that her father was not a man of evil and her mother was not unchaste [c1]. She pointed to him, and they asked how they could speak to one who was a child in the cradle [c2]. He said that he was a servant of God, that God had given him the Book and made him a prophet, had made him blessed wherever he might be, had enjoined on him prayer and almsgiving as long as he lived, had made him dutiful to his mother, and had not made him a wretched tyrant, and that peace was upon him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c3]. The Quran says that this is Isa, son of Maryam, a statement of the truth about which they are in doubt [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The people call her sister of Harun, and the ayat do not say which Harun is meant [c1]. The words from the cradle are the child's own, recorded in the first person, and the ayah names him afterwards [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: Maryam came to her people carrying the child, and they were upset with her [c1]. She pointed to him [c2]. He said that he was a servant of God, who had given him the Book and made him a prophet [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Maryam answers her people by pointing to the child and that the child speaks of himself as a servant of God [c2][c3]. Another is that the passage closes by calling the account a statement of the truth about which they are in doubt [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which Harun the people meant by calling her sister of Harun; the ayah does not say whether this is the Harun named elsewhere or another.
- Not established: the age of the child when he spoke, beyond the words in the cradle.
- Not established: who else was present, or what the people did next.
- Not established: how the people knew her father and mother.

claims.statement_en: God says of the woman who guarded her chastity that He breathed into her of His spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
God made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign, and gave them refuge on high ground with a place of rest and flowing water.

The ayah mentions Maryam, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, and says that God breathed into it of His spirit and that she confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout.
The Quran charges some people with disbelief and with speaking a great slander against Maryam.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He made the woman who guarded her chastity and her son a sign for the worlds [c1]. He gave the son of Maryam and his mother refuge on high ground [c2]. Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout [c3].
chapters.body_md: God says of the woman who guarded her chastity that He breathed into her of His spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds [c1]. God made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign, and gave them refuge on high ground with a place of rest and flowing water [c2]. The ayah mentions Maryam, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, and says that God breathed into it of His spirit and that she confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout [c3]. The Quran charges some people with disbelief and with speaking a great slander against Maryam [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat that name Maryam elsewhere call her and her son a sign [c1][c2]. In the ayah about Maryam, daughter of Imran, the pronoun in the words God breathed into it is not spelled out, and the ayah leaves it without comment [c3]. A separate ayah charges some people with a great slander against her [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God made Maryam and her son a sign for the worlds [c1]. He gave them refuge on high ground with flowing water [c2]. Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and was among the devout [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passages present Maryam as faithful and devout [c3]. Another is that they place the slander spoken against her beside God's words about her [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the high ground was; the ayah gives no name.
- Not established: what the pronoun in the words God breathed into it refers to; the ayah leaves it open.
- Not established: who the people were who spoke the slander, or what they said.
- Not established: which books are meant by her Lord's books.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the spirit that was sent to her is identified as Jibril, and later works give details of her age, her place and the birth.
The Quran uses the words sister of Harun for her; which Harun is meant is not settled by the text.
Hadith to add later: reports about Maryam and her place among women, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: A speaker who had stayed away only a short while said to the one he addressed that he had learned what the other had not, and that he had come from Saba with certain news.
He said that he had found a woman who rules over them, who had been given of everything and had a great throne.
He said that he had found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, that Satan had made their deeds seem fair to them and turned them from the way, so that they were not guided.

The speaker said that they did not prostrate to God, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what they hide and what they declare, God, besides whom there is no god, Lord of the great throne.

chapters.summary_md: A speaker came with certain news from Saba [c1]. He said that he had found a woman who rules over them and who had a great throne [c2], and that she and her people prostrated to the sun instead of God [c3].
chapters.body_md: A speaker who had stayed away only a short while said to the one he addressed that he had learned what the other had not, and that he had come from Saba with certain news [c1]. He said that he had found a woman who rules over them, who had been given of everything and had a great throne [c2]. He said that he had found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, that Satan had made their deeds seem fair to them and turned them from the way, so that they were not guided [c3]. The speaker said that they did not prostrate to God, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth and knows what they hide and what they declare, God, besides whom there is no god, Lord of the great throne [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not name the speaker or the one he addresses [c1]. The end of the report can be read as a statement that they do not prostrate to God or as a call to prostrate to Him, since the Arabic allows both [c4].
chapters.kids_md: A speaker brought news from Saba [c1]. He had found a woman who ruled over the people there [c2]. They prostrated to the sun and not to God [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the report notes the woman's wealth and great throne and then turns to what she and her people worshipped [c2][c3]. Another is that the report ends by naming God as the Lord of the great throne [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established in these ayat: who the speaker is or whom he addresses; the identification comes from the ayat before this item.
- Not established: where Saba lay, or when this took place.
- Not established: her name, how she came to rule, or how long she ruled.
- Not established: what given of everything means in detail.

claims.statement_en: The one addressed said that they would see whether the speaker had told the truth or was a liar, and told him to take his letter, throw it to them, turn away from them and see what they would answer.

She told the chiefs that a noble letter had been thrown to her, that it was from Sulayman, that it began in the name of God, and that it said not to exalt themselves against him but to come to him in submission.

She asked the chiefs to advise her on her matter, saying that she decided no matter until they were present, and they answered that they had strength and great might, but the command was hers, so she should consider what to command.

She said that kings, when they enter a town, ruin it and make its mighty people low, and that this is what they do, and that she was sending them a gift and would see with what the envoys would return.

When the envoy came to Sulayman, he said that they should not supply him with wealth, since what God had given him was better than what He had given them, and that they rejoiced in their gift, and he told the envoy to go back to them and said that he would come to them with forces they could not face and drive them out from there humbled and in disgrace.

chapters.summary_md: A letter from Sulayman was thrown to her, and she told the chiefs what it said and asked their advice [c2][c3]. She said that she would send a gift and see what the envoys returned with [c4]. Sulayman answered that what God had given him was better than their gift [c5].
chapters.body_md: The one addressed said that they would see whether the speaker had told the truth or was a liar, and told him to take his letter, throw it to them, turn away from them and see what they would answer [c1]. She told the chiefs that a noble letter had been thrown to her, that it was from Sulayman, that it began in the name of God, and that it said not to exalt themselves against him but to come to him in submission [c2]. She asked the chiefs to advise her on her matter, saying that she decided no matter until they were present, and they answered that they had strength and great might, but the command was hers, so she should consider what to command [c3]. She said that kings, when they enter a town, ruin it and make its mighty people low, and that this is what they do, and that she was sending them a gift and would see with what the envoys would return [c4]. When the envoy came to Sulayman, he said that they should not supply him with wealth, since what God had given him was better than what He had given them, and that they rejoiced in their gift, and he told the envoy to go back to them and said that he would come to them with forces they could not face and drive them out from there humbled and in disgrace [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat show her asking for advice before deciding, and the chiefs leaving the command to her [c3]. She gives her words about kings entering a town beside her decision to send a gift [c4]. The Arabic verb for the coming to Sulayman is singular while the envoys in the previous ayah are plural, and the ayat do not explain this [c5].
chapters.kids_md: She received a letter from Sulayman [c2]. She asked the chiefs for their advice [c3]. She decided to send a gift [c4]. Sulayman said that what God had given him was better [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that she asked for advice before she acted [c3]. Another is that Sulayman put what God had given him above a gift of wealth [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how the letter was delivered, or what else it said beyond the words recorded.
- Not established: what the gift was, or how many envoys carried it.
- Not established: how many forces Sulayman meant, or whether they were ever sent.
- Not established: who the chiefs were, or how many.

claims.statement_en: Sulayman asked the chiefs which of them would bring him her throne before they came to him in submission.
A strong one from the jinn said that he would bring it before Sulayman rose from his place, and one who had knowledge of the Book said that he would bring it before his glance returned to him.

When he saw it set before him, he said that it was of the favour of his Lord, to test whether he would be thankful or ungrateful, and that whoever is thankful is thankful only for himself, while whoever is ungrateful, his Lord is self-sufficient and generous.

He said to disguise her throne for her, to see whether she would be guided or be among those who are not guided, and when she came she was asked whether her throne was like this, and she said that it seemed to be it.
A statement follows that they had been given knowledge before her and had been in submission, and the ayah does not mark who says it.
The ayah says that what she used to worship besides God had barred her, for she was of a disbelieving people.

She was told to enter the palace, and when she saw it she took it for a pool of water, and he said that it was a palace smoothed with glass, and she said, my Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds.

chapters.summary_md: Sulayman asked which of the chiefs would bring her throne before they came to him in submission [c1], and one who had knowledge of the Book offered to bring it before his glance returned [c2]. She was asked whether her throne was like this and said that it seemed to be it [c4]. In the end she said that she had wronged herself and submitted with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds [c7].
chapters.body_md: Sulayman asked the chiefs which of them would bring him her throne before they came to him in submission [c1]. A strong one from the jinn said that he would bring it before Sulayman rose from his place, and one who had knowledge of the Book said that he would bring it before his glance returned to him [c2]. When he saw it set before him, he said that it was of the favour of his Lord, to test whether he would be thankful or ungrateful, and that whoever is thankful is thankful only for himself, while whoever is ungrateful, his Lord is self-sufficient and generous [c3]. He said to disguise her throne for her, to see whether she would be guided or be among those who are not guided, and when she came she was asked whether her throne was like this, and she said that it seemed to be it [c4]. A statement follows that they had been given knowledge before her and had been in submission, and the ayah does not mark who says it [c5]. The ayah says that what she used to worship besides God had barred her, for she was of a disbelieving people [c6]. She was told to enter the palace, and when she saw it she took it for a pool of water, and he said that it was a palace smoothed with glass, and she said, my Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to God, Lord of the worlds [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The first speaker in the passage is not named in these ayat, and the draft names Sulayman because the passage continues from his earlier words [c1]. The ayah leaves open who says that they had been given knowledge before her [c5]. The one with knowledge of the Book is not named [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman asked who could bring her throne [c1]. One who had knowledge of the Book said that he could bring it before his glance came back [c2]. When she came, she said that her throne seemed to be it [c4]. At the end she said that she submitted to God, Lord of the worlds [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Sulayman, on seeing the throne before him, spoke of it as a favour from his Lord and a test of thanks [c3]. Another is that her last words in the passage are an admission of having wronged herself and a statement of submission to God [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the one with knowledge of the Book was, or what knowledge he had. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is called Asaf.
- Not established: how the throne was brought, or how far it was.
- Not established: who speaks the statement about knowledge and submission in the ayah, and who says that the palace is smoothed with glass; the pronouns are not marked.
- Not established: anything about her life after the last words of the passage.
- The ayah mentions an action she took on seeing the palace; this draft leaves that detail out.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: she is called Bilqis (or Balqis), and later works give her lineage, her city and the later course of her life.
Hadith to add later: reports about the woman who ruled Saba, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, when she feared for him, to cast him into the water.
She was told not to fear and not to grieve, for God would return him to her and make him one of the messengers.

God says to Musa that He inspired his mother with what was inspired: to put him in the chest and cast it into the water, so that the water would throw it on the bank, where one who was an enemy to God and to him would take him.

chapters.summary_md: God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, when she feared for him, to cast him into the water [c1]. She was told not to fear or grieve, because God would return him to her [c2].
chapters.body_md: God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, when she feared for him, to cast him into the water [c1]. She was told not to fear and not to grieve, for God would return him to her and make him one of the messengers [c2]. God says to Musa that He inspired his mother with what was inspired: to put him in the chest and cast it into the water, so that the water would throw it on the bank, where one who was an enemy to God and to him would take him [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The instruction appears in one passage as an inspiration to nurse and then to cast him out [c1], and in another as putting him in the chest and casting it into the water [c3]. The Arabic for the water, al-yamm, can mean a river or a sea, and the ayat do not say which [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God told the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, if she was afraid, to put him in the water [c1]. God told her not to be afraid or sad, because He would bring him back to her [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the instruction and the promise of his return are given together [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the mother's name, her age or where she lived.
- Not established: how the inspiration came to her; the ayat do not say whether it was a dream, a voice or another means.
- Not established: how old the child was when she cast him out, or how long she nursed him.
- Not established: which water was meant, or what the chest was made of.

claims.statement_en: The family of Fir'awn picked him up, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, for Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error.
The heart of the mother of Musa became empty, and she would almost have revealed him had God not strengthened her heart, so that she would be among the believers.
She told his sister to follow him, and she watched him from a distance, while they did not perceive.
God had forbidden him wet-nurses beforehand, and his sister asked whether she might direct them to a household that would take care of him for them and wished him well.
God returned him to his mother so that she would be comforted and not grieve, and so that she would know that God's promise is true, though most of them do not know.

chapters.summary_md: The family of Fir'awn picked up the child [c1]. The heart of the mother of Musa became empty, and God strengthened it so that she would be among the believers [c2]. His sister watched, and spoke of a household that would take care of him, and God returned him to his mother [c3][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md: The family of Fir'awn picked him up, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, for Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error [c1]. The heart of the mother of Musa became empty, and she would almost have revealed him had God not strengthened her heart, so that she would be among the believers [c2]. She told his sister to follow him, and she watched him from a distance, while they did not perceive [c3]. God had forbidden him wet-nurses beforehand, and his sister asked whether she might direct them to a household that would take care of him for them and wished him well [c4]. God returned him to his mother so that she would be comforted and not grieve, and so that she would know that God's promise is true, though most of them do not know [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat speak of the mother, the sister and the child without naming them [c3][c5]. The words describing her heart as empty are read in more than one way, as empty of patience or as empty of everything but him [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The mother of Musa told his sister to follow him [c3]. His sister watched from a distance [c3]. God returned him to his mother, so that she would be comforted and not grieve [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage describes a mother whose heart God strengthened and to whom God returned her child [c2][c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how the family of Fir'awn picked him up, or where.
- Not established: how long the child was away from his mother.
- Not established: which household took care of him, beyond the words of his sister.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give names to the mother and the sister.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give a name to the mother of Musa and to his sister, and describe where the chest came to rest.
Hadith to add later: reports about the mother of Musa and the chest, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: The women of Madyan and their father

claims.statement_en: A man who came to the water of Madyan found there a crowd of people watering, and found apart from them a pair of women holding back, and when he asked what their concern was, they said that they could not water until the shepherds withdrew, since their father was a very old man.
He watered for them, then went back to the shade and said, my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.

One of them came to him with modesty and said that her father was calling him to repay him for watering for them, and when he came to her father and told him his account, the father said, do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.
One of them said to her father that he should hire him, since the best one to hire is the strong and the trustworthy.

The father said that he wished to marry one of these daughters of his to him on condition that he work for him for eight years, and if he completed ten it would be of his own accord, adding that he did not wish to burden him and that he would find him, if God willed, among the righteous.
The man answered that this was agreed between them, that whichever term he completed there would be no wrong against him, and that God was a guardian over what they said.

chapters.summary_md: A man came to the water of Madyan and watered for a pair of women who were holding back [c1][c2]. Their father called him, and one of the women said that he should be hired as the strong and trustworthy one [c3][c4]. The father proposed that he work for him for eight years, or ten if he chose, and offered one of his daughters in marriage [c5].
chapters.body_md: A man who came to the water of Madyan found there a crowd of people watering, and found apart from them a pair of women holding back, and when he asked what their concern was, they said that they could not water until the shepherds withdrew, since their father was a very old man [c1]. He watered for them, then went back to the shade and said, my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me [c2]. One of them came to him with modesty and said that her father was calling him to repay him for watering for them, and when he came to her father and told him his account, the father said, do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people [c3]. One of them said to her father that he should hire him, since the best one to hire is the strong and the trustworthy [c4]. The father said that he wished to marry one of these daughters of his to him on condition that he work for him for eight years, and if he completed ten it would be of his own accord, adding that he did not wish to burden him and that he would find him, if God willed, among the righteous [c5]. The man answered that this was agreed between them, that whichever term he completed there would be no wrong against him, and that God was a guardian over what they said [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat name neither the women, their father nor the man [c1]. They record the terms the father offered, eight years with ten as a favour from the man [c5].
chapters.kids_md: A man came to the water of Madyan [c1]. He saw a pair of women holding back and watered for them [c1][c2]. Their father asked to see him, and one of the women said that he was strong and trustworthy [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that after helping the women the man turned to God and said that he needed whatever good God might send [c2]. Another is that one of the women described the best person to hire as strong and trustworthy [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the names of the women, their father or the man, or where Madyan lay.
- Not established: the Arabic word in the ayah that is rendered years can also mean pilgrimages, and years is the usual reading.
- Not established: which of the women the father meant, or whether the marriage took place within these ayat; the ayah records the offer and the man's reply.
- Not established: how long the man stayed, or how long the work lasted.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the father is identified with a prophet of Madyan, and the women and their father are given names in later works.
The man in these ayat is not named in them; linking him to a person of the same surah is an inference from the context.
Hadith to add later: reports about the women of Madyan and their father, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: The man who came running to warn Musa

claims.statement_en: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said to Musa that the chiefs were plotting against him to kill him, so he should leave, since he was one of those who advised him well.
Musa left the city fearful and watchful, and said, my Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.

chapters.summary_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and warned Musa that the chiefs were plotting to kill him [c1]. Musa left the city fearful and asked his Lord to save him from the wrongdoing people [c2].
chapters.body_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said to Musa that the chiefs were plotting against him to kill him, so he should leave, since he was one of those who advised him well [c1]. Musa left the city fearful and watchful, and said, my Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the man's words as advice from one who wishes him well [c1]. It does not say how he knew of the plot [c1].
chapters.kids_md: A man ran from the far side of the city to warn Musa [c1]. Musa left the city and asked his Lord to save him [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that a warning was given and heeded [c1][c2]. Another is that Musa, after leaving, turned to his Lord [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the man's name, his faith or his relation to Musa.
- Not established: the name of the city, or who the chiefs were.
- Not established: how the man knew of the plot, or what became of him.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give the man a name and say who he was; the text itself only calls him a man from the farthest part of the city.
Hadith to add later: reports about the man who warned Musa, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: Musa and the servant of God

chapters.title_en: The meeting place of the seas

claims.statement_en: Musa told his young companion that he would not stop until he reached the meeting place of the seas, or went on for a long time.
When they reached the place where the seas met, they forgot their fish, and it made its way into the sea like a tunnel.
When they had passed on, Musa told his companion to bring their meal, saying that they had met weariness on this journey.

The companion said that when they had taken shelter at the rock, he had forgotten the fish, that only Satan had made him forget to mention it, and that the fish had taken its way into the sea in a strange way.
Musa said that this was what they had been seeking, and they went back, following their own tracks.

chapters.summary_md: Musa told his young companion that he would not stop until he reached the meeting place of the seas [c1]. They forgot their fish there, and it made its way into the sea [c2]. When Musa asked for their meal, the companion said that only Satan had made him forget to mention the fish [c3][c4]. Musa said that this was what they had been seeking, and they went back [c5].
chapters.body_md: Musa told his young companion that he would not stop until he reached the meeting place of the seas, or went on for a long time [c1]. When they reached the place where the seas met, they forgot their fish, and it made its way into the sea like a tunnel [c2]. When they had passed on, Musa told his companion to bring their meal, saying that they had met weariness on this journey [c3]. The companion said that when they had taken shelter at the rock, he had forgotten the fish, that only Satan had made him forget to mention it, and that the fish had taken its way into the sea in a strange way [c4]. Musa said that this was what they had been seeking, and they went back, following their own tracks [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The Arabic form for the seas in the meeting place is a dual form, and the ayat do not say which seas are meant or where [c1]. The ayah gives the fish's way as like a tunnel and leaves the manner open [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Musa told his young companion that he would not stop until he reached the meeting place of the seas [c1]. They forgot their fish, and it made its way into the sea [c2]. They went back, following their own tracks [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage links the forgetting to Satan's doing, in the companion's words [c4]. Another is that Musa takes what happened to the fish to be what they had been seeking [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the place of the meeting of the seas, or which seas are meant.
- Not established: the kind of fish, or why they carried it; the ayah calls it their fish.
- Not established: the name of the young companion, or his relation to Musa. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is called Yusha.
- Not established: how long Musa meant by going on for a long time; the Arabic word is huqub, and the ayah gives no length.

chapters.title_en: The servant and what he did

claims.statement_en: They found a servant from among God's servants, to whom God had given mercy from Himself and whom He had taught knowledge from Himself.
Musa asked him whether he might follow him, so that he would teach him some of what he had been taught of right guidance.
The servant said that Musa would not be able to bear with him patiently, and asked how he could be patient about what he had no full knowledge of.
Musa said that he would find him patient, if God willed, and would not disobey him in any matter.
The servant said that if he followed him he should not ask him about anything until he himself spoke to him of it.
They set out, and when they boarded the ship, he made a hole in it, and Musa asked whether he had done it to drown its people and said that he had done a grave thing.

The servant asked whether he had not said that Musa could not bear with him patiently, and Musa asked him not to hold him to account for what he had forgotten and not to burden him with hardship in his affair.
They went on until they met a boy, and the servant killed him, and Musa asked whether he had killed an innocent soul who had killed no one and said that he had done a terrible thing.
The servant repeated his earlier words, and Musa said that if he asked him about anything after this the servant need not keep him as a companion, since he had reached an excuse from him.

They went on until they came to the people of a town and asked them for food, but they refused to host them, and there they found a wall about to fall, and the servant set it upright, and Musa said that if he had wished he could have taken payment for it.
The servant said that this was the parting between them, and that he would inform Musa of the meaning of what he had been unable to bear patiently.
He said that the ship belonged to poor people who worked at sea, that he wished to damage it, since behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.
He said that the boy's parents were believers and that, speaking in the plural, he feared the boy would burden them with transgression and disbelief.
Again in the plural, he said that they wished that the parents' Lord would give them in exchange one better than the boy in purity and nearer in mercy.

He said that the wall belonged to orphan boys in the city, that beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and that their father had been righteous, so your Lord wished them to reach their maturity and bring out their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord.
He said that he had not done it of his own command, and that this was the meaning of what Musa had been unable to bear patiently.

chapters.summary_md: Musa found a servant of God to whom God had given mercy and knowledge, and asked to follow him [c1][c2]. The servant said that Musa would not be able to be patient, and told him not to ask about anything until he himself spoke of it [c3][c5]. On the way the servant made a hole in a ship, killed a boy and set upright a wall [c6][c8][c10]. At the parting he explained each of them [c11][c12][c13][c15].
chapters.body_md: They found a servant from among God's servants, to whom God had given mercy from Himself and whom He had taught knowledge from Himself [c1]. Musa asked him whether he might follow him, so that he would teach him some of what he had been taught of right guidance [c2]. The servant said that Musa would not be able to bear with him patiently, and asked how he could be patient about what he had no full knowledge of [c3]. Musa said that he would find him patient, if God willed, and would not disobey him in any matter [c4]. The servant said that if he followed him he should not ask him about anything until he himself spoke to him of it [c5]. They set out, and when they boarded the ship, he made a hole in it, and Musa asked whether he had done it to drown its people and said that he had done a grave thing [c6]. The servant asked whether he had not said that Musa could not bear with him patiently, and Musa asked him not to hold him to account for what he had forgotten and not to burden him with hardship in his affair [c7]. They went on until they met a boy, and the servant killed him, and Musa asked whether he had killed an innocent soul who had killed no one and said that he had done a terrible thing [c8]. The servant repeated his earlier words, and Musa said that if he asked him about anything after this the servant need not keep him as a companion, since he had reached an excuse from him [c9]. They went on until they came to the people of a town and asked them for food, but they refused to host them, and there they found a wall about to fall, and the servant set it upright, and Musa said that if he had wished he could have taken payment for it [c10]. The servant said that this was the parting between them, and that he would inform Musa of the meaning of what he had been unable to bear patiently [c11]. He said that the ship belonged to poor people who worked at sea, that he wished to damage it, since behind them was a king who seized every ship by force [c12]. He said that the boy's parents were believers and that, speaking in the plural, he feared the boy would burden them with transgression and disbelief [c13]. Again in the plural, he said that they wished that the parents' Lord would give them in exchange one better than the boy in purity and nearer in mercy [c14]. He said that the wall belonged to orphan boys in the city, that beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and that their father had been righteous, so your Lord wished them to reach their maturity and bring out their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord [c15]. He said that he had not done it of his own command, and that this was the meaning of what Musa had been unable to bear patiently [c16].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah calls him only a servant from among God's servants, and does not call him a prophet or a messenger [c1]. The knowledge he was taught is called knowledge from God's own presence, in the Arabic min ladunna [c1]. Each act is explained only afterwards, and the servant says that he did not do it of his own command [c16]. The servant speaks in the plural in the words we feared and we wished, and the ayat do not say who is meant [c13][c14]. The Arabic for behind them can mean ahead of them or behind them, and the ayah does not say which [c12].
chapters.kids_md: Musa found a servant of God who had been taught knowledge by God [c1]. Musa asked to follow him [c2]. The servant told him not to ask about anything until he spoke of it himself [c5]. Later the servant explained that the ship belonged to poor people who worked at sea [c12]. He explained that the wall belonged to orphan boys and that a treasure lay beneath it [c15].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins a request to learn with a promise of patience, made with the words if God willed [c2][c4]. Another is that each act is explained only afterwards, and that the servant says he did not act of his own command [c12][c16].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the servant's name, where he was found, or how Musa knew to seek him.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the servant is called al-Khidr.
- Not established: whether he was a prophet; the ayah says only that God gave him mercy and taught him knowledge.
- Not established: what the knowledge was, beyond the actions that follow.
- Not established: the kind of ship, where it sailed, how many were aboard, or the king's name or land.
- Not established: whether the hole sank the ship or only damaged it; the servant says only that he wished to damage it.
- Not established: the boy's name or age, how the servant killed him, how he knew what he says he feared, who is meant by the plural we, or what became of the parents.
- Not established: the name of the town or its people, what the treasure was, or how the servant knew what lay beneath the wall.
- Not established: what happened between Musa and the servant after the parting.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the servant is called al-Khidr and the young companion Yusha, and later works name the boy, the king and the town.
Whether the servant was a prophet is not stated; the Quran calls him only a servant from among God's servants.
Hadith to add later: reports about Musa and the servant, including accounts of the meeting place, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: God told Musa that his people had been tried after he left, and that the Samiri had led them astray.

Musa returned to his people angry and grieved, and asked whether their Lord had not promised them a good promise, whether the time had seemed long to them, or whether they had wished that anger from their Lord should fall on them, so that they broke their promise to him.
They answered that they had not broken their promise to him of their own accord, but had been made to carry loads of the people's ornaments, which they threw, and that the Samiri threw likewise.
He brought out for them a calf, a body that made a lowing sound, and they said that this was their god and the god of Musa, and that he had forgotten.
God asks whether they did not see that it returned no word to them and had no power to harm or benefit them.
Harun had told them before this that they were only being tried by it, that their Lord is the Merciful, and that they should follow him and obey his command.
They said that they would not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returned to them.
Musa asked Harun what had prevented him, when he saw them go astray, from following him, and asked whether he had disobeyed his command.

Harun, addressing him as son of his mother, asked him not to seize him, and said that he had feared that Musa would say that he had caused division among the Children of Israel and had not waited for his word.
Musa asked the Samiri what his concern was.
The Samiri said that he had seen what they had not seen, so he took a handful from the trace of the messenger and threw it, and that this was how his soul had suggested it to him.

Musa told him to go, for it would be his lot in this life to say that there is to be no touching, and that he had an appointment that he would not miss, and he told him to look at his god, to which he had stayed devoted, saying that he would burn it and scatter it in the sea.

chapters.summary_md: God told Musa that his people had been tried after he left, and that the Samiri had led them astray [c1]. The Samiri brought out a calf, and the people said that it was their god [c4]. Harun had told them that they were only being tried by it, but they said that they would stay devoted to it until Musa returned [c6][c7]. Musa asked Harun and then the Samiri what lay behind it, and told the Samiri to go [c8][c10][c12].
chapters.body_md: God told Musa that his people had been tried after he left, and that the Samiri had led them astray [c1]. Musa returned to his people angry and grieved, and asked whether their Lord had not promised them a good promise, whether the time had seemed long to them, or whether they had wished that anger from their Lord should fall on them, so that they broke their promise to him [c2]. They answered that they had not broken their promise to him of their own accord, but had been made to carry loads of the people's ornaments, which they threw, and that the Samiri threw likewise [c3]. He brought out for them a calf, a body that made a lowing sound, and they said that this was their god and the god of Musa, and that he had forgotten [c4]. God asks whether they did not see that it returned no word to them and had no power to harm or benefit them [c5]. Harun had told them before this that they were only being tried by it, that their Lord is the Merciful, and that they should follow him and obey his command [c6]. They said that they would not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returned to them [c7]. Musa asked Harun what had prevented him, when he saw them go astray, from following him, and asked whether he had disobeyed his command [c8]. Harun, addressing him as son of his mother, asked him not to seize him, and said that he had feared that Musa would say that he had caused division among the Children of Israel and had not waited for his word [c9]. Musa asked the Samiri what his concern was [c10]. The Samiri said that he had seen what they had not seen, so he took a handful from the trace of the messenger and threw it, and that this was how his soul had suggested it to him [c11]. Musa told him to go, for it would be his lot in this life to say that there is to be no touching, and that he had an appointment that he would not miss, and he told him to look at his god, to which he had stayed devoted, saying that he would burn it and scatter it in the sea [c12].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the Samiri's act as bringing out a calf, a body that made a lowing sound, and does not say how it was made [c4]. The words and he had forgotten can be read as said by the people of Musa or of the Samiri, and the Arabic allows both [c4]. The ayah gives Harun's address as son of my mother and records a physical action in his words, which this draft leaves out [c9]. The messenger in the Samiri's words is not named in the ayah [c11]. The ayah gives the sentence there is to be no touching without explaining it [c12].
chapters.kids_md: The Samiri led the people astray [c1]. He brought out a calf, and the people said that it was their god [c4]. Harun told them that they were only being tried by it [c6]. They said that they would stay devoted to it until Musa returned [c7]. Musa asked Harun why he had not followed him, and Harun said that he feared Musa would say he had caused division among the Children of Israel [c8][c9]. Musa told the Samiri to go, and said that he would burn the god to which he had stayed devoted [c12].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places the people's devotion to the calf beside God's question about whether they saw that it returned no word [c4][c5]. Another is that Harun's answer is about fear of causing division and the Samiri's is about what his soul suggested [c9][c11].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the Samiri's personal name, his tribe or his origin; the ayah uses only the descriptive form the Samiri.
- Not established: where the ornaments came from, or how the calf was made or how it came to make a sound.
- Not established: how long Musa was away.
- Not established: who is the subject of the words and he had forgotten.
- Not established: who the messenger is in the Samiri's words, what the handful was, or what the trace was. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the messenger is identified as Jibril, and the handful as dust from the track of his horse.
- Not established: what the words no touching mean, or how they applied to him.
- Not established: what the appointment was, what became of the Samiri, or whether the calf was burned beyond Musa's words that he would burn it.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give the Samiri a personal name and an origin, and describe the calf and the handful at length.
Hadith to add later: reports about the Samiri and the calf, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: Fir'awn exalted himself in the land and divided its people into groups, weakening one group by killing their sons and sparing their women, and he was one of the corrupters.
God wished to favour those who were weakened in the land, make them leaders and heirs, establish them in the land, and show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces through them what they feared.

chapters.summary_md: Fir'awn exalted himself in the land and divided its people into groups [c1]. He weakened one group by killing their sons and sparing their women [c1]. God wished to favour those who were weakened, and to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces what they feared [c2].
chapters.body_md: Fir'awn exalted himself in the land and divided its people into groups, weakening one group by killing their sons and sparing their women, and he was one of the corrupters [c1]. God wished to favour those who were weakened in the land, make them leaders and heirs, establish them in the land, and show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces through them what they feared [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that Fir'awn divided the people of the land into groups and weakened one of them [c1]. These ayat do not name the weakened group [c1][c2].
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn weakened one group of people in the land [c1]. God wished to favour those who were weakened [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets Fir'awn's exalting of himself beside God's wish to favour the weakened [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Fir'awn's personal name, his dynasty or his time; the Quran uses the word Fir'awn.
- Not established: which group was weakened, how many were killed, or for how long.
- Not established: what they feared, beyond the words of the ayah.

claims.statement_en: God called to Musa in the sacred valley of Tuwa and told him to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed.
God told Musa to ask Fir'awn whether he wished to be purified, and that he would guide him to his Lord so that he would fear.
Musa showed him the greatest sign, but Fir'awn denied it and disobeyed.
Then he turned his back, hurrying, gathered people and called out, saying that he was their lord, the highest.

chapters.summary_md: God called to Musa and told him to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed [c1]. Musa was to ask Fir'awn whether he wished to be purified and to offer to guide him to his Lord [c2]. Musa showed him the greatest sign, but Fir'awn denied and disobeyed, gathered people and said that he was their lord, the highest [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: God called to Musa in the sacred valley of Tuwa and told him to go to Fir'awn, who had transgressed [c1]. God told Musa to ask Fir'awn whether he wished to be purified, and that he would guide him to his Lord so that he would fear [c2]. Musa showed him the greatest sign, but Fir'awn denied it and disobeyed [c3]. Then he turned his back, hurrying, gathered people and called out, saying that he was their lord, the highest [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not say what the greatest sign was [c3]. The words that he was their lord, the highest, are recorded as Fir'awn's own, and the ayat do not explain how he meant them [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God told Musa to go to Fir'awn [c1]. Musa was to ask Fir'awn whether he wished to be purified [c2]. Fir'awn denied and disobeyed, and said that he was their lord, the highest [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Musa is sent first with a question and an offer of guidance [c2]. Another is that Fir'awn's answer is denial and a claim to be the highest lord [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when and where Musa went to Fir'awn, beyond the sacred valley where he was called.
- Not established: what the greatest sign was.
- Not established: whom Fir'awn gathered, or where.

claims.statement_en: God sent Musa with His signs and clear authority to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, and they said that he was a lying sorcerer.
When he brought them the truth from God, they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women, and the plotting of the disbelievers was only in error.
Fir'awn said that they should leave him to kill Musa and let him call on his Lord, for he feared that Musa would change their religion or cause corruption to appear in the land.
Musa said that he took refuge in his Lord and their Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account.
God sent Musa with His signs to Fir'awn and his chiefs, and he said that he was a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, and when he brought them the signs, they laughed at them.
Each sign that God showed them was greater than its sister, and He seized them with punishment so that they might return.

They addressed him as sorcerer and asked him to call on his Lord for them by what He had covenanted with him, saying that they would be guided, but when God removed the punishment from them, they broke their word.

chapters.summary_md: Musa came to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun with God's signs, and they called him a lying sorcerer [c1]. They said to kill the sons of those who believed with him [c2], and Fir'awn said that he feared Musa would change their religion [c3]. They laughed at the signs [c5], and when the punishment was removed from them they broke their word [c7].
chapters.body_md: God sent Musa with His signs and clear authority to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, and they said that he was a lying sorcerer [c1]. When he brought them the truth from God, they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women, and the plotting of the disbelievers was only in error [c2]. Fir'awn said that they should leave him to kill Musa and let him call on his Lord, for he feared that Musa would change their religion or cause corruption to appear in the land [c3]. Musa said that he took refuge in his Lord and their Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account [c4]. God sent Musa with His signs to Fir'awn and his chiefs, and he said that he was a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, and when he brought them the signs, they laughed at them [c5]. Each sign that God showed them was greater than its sister, and He seized them with punishment so that they might return [c6]. They addressed him as sorcerer and asked him to call on his Lord for them by what He had covenanted with him, saying that they would be guided, but when God removed the punishment from them, they broke their word [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat place Qarun and Haman with Fir'awn as those to whom Musa was sent [c1]. They record that each sign was greater than its sister [c6]. The ayat do not say what the signs or the punishments were [c6].
chapters.kids_md: Musa came with signs from God, and Fir'awn and his chiefs laughed at them [c5]. They called Musa a sorcerer and said that they would be guided if he called on his Lord [c1][c7]. But when God removed the punishment, they broke their word [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage shows a promise made under punishment and broken when the punishment was removed [c7]. Another is that Musa answered Fir'awn's threat by taking refuge in his Lord [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the signs were, or in what order they came.
- Not established: what the punishments were that were removed, or how many times this happened.
- Not established: what the covenant was that they mention.

claims.statement_en: Fir'awn called out among his people, asking whether the kingdom of Egypt was not his and these rivers flowing beneath him, and asking whether they did not see.
He asked why gold ornaments had not been cast upon Musa and why angels had not come with him as companions.
He swayed his people and they obeyed him, for they were a defiantly disobedient people.

Fir'awn said to the chiefs that he knew of no god for them other than himself, told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.
He and his forces were arrogant in the land without right and thought that they would not be returned to God.
Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw and guided them only to the way of right conduct.

Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar, and his evil deed was made to seem fair to him and he was barred from the way, and his plotting was only in ruin.

chapters.summary_md: Fir'awn asked his people whether the kingdom of Egypt and its rivers were not his [c1]. He told the chiefs that he knew of no god for them other than himself, and told Haman to build him a lofty tower to climb up to the god of Musa [c4][c7]. The ayat say that he and his forces were arrogant in the land and thought that they would not be returned to God [c5].
chapters.body_md: Fir'awn called out among his people, asking whether the kingdom of Egypt was not his and these rivers flowing beneath him, and asking whether they did not see [c1]. He asked why gold ornaments had not been cast upon Musa and why angels had not come with him as companions [c2]. He swayed his people and they obeyed him, for they were a defiantly disobedient people [c3]. Fir'awn said to the chiefs that he knew of no god for them other than himself, told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c4]. He and his forces were arrogant in the land without right and thought that they would not be returned to God [c5].
