Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw and guided them only to the way of right conduct [c6]. Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar, and his evil deed was made to seem fair to him and he was barred from the way, and his plotting was only in ruin [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat record Fir'awn's claims in his own words, including that he guided only to the way of right conduct [c6]. They also record that his evil deed was made to seem fair to him [c7]. An ayah in this passage records a remark by Fir'awn about Musa himself, which this draft does not restate [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn said that he knew of no god for the chiefs other than himself [c4]. He told Haman to build him a lofty tower so that he could climb up to the god of Musa [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets Fir'awn's claims beside the statement that he and his forces thought they would not be returned to God [c5]. Another is that his tower is presented as an attempt to reach the god of Musa [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether the tower was built, or what happened to it.
- Not established: what the ways of the heavens means in detail.
- Not established: how far the kingdom of Egypt extended, or which rivers are meant.
- Not established: how Haman answered.

claims.statement_en: God seized him and his forces and cast them into the sea, and the ayah tells the listener to look at the end of the wrongdoers.
God made them leaders who call to the Fire, on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped, in this world a curse followed them, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.
When they angered God, He took vengeance on them and drowned them all, and made them a precedent and an example for later people.
God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and of the first life, and the ayah says that in this is a lesson for whoever fears.
God says that as He sent a messenger to Fir'awn, He has sent a messenger to the listeners as a witness over them, and that Fir'awn disobeyed the messenger, so God seized him with a heavy seizing.

The family of Fir'awn were enveloped by the worst of punishment, the Fire is shown to them morning and evening, and on the day the Hour is established they are to be entered into the severest punishment.
The Quran asks whether the story of the forces has reached the listener, Fir'awn and Thamud, and says that those who disbelieve are in denial while God encompasses them from behind.

chapters.summary_md: God seized Fir'awn and his forces and cast them into the sea [c1]. The Quran says that a curse followed them in this world [c2] and that God took vengeance on them and drowned them all, making them an example for later people [c3]. It adds that in this is a lesson for whoever fears [c4].
chapters.body_md: God seized him and his forces and cast them into the sea, and the ayah tells the listener to look at the end of the wrongdoers [c1]. God made them leaders who call to the Fire, on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped, in this world a curse followed them, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised [c2]. When they angered God, He took vengeance on them and drowned them all, and made them a precedent and an example for later people [c3]. God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and of the first life, and the ayah says that in this is a lesson for whoever fears [c4]. God says that as He sent a messenger to Fir'awn, He has sent a messenger to the listeners as a witness over them, and that Fir'awn disobeyed the messenger, so God seized him with a heavy seizing [c5]. The family of Fir'awn were enveloped by the worst of punishment, the Fire is shown to them morning and evening, and on the day the Hour is established they are to be entered into the severest punishment [c6]. The Quran asks whether the story of the forces has reached the listener, Fir'awn and Thamud, and says that those who disbelieve are in denial while God encompasses them from behind [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat speak of the end in various ways: a seizing, a drowning, a curse in this world and the Fire shown morning and evening [c1][c3][c5][c6]. The ayat do not explain what the Fire shown morning and evening means for the time between the drowning and the Hour [c6].
chapters.kids_md: God seized Fir'awn and his forces and cast them into the sea [c1]. God made them an example for later people [c3]. The Quran says that in this is a lesson for whoever fears [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat present the end of Fir'awn as a lesson for whoever fears [c4]. Another is that they present his end as an example for later people [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the date or the place of the drowning, or how many were with him.
- Not established in these ayat: what became of his body.
- Not established: who succeeded him, or what became of his people.
- Not established: how the Fire shown morning and evening is to be understood.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give a personal name to the ruler and place him in a dynasty, with different identifications.
Whether Fir'awn is a personal name or a title is not settled by the text.
Hadith to add later: reports about Fir'awn and his end, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces, through those who were weakened, what they feared.
The family of Fir'awn picked up the child, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, and Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error.

chapters.summary_md: God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces what they feared [c1]. The ayah names Haman among those who were in error when the family of Fir'awn picked up the child [c2].
chapters.body_md: God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces, through those who were weakened, what they feared [c1]. The family of Fir'awn picked up the child, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, and Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error [c2].
chapters.deep_md: In both ayat Haman is named after Fir'awn and before the forces [c1][c2]. The ayat do not give his office, and they do not say what he did [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran names Haman beside Fir'awn and their forces [c1][c2]. God wished to show them what they feared [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran names Haman among those who were in error [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Haman's office, his origin or his time.
- Not established: what Haman did in these events.
- Not established: what they feared, beyond the words of the ayah.

claims.statement_en: Fir'awn told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower, so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.
Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.

chapters.summary_md: Fir'awn told Haman to build him a lofty tower so that he might climb up to the god of Musa [c1][c2]. He said that he thought Musa a liar [c1].
chapters.body_md: Fir'awn told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower, so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c1]. Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c2].
chapters.deep_md: One passage tells Haman to light a fire on clay and the other to build [c1][c2]. Neither says whether Haman did it or whether the tower was finished [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn told Haman to build him a lofty tower [c1]. He wanted to climb up to the god of Musa [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passages record an order given to Haman and not his answer [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether Haman built the tower, or how he answered.
- Not established: what became of Haman.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Haman is described as Fir'awn's minister or vizier, and later works discuss his origin and his end.
Whether Haman is a personal name or a title is not settled by the text.
Hadith to add later: reports about Haman, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn.
She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son.
The ayah adds that they did not perceive.

chapters.summary_md: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son [c2].
chapters.body_md: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son [c2]. The ayah adds that they did not perceive [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name the one she speaks of and refers to him only as him [c1]. The words they did not perceive are given after her speech and do not say who is meant [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that her words hope that he might benefit them or be adopted as a son [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: her name, or whether she believed at the time of these words.
- Not established in this ayah: who she is speaking about; the pronoun refers to the child mentioned in the previous ayah.
- Not established: who they are in the words they did not perceive, or what they did not perceive.

claims.statement_en: God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe, when she said, my Lord, build me a house with You in the Garden, save me from Fir'awn and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.

chapters.summary_md: God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe [c1]. She asked her Lord to build her a house with Him in the Garden and to save her from Fir'awn and his deeds [c1].
chapters.body_md: God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe, when she said, my Lord, build me a house with You in the Garden, save me from Fir'awn and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people [c1].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that God set her forth as an example for those who believe, and it gives her prayer [c1]. It does not say when she prayed [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The wife of Fir'awn asked her Lord to build her a house with Him in the Garden [c1]. She also asked Him to save her from Fir'awn and his deeds [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah presents her prayer as an example for those who believe [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when she prayed, or what became of her.
- Not established: whether she is the same woman as the one who spoke about the child, beyond the title the wife of Fir'awn.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: she is called Asiya, and later works describe her faith and her end.
Hadith to add later: reports about the wife of Fir'awn, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who concealed his belief, asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God, when he had come to them with clear proofs from their Lord, adding that if he was lying his lie would be on him, and if he was truthful, some of what he promised would befall them, and that God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.

He said that the kingdom was theirs that day, prevailing in the land, and asked who would help them against the might of God if it came to them, and Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw and guided them only to the way of right conduct.

chapters.summary_md: A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who concealed his belief, asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God [c1]. He asked who would help them against God's might if it came [c2]. Fir'awn answered that he showed them only what he saw [c2].
chapters.body_md: A believing man from the family of Fir'awn, who concealed his belief, asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God, when he had come to them with clear proofs from their Lord, adding that if he was lying his lie would be on him, and if he was truthful, some of what he promised would befall them, and that God does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar [c1]. He said that the kingdom was theirs that day, prevailing in the land, and asked who would help them against the might of God if it came to them, and Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw and guided them only to the way of right conduct [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that he concealed his belief, and it does not say why he now spoke [c1]. Neither the believer nor the man he speaks of is named in this ayah [c1].
chapters.kids_md: A believing man in the family of Fir'awn spoke up [c1]. He asked whether they would kill a man for saying that his Lord is God [c1]. Fir'awn said that he showed them only what he saw [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believer argues that a lie would fall on the liar and a truth would bring some of what is promised [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the believer's name, his rank or his kinship to Fir'awn.
- Not established: how long he had concealed his belief, or how it came to be known.
- Not established in this ayah: who the man is whom the believer defends.

claims.statement_en: The believer said that he feared for them a day like the day of the factions, like the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud and those after them, and that God does not wish injustice for His servants.
He said that he feared for them the day of mutual calling, the day when they would turn back, with no protector for them from God, and that whoever God lets go astray has no guide.

He said that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs, yet they remained in doubt about what he brought, and when he died they said that God would never send a messenger after him, and that thus God lets go astray the transgressor, the doubter.
He said of those who dispute God's signs without any authority that this is greatly hateful to God and to those who believe, and that thus God seals every arrogant, tyrannical heart.

chapters.summary_md: The believer warned them of a day like the day of the factions, like the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud [c1]. He spoke of the day when they would turn back with no protector from God [c2]. He said that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs, yet they remained in doubt [c3].
chapters.body_md: The believer said that he feared for them a day like the day of the factions, like the fate of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud and those after them, and that God does not wish injustice for His servants [c1]. He said that he feared for them the day of mutual calling, the day when they would turn back, with no protector for them from God, and that whoever God lets go astray has no guide [c2]. He said that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs, yet they remained in doubt about what he brought, and when he died they said that God would never send a messenger after him, and that thus God lets go astray the transgressor, the doubter [c3]. He said of those who dispute God's signs without any authority that this is greatly hateful to God and to those who believe, and that thus God seals every arrogant, tyrannical heart [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The believer names earlier peoples as warnings [c1] and then speaks of Yusuf [c3]. The ayah does not say which Yusuf is meant beyond the name, nor when he came to them [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The believer reminded them of the people of Nuh, Ad and Thamud [c1]. He said that Yusuf had come to them with clear proofs, yet they stayed in doubt [c3]. He said that God does not wish injustice for His servants [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believer's warnings begin with earlier peoples and end with a messenger whose proofs they doubted [c1][c3]. Another is that he describes those who dispute God's signs without authority as greatly hated by God and by the believers [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which Yusuf is meant; the ayah gives only the name and says that he came with clear proofs.
- Not established: when Yusuf came to them, or how long he was among them.
- Not established: what the day of the factions or the day of mutual calling mean beyond the words of the ayat.

claims.statement_en: He said, my people, follow me, I will guide you to the way of right conduct, this life is only enjoyment and the Hereafter is the home of settlement, whoever does an evil deed is repaid only the like of it, while whoever does righteous work, male or female, and is a believer, those enter the Garden, provided for without reckoning.

He asked why he called them to salvation while they called him to the Fire, said that they called him to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him what he had no knowledge of, while he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving, and said that what they called him to has no claim in this world or the Hereafter, that their return is to God, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
He said that they would remember what he told them, and that he committed his affair to God, who sees His servants.
God protected him from the evil of what they plotted, and the worst punishment enveloped the family of Fir'awn.

chapters.summary_md: The believer asked them to follow him, and said that he would guide them to the way of right conduct [c1]. He said that he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving, while they called him to the Fire [c2]. He committed his affair to God, who protected him from the evil of what they plotted [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: He said, my people, follow me, I will guide you to the way of right conduct, this life is only enjoyment and the Hereafter is the home of settlement, whoever does an evil deed is repaid only the like of it, while whoever does righteous work, male or female, and is a believer, those enter the Garden, provided for without reckoning [c1]. He asked why he called them to salvation while they called him to the Fire, said that they called him to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him what he had no knowledge of, while he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving, and said that what they called him to has no claim in this world or the Hereafter, that their return is to God, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire [c2]. He said that they would remember what he told them, and that he committed his affair to God, who sees His servants [c3]. God protected him from the evil of what they plotted, and the worst punishment enveloped the family of Fir'awn [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The believer speaks of this life as enjoyment and of the Hereafter as the home of settlement [c1]. The pronoun in the words God protected him is not spelled out, and the ayah does not say whom it refers to beyond the speaker [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The believer asked his people to follow him [c1]. He said that he called them to the Almighty, the Forgiving [c2]. He committed his affair to God, who sees His servants [c3]. God protected him from the evil of what they plotted [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believer ends by committing his affair to God and that the ayah then says God protected him [c3][c4]. Another is that he contrasts calling to the Garden and calling to the Fire [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what became of the believer after these words, beyond the statement that God protected him from the evil of what they plotted.
- Not established: who is meant by him in the words God protected him; the ayah leaves it open.
- Not established: whether the people answered him, or how.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give the believer a name, and the works disagree on it.
Which Yusuf is meant in the believer's words is not stated by the Quran beyond the name.
Hadith to add later: reports about the believer from the family of Fir'awn, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: Qarun was of the people of Musa, and he oppressed them, and God had given him treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men.
His people told him not to exult, for God does not love the exultant.

They told him to seek, in what God had given him, the home of the Hereafter, not to forget his share of this world, to do good as God had done good to him, and not to seek corruption in the land, for God does not love the corrupters.

He said that he had been given it only because of knowledge that he had, and the ayah asks whether he did not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him and had gathered more, and that the guilty are not asked about their sins.

chapters.summary_md: Qarun was of the people of Musa, and God had given him treasures [c1]. His people told him not to exult and to seek the home of the Hereafter in what God had given him [c2][c3]. He said that he had been given it because of knowledge that he had [c4].
chapters.body_md: Qarun was of the people of Musa, and he oppressed them, and God had given him treasures whose keys would weigh down a band of strong men [c1]. His people told him not to exult, for God does not love the exultant [c2]. They told him to seek, in what God had given him, the home of the Hereafter, not to forget his share of this world, to do good as God had done good to him, and not to seek corruption in the land, for God does not love the corrupters [c3]. He said that he had been given it only because of knowledge that he had, and the ayah asks whether he did not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him and had gathered more, and that the guilty are not asked about their sins [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give his people's counsel as a warning against exulting and a call to seek the Hereafter without forgetting his share of this world [c2][c3]. The knowledge he claims is not described [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Qarun had been given great treasures by God [c1]. His people told him not to exult [c2]. He said that he had been given them because of knowledge that he had [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets his people's counsel beside his answer that his wealth came from his own knowledge [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how much wealth he had, or how he came by it.
- Not established: how he was related to the people of Musa, beyond the words that he was of them.
- Not established: what knowledge he claimed.

claims.statement_en: He came out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted the life of this world said that they wished they had what Qarun had been given, for he was possessor of a great fortune.
Those who had been given knowledge said, woe to you, the reward of God is better for one who believes and does good, and none will attain it except the patient.
God made the earth swallow him and his house, and he had no group to help him other than God, and was not of those who could defend themselves.

The next morning, those who had wished for his place the day before said that it is God who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it, and that had God not favoured them, He would have made the earth swallow them, and that the disbelievers do not succeed.

chapters.summary_md: Qarun came out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted this life wished they had what he had [c1]. Those who had been given knowledge said that the reward of God is better [c2]. God made the earth swallow him and his house [c3].
chapters.body_md: He came out before his people in his finery, and those who wanted the life of this world said that they wished they had what Qarun had been given, for he was possessor of a great fortune [c1]. Those who had been given knowledge said, woe to you, the reward of God is better for one who believes and does good, and none will attain it except the patient [c2]. God made the earth swallow him and his house, and he had no group to help him other than God, and was not of those who could defend themselves [c3]. The next morning, those who had wished for his place the day before said that it is God who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it, and that had God not favoured them, He would have made the earth swallow them, and that the disbelievers do not succeed [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passage sets groups of onlookers against each other, those who wanted the life of this world and those who had been given knowledge [c1][c2]. The next morning the first group speaks of God's extending and restricting provision [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Qarun came out before his people in his finery [c1]. Those who had knowledge said that the reward of God is better [c2]. God made the earth swallow him and his house [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the onlookers change their words after the earth swallows him, and speak of God as the one who extends and restricts provision [c1][c4]. Another is that the reward of God is described as better and as reached only by the patient [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the finery was, or where this took place.
- Not established: how the earth swallowed him and his house, or how long after the display.
- Not established: how many were in the groups of onlookers.

claims.statement_en: Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they could not outrun God.

God seized each for his sin, so that against some He sent a storm of stones, some were seized by the blast, some He made the earth swallow, and some He drowned, and God did not wrong them but they wronged themselves.
God sent Musa to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, and they said that he was a lying sorcerer.
When he brought them the truth from God, they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women, and the plotting of the disbelievers was only in error.

chapters.summary_md: Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land [c1]. They said that he was a lying sorcerer [c3]. God seized each for his sin, and the ayah lists various ways in which He did so [c2].
chapters.body_md: Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they could not outrun God [c1]. God seized each for his sin, so that against some He sent a storm of stones, some were seized by the blast, some He made the earth swallow, and some He drowned, and God did not wrong them but they wronged themselves [c2]. God sent Musa to Fir'awn, Haman and Qarun, and they said that he was a lying sorcerer [c3]. When he brought them the truth from God, they said to kill the sons of those who believed with him and spare their women, and the plotting of the disbelievers was only in error [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat name Qarun together with Fir'awn and Haman [c1][c3]. The ayah that lists the ways in which God seized them does not say which fate belonged to whom [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Musa came to Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman with clear proofs [c1]. They were arrogant in the land [c1]. They called Musa a lying sorcerer [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage names Qarun beside the rulers to whom Musa was sent [c1][c3]. Another is that it ends with God saying that He did not wrong them but they wronged themselves [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which of the fates in the ayah was Qarun's.
- Not established: when Qarun spoke against Musa, or in what words beyond those recorded.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works describe a kinship between Qarun and Musa, give the source of his wealth, and give other names for him.
Hadith to add later: reports about Qarun, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The Quran asks whether the listener thought that the companions of the cave and the Raqim were an extraordinary sign among God's signs.
The youths took refuge in the cave and said, our Lord, grant us mercy from You and prepare right guidance for us in our affair.

God struck over their ears in the cave for a number of years, an expression commonly read as sleep, and then raised them up so that He might know which of the parties best counted the time that they had stayed.
God said that He relates their news in truth, that they were youths who believed in their Lord, and that He increased them in guidance.
God strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, we will never call on any god besides Him, for then we would have spoken an outrage.
They said of their people that they had taken gods besides Him, asked why they did not bring a clear authority for them, and asked who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against God.

One of them said that, since they had withdrawn from them and from what they worship except God, they should take refuge in the cave, where their Lord would spread His mercy for them and prepare ease for them in their affair.

chapters.summary_md: The companions of the cave were youths who believed in their Lord, and God increased them in guidance [c4]. They took refuge in the cave and asked their Lord for mercy [c2]. They said that they would never call on any god besides Him [c5], and agreed to withdraw from their people to the cave [c7].
chapters.body_md: The Quran asks whether the listener thought that the companions of the cave and the Raqim were an extraordinary sign among God's signs [c1]. The youths took refuge in the cave and said, our Lord, grant us mercy from You and prepare right guidance for us in our affair [c2]. God struck over their ears in the cave for a number of years, an expression commonly read as sleep, and then raised them up so that He might know which of the parties best counted the time that they had stayed [c3]. God said that He relates their news in truth, that they were youths who believed in their Lord, and that He increased them in guidance [c4]. God strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, we will never call on any god besides Him, for then we would have spoken an outrage [c5]. They said of their people that they had taken gods besides Him, asked why they did not bring a clear authority for them, and asked who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against God [c6]. One of them said that, since they had withdrawn from them and from what they worship except God, they should take refuge in the cave, where their Lord would spread His mercy for them and prepare ease for them in their affair [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The Quran names them the companions of the cave and the Raqim, and the ayat do not explain the word Raqim [c1]. The expression struck over their ears is commonly read as sleep [c3]. The ayat leave open who speaks the last words [c7].
chapters.kids_md: The youths believed in their Lord, and God increased them in guidance [c4]. They took refuge in the cave and asked their Lord for mercy [c2]. They said that they would never call on any god besides God [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the youths took refuge in the cave and asked their Lord for mercy and right guidance [c2]. Another is that God says He strengthened their hearts when they stood up [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how many youths there were, their names, their city, their time or where the cave was.
- Not established: what the Raqim is; the ayah mentions it beside the companions of the cave without explaining it.
- Not established: how many years they stayed in this passage; it says only a number of years, and the length is taken up later in the passage.
- Not established: who their people were, beyond the words their people.

claims.statement_en: The listener would see the sun, when it rose, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it set, passing them on the left, while they were in a wide space within it, which the ayah calls one of God's signs.
Whoever God guides is rightly guided, and whoever He leads astray, for him the listener will find no guiding friend.
The listener would think them awake while they were asleep, and God turned them to the right and to the left, and their dog was at the threshold.
If the listener had looked at them, he would have turned away from them in flight and been filled with fear.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat describe the sun inclining away from their cave on the right when it rose and passing them on the left when it set, while they were in a wide space within it [c1]. They seemed awake though they were asleep, and God turned them to the right and to the left [c3].
chapters.body_md: The listener would see the sun, when it rose, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it set, passing them on the left, while they were in a wide space within it, which the ayah calls one of God's signs [c1]. Whoever God guides is rightly guided, and whoever He leads astray, for him the listener will find no guiding friend [c2]. The listener would think them awake while they were asleep, and God turned them to the right and to the left, and their dog was at the threshold [c3]. If the listener had looked at them, he would have turned away from them in flight and been filled with fear [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah calls the movement of the sun one of God's signs [c1]. It speaks of their dog at the threshold and gives no more about it [c3]. The words about turning away in flight are addressed to the listener and describe the listener's reaction, not the youths [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The sun inclined away from their cave when it rose and passed them when it set [c1]. They seemed awake though they were asleep, and God turned them to the right and to the left [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah describes the youths as kept by God, who turned them to the right and to the left [c3]. Another is that whoever God guides is rightly guided [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how they slept, or why God turned them.
- Not established: which way the cave faced; the ayah speaks of the movement of the sun and gives no compass direction.
- Not established: anything about the dog beyond the words their dog and the threshold. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the dog is given a name in later works.

claims.statement_en: God raised them so that they might question one another, and one of them asked how long they had stayed, and they answered a day or part of a day, and others said that their Lord knew best how long they had stayed.
They said to send one of them with this silver to the city, to see which food is purest and bring provision from it, and to be gentle and let no one learn of them.
They said that if those people found them out, they would stone them or return them to their religion, and then they would never succeed.
God caused them to be found so that people would know that God's promise is true and that the Hour is beyond doubt, when people were disputing among themselves about their affair.
Some said to build a structure over them, their Lord knowing best about them, and those who prevailed over their affair said that they would build a place of prostration over them.

chapters.summary_md: God raised them so that they might question one another, and they answered that they had stayed a day or part of a day [c1]. They sent one of them to the city with silver, asking him to be gentle and let no one learn of them [c2]. God caused them to be found so that people would know that God's promise is true and that the Hour is beyond doubt [c4].
chapters.body_md: God raised them so that they might question one another, and one of them asked how long they had stayed, and they answered a day or part of a day, and others said that their Lord knew best how long they had stayed [c1]. They said to send one of them with this silver to the city, to see which food is purest and bring provision from it, and to be gentle and let no one learn of them [c2]. They said that if those people found them out, they would stone them or return them to their religion, and then they would never succeed [c3]. God caused them to be found so that people would know that God's promise is true and that the Hour is beyond doubt, when people were disputing among themselves about their affair [c4]. Some said to build a structure over them, their Lord knowing best about them, and those who prevailed over their affair said that they would build a place of prostration over them [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that others among them replied that their Lord knew best how long they had stayed [c1]. It records a dispute among people about their affair, and the words of those who prevailed over it [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: God raised them so that they could ask one another how long they had stayed [c1]. They sent one of them to the city with silver to buy food [c2]. God caused them to be found so that people would know that God's promise is true [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat give them the words their Lord knew best about how long they had stayed [c1]. Another is that being found is presented as a way for people to know that God's promise is true [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name of the city, or who ruled it.
- Not established: who those people were that they feared, or how they would have treated them.
- Not established: who the people were who found them, or who prevailed over their affair.
- Not established: what structure or place of prostration was built, or where.

chapters.title_en: The count and the length of the stay

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that people will give differing numbers for the youths, calling these guesses at the unseen, and tells the listener to say that his Lord knows best their number, that few know it, and not to argue about them except with plain argument nor seek information about them from any of them.

The Quran tells the one addressed not to say of anything that he will do it tomorrow, without adding if God wills, to remember his Lord when he forgets, and to say, perhaps my Lord will guide me to something closer to right guidance than this.
The ayah says that they stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine.

The next ayah tells the listener to say that God knows best how long they stayed, that the unseen of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, that He sees and hears perfectly, that they have no guardian besides Him, and that He shares His judgement with no one.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that people will give differing numbers for the youths, and tells the listener to say that his Lord knows best their number [c1]. It states that they stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine [c3], and the next ayah says that God knows best how long they stayed [c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that people will give differing numbers for the youths, calling these guesses at the unseen, and tells the listener to say that his Lord knows best their number, that few know it, and not to argue about them except with plain argument nor seek information about them from any of them [c1]. The Quran tells the one addressed not to say of anything that he will do it tomorrow, without adding if God wills, to remember his Lord when he forgets, and to say, perhaps my Lord will guide me to something closer to right guidance than this [c2]. The ayah says that they stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine [c3]. The next ayah tells the listener to say that God knows best how long they stayed, that the unseen of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, that He sees and hears perfectly, that they have no guardian besides Him, and that He shares His judgement with no one [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The sentence about three hundred years and nine added is followed at once by the statement that God knows best how long they stayed, and readers differ on whether the first is God's own statement or a report of what people say [c3][c4]. The words about saying if God wills are addressed to the listener and sit inside this passage [c2].
chapters.kids_md: People will give different numbers for the youths, but God knows best their number [c1]. The Quran says that they stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine [c3]. Then it says that God knows best how long they stayed [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sends questions about the number and the length of the stay back to God's knowledge [c1][c4]. Another is that it tells the one addressed to say if God wills when speaking of tomorrow [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the number of the youths; the passage reports differing guesses without confirming one, and says that few know it.
- Not established: whether the years are solar or lunar, or whether the sentence about three hundred years and nine added is God's own statement or a report; readers differ.
- Not established: how the words about saying if God wills relate to the account of the youths, beyond their place in the passage.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give names to the youths, their dog, the ruler and the city, say how many they were, and place the cave in different lands.
Hadith to add later: reports about the companions of the cave, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that people ask about Dhul-Qarnayn, and tells the listener to say that he will recite to them a mention of him.
God established him in the land and gave him a means to everything, and he followed a means.

chapters.summary_md: People asked about Dhul-Qarnayn [c1]. God established him in the land and gave him a means to everything, and he followed a means [c2].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that people ask about Dhul-Qarnayn, and tells the listener to say that he will recite to them a mention of him [c1]. God established him in the land and gave him a means to everything, and he followed a means [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives his name as the Arabic title Dhul-Qarnayn, and the ayat do not explain it [c1]. The word rendered means is not explained in these ayat [c2].
chapters.kids_md: People asked about Dhul-Qarnayn [c1]. God established him in the land and gave him a means to everything [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage opens by saying that his place in the land was established by God [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who he was, when he lived or where; the ayat give only the title.
- Not established: whether he was a prophet, a king or both; the ayat say only that God established him in the land.
- Not established: what the title means; the Arabic is a dual form whose sense the ayat do not give.

claims.statement_en: When he reached the place where the sun sets, he found it setting in a spring of murky water and found a people near it.
God said to him, Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish them or treat them with kindness.
He said that whoever did wrong would be punished by them and then returned to his Lord, who would punish him with a terrible punishment.
He said that whoever believed and did good would have the best reward, and that they would speak to him of ease from their command.

chapters.summary_md: Dhul-Qarnayn reached the place where the sun sets and found a people near it [c1]. God told him to punish them or treat them with kindness [c2]. He answered that whoever did wrong would be punished, and whoever believed and did good would have the best reward [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: When he reached the place where the sun sets, he found it setting in a spring of murky water and found a people near it [c1]. God said to him, Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish them or treat them with kindness [c2]. He said that whoever did wrong would be punished by them and then returned to his Lord, who would punish him with a terrible punishment [c3]. He said that whoever believed and did good would have the best reward, and that they would speak to him of ease from their command [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that he found the sun setting in a spring, and the Arabic word for the spring's water is read as murky or as hot [c1]. The ayah says that God spoke to him and does not say how [c2].
chapters.kids_md: He reached the place where the sun sets and found a people there [c1]. God told him to punish them or treat them with kindness [c2]. He said that whoever believed and did good would have the best reward [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that his answer separates the one who did wrong from the one who believed and did good [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the place was, or who the people were.
- Not established: how God spoke to him; the ayah uses the plural we.
- Not established: whether he punished or treated anyone with kindness in the end; the ayah records his words.

claims.statement_en: Dhul-Qarnayn followed a means until he reached the place where the sun rises and found it rising on a people to whom God had given no shelter from it.
The ayah adds that it was so, and that God had full knowledge of what he had.

chapters.summary_md: Dhul-Qarnayn followed a means until he reached the place where the sun rises [c1]. He found it rising on a people to whom God had given no shelter from it [c1].
chapters.body_md: Dhul-Qarnayn followed a means until he reached the place where the sun rises and found it rising on a people to whom God had given no shelter from it [c1]. The ayah adds that it was so, and that God had full knowledge of what he had [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not say what the shelter was that the people lacked [c1]. It adds that God had full knowledge of what he had [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Dhul-Qarnayn followed a means until he reached the place where the sun rises [c1]. God had full knowledge of what he had [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage closes the journey with the statement that God had full knowledge of what he had [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the place was, or who the people were.
- Not established: what kind of shelter is meant, or why they lacked it.

claims.statement_en: He followed a means until he reached a place between the barriers and found beside them a people who could hardly understand speech.
They said, Dhul-Qarnayn, Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the land, and asked whether they might pay him a tribute so that he would set up a barrier between them and Yajuj and Majuj.
He said that what his Lord had established him in was better, and told them to help him with strength so that he would make a rampart between them and Yajuj and Majuj.

He told them to bring him blocks of iron, and when he had made level the space between the steep sides, he told them to blow, and when he had made it fire, he told them to bring him molten metal to pour over it.
They were not able to climb over it, nor were they able to make a breach in it.
He said that this was a mercy from his Lord, and that when the promise of his Lord comes, He will make it crumble to dust, and that the promise of his Lord is true.

chapters.summary_md: Dhul-Qarnayn reached a place between the barriers and found a people who asked him for a barrier against Yajuj and Majuj [c1][c2]. He asked them to help him with strength, and had iron brought [c3][c4]. Yajuj and Majuj could not climb over it, and he called it a mercy from his Lord [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md: He followed a means until he reached a place between the barriers and found beside them a people who could hardly understand speech [c1]. They said, Dhul-Qarnayn, Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the land, and asked whether they might pay him a tribute so that he would set up a barrier between them and Yajuj and Majuj [c2]. He said that what his Lord had established him in was better, and told them to help him with strength so that he would make a rampart between them and Yajuj and Majuj [c3]. He told them to bring him blocks of iron, and when he had made level the space between the steep sides, he told them to blow, and when he had made it fire, he told them to bring him molten metal to pour over it [c4]. They were not able to climb over it, nor were they able to make a breach in it [c5]. He said that this was a mercy from his Lord, and that when the promise of his Lord comes, He will make it crumble to dust, and that the promise of his Lord is true [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not say where the barriers are, or who Yajuj and Majuj are beyond calling them corrupters in the land [c2]. The molten metal is given in Arabic as qitr, and the ayat do not say which metal it is [c4].
chapters.kids_md: He reached a place between the barriers and found a people who could hardly understand speech [c1]. They asked him for a barrier against Yajuj and Majuj [c2]. He told them to help him with strength, and he said that he would make a rampart [c3]. He said that it was a mercy from his Lord [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that he answers the offer of tribute by saying that what his Lord had established him in was better [c3]. Another is that he calls the barrier a mercy from his Lord and puts the promise of his Lord above it [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the barriers were, who the people were, or how many helped him.
- Not established: who Yajuj and Majuj are, how many they are, or when the promise of his Lord comes.
- Not established: which metal the molten metal was, or how long the rampart was built.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Dhul-Qarnayn has been identified with various historical rulers, among them Alexander and Cyrus, and later works describe his journeys and the barrier at length.
Whether he was a prophet is not stated by the Quran and is discussed in later works.
Hadith to add later: reports about Dhul-Qarnayn and about Yajuj and Majuj, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The Quran asks about the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, who said to a prophet of theirs, appoint a king for us so that we may fight in the way of God.

He asked whether, if fighting were decreed for them, they might not fight, and they asked why they should not fight in the way of God when they had been driven out from their homes and from their children, but when fighting was decreed for them, they turned back, except a few of them, and God knows the wrongdoers.

chapters.summary_md: After Musa, the chiefs of the Children of Israel asked a prophet of theirs to appoint a king so that they might fight in the way of God [c1]. When fighting was decreed for them, they turned back, except a few of them [c2].
chapters.body_md: The Quran asks about the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, who said to a prophet of theirs, appoint a king for us so that we may fight in the way of God [c1]. He asked whether, if fighting were decreed for them, they might not fight, and they asked why they should not fight in the way of God when they had been driven out from their homes and from their children, but when fighting was decreed for them, they turned back, except a few of them, and God knows the wrongdoers [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name the prophet or the chiefs [c1]. It reports the prophet's doubt that they would fight, and their answer that they had been driven from their homes and children [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The chiefs of the Children of Israel asked a prophet of theirs to appoint a king [c1]. When fighting was decreed, they turned back, except a few of them [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets the chiefs' words beside what they did when fighting was decreed [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the prophet's name, the chiefs' names, or the time and place. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the prophet is given a name in later works.
- Not established: who drove them out of their homes.
- Not established: how many turned back, or how many stayed.

claims.statement_en: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king for them, and they asked how he could have kingship over them when they were more deserving of it than he, and he had not been given abundance of wealth.
He said that God had chosen him over them and increased him in knowledge and in body, and that God gives His kingship to whom He wills.

Their prophet told them that the sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them, with tranquillity from their Lord in it and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun had left, carried by the angels, and the ayah says that in this is a sign for them if they are believers.

chapters.summary_md: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king for them [c1]. He said that God had chosen him over them and increased him in knowledge and in body [c2]. The sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them [c3].
chapters.body_md: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king for them, and they asked how he could have kingship over them when they were more deserving of it than he, and he had not been given abundance of wealth [c1]. He said that God had chosen him over them and increased him in knowledge and in body, and that God gives His kingship to whom He wills [c2]. Their prophet told them that the sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them, with tranquillity from their Lord in it and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun had left, carried by the angels, and the ayah says that in this is a sign for them if they are believers [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The objection in the ayah is about wealth and about who was more deserving of kingship [c1]. The reply gives God's choice and knowledge and body as the reasons [c2]. The ayat say what the chest contains but not what became of it [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Their prophet told them that God had sent Talut as a king [c1]. They asked how he could be king [c1]. He said that God had chosen him and increased him in knowledge [c2]. The sign of his kingship would be that the chest would come to them [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the prophet answers the objection about wealth by pointing to God's choice and to knowledge [c1][c2]. Another is that the chest is given as a sign for those who believe [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Talut's lineage, his age or what he did before; the ayah gives only the name.
- Not established: what the chest was, where it came from, or what the remnant was.
- Not established: what increased in body means in detail.

claims.statement_en: When Talut set out with the forces, he said that God would test them with a river, so that whoever drank from it was not of him, and whoever did not taste it was of him, except one who scooped a handful with his hand, and they drank from it, except a few of them.

When he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said that they had no strength that day against Jalut and his forces, but those who were certain that they would meet God said that many a small group has overcome a large group by God's permission, and that God is with the patient.
When they went out against Jalut and his forces, they said, our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm and help us against the disbelieving people.
They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut, and God gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed.
The ayah adds that, were it not for God's repelling of people, some by others, the earth would be corrupted, but God is possessor of bounty over the worlds.
God says that these are His signs, which He recites to the listener in truth, and that the listener is among the messengers.

chapters.summary_md: Talut told his forces that God would test them with a river [c1]. When they met Jalut and his forces, they asked God to pour patience upon them [c3]. They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut [c4].
chapters.body_md: When Talut set out with the forces, he said that God would test them with a river, so that whoever drank from it was not of him, and whoever did not taste it was of him, except one who scooped a handful with his hand, and they drank from it, except a few of them [c1]. When he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said that they had no strength that day against Jalut and his forces, but those who were certain that they would meet God said that many a small group has overcome a large group by God's permission, and that God is with the patient [c2]. When they went out against Jalut and his forces, they said, our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm and help us against the disbelieving people [c3]. They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut, and God gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed [c4]. The ayah adds that, were it not for God's repelling of people, some by others, the earth would be corrupted, but God is possessor of bounty over the worlds [c5]. God says that these are His signs, which He recites to the listener in truth, and that the listener is among the messengers [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not say how many drank and how many did not [c1]. It gives the words of those who had no strength that day, and the answer of those who were certain they would meet God [c2]. It names Dawud only in the verse about the defeat of Jalut [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Talut told his forces that God would test them with a river [c1]. When they met Jalut and his forces, they asked God to pour patience upon them [c3]. They defeated them by God's permission, and Dawud killed Jalut [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets the words of those who had no strength that day beside the words of those who were certain they would meet God [c2]. Another is that the victory is attributed to God's permission [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how many were in the forces, how many drank, or where the river was.
- Not established: how Dawud killed Jalut, or how old Dawud was.
- Not established: Jalut's origin or his people. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Talut and Jalut are matched with figures of earlier scriptures, and the numbers of those who crossed the river are given in later works.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the prophet, Talut's lineage and the numbers of the forces are given in later works, and Talut and Jalut are matched with figures of earlier scriptures.
Hadith to add later: reports about the forces who crossed the river, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: God gave Luqman wisdom, saying, be grateful to God.
Whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself, and whoever is ungrateful, God is self-sufficient and worthy of praise.

chapters.summary_md: God gave Luqman wisdom [c1]. The ayah adds that whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself [c2].
chapters.body_md: God gave Luqman wisdom, saying, be grateful to God [c1]. Whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself, and whoever is ungrateful, God is self-sufficient and worthy of praise [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah says that God gave Luqman wisdom, and it does not say that he was a prophet [c1]. The words be grateful to God follow the gift of wisdom [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God gave Luqman wisdom [c1]. Whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the gift of wisdom is joined at once to a call to be grateful to God [c1]. Another is that the ayah says gratitude is for the grateful one's own benefit [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether Luqman was a prophet, a sage or a righteous person; the ayah says only that God gave him wisdom, and readers have differed.
- Not established: his time, his land or his occupation.

claims.statement_en: Luqman said to his son, while advising him, that he should not associate anything with God, since association is a great wrong.

The passage then states that the human being has been enjoined to be kind to his parents, that his mother bore him in weakness upon weakness, and that he should be grateful to God and to his parents, since the return is to God.

It adds that if they strive with him to make him associate with God what he has no knowledge of, he is not to obey them, but is to keep company with them in this world with kindness and follow the way of one who turns to God, for the return is to God, who will tell them what they did.
Luqman told his son that even if a thing were the weight of a grain of mustard seed, inside a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, God would bring it, for God is subtle and aware.
He told him to establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong and be patient with whatever befalls him, for that is among matters of firm resolve.
He told him not to turn away from people in scorn and not to walk in the earth exultantly, for God does not love any self-deluded boaster.
He told him to be moderate in his walking and to lower his voice, for the most disagreeable of voices is the voice of donkeys.

chapters.summary_md: Luqman told his son not to associate anything with God [c1]. He told him that God would bring even a thing the weight of a grain of mustard seed [c4], and to establish prayer and be patient [c5]. He told him not to walk exultantly, to be moderate in his walking and to lower his voice [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md: Luqman said to his son, while advising him, that he should not associate anything with God, since association is a great wrong [c1]. The passage then states that the human being has been enjoined to be kind to his parents, that his mother bore him in weakness upon weakness, and that he should be grateful to God and to his parents, since the return is to God [c2]. It adds that if they strive with him to make him associate with God what he has no knowledge of, he is not to obey them, but is to keep company with them in this world with kindness and follow the way of one who turns to God, for the return is to God, who will tell them what they did [c3]. Luqman told his son that even if a thing were the weight of a grain of mustard seed, inside a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, God would bring it, for God is subtle and aware [c4]. He told him to establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong and be patient with whatever befalls him, for that is among matters of firm resolve [c5]. He told him not to turn away from people in scorn and not to walk in the earth exultantly, for God does not love any self-deluded boaster [c6]. He told him to be moderate in his walking and to lower his voice, for the most disagreeable of voices is the voice of donkeys [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passage places a statement about kindness to parents between Luqman's first and later words, and the ayat do not mark whether it is his speech or God's [c2][c3]. The ayah also gives a period for weaning, which this draft leaves out of its claims [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Luqman told his son not to associate anything with God [c1]. He told him that God would bring even a thing the weight of a grain of mustard seed [c4]. He told him to be patient, to be moderate in his walking and to lower his voice [c5][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Luqman begins his advice with the greatest wrong and ends with matters of conduct such as walking and speaking [c1][c7]. Another is that the passage places kindness to parents beside the warning not to obey them in association with God [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the son's name or age, or how he answered.
- Not established: whether the passage about parents is Luqman's speech or God's own words added within it.
- Not established: what the voice of donkeys refers to beyond the comparison in the ayah.
- Not established: where and when Luqman said these things.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give a name to Luqman's son and describe Luqman's origin and occupation.
Whether Luqman was a prophet is not stated by the Quran; the text says that God gave him wisdom.
Hadith to add later: reports about Luqman, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: Some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman.
Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery.
They also followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut.
They did not teach anyone until they had said that they were only a trial, and that he should therefore not disbelieve.
People learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they harm no one by it except by God's permission.
They learned what harms them and does not benefit them, and they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah says that some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman, and that Sulayman did not disbelieve [c1][c2]. It also says that they followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut, who taught no one until they had said that they were only a trial [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: Some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman [c1]. Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery [c2]. They also followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut [c3]. They did not teach anyone until they had said that they were only a trial, and that he should therefore not disbelieve [c4]. People learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they harm no one by it except by God's permission [c5]. They learned what harms them and does not benefit them, and they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah is one long sentence, and it does not say who the people are who followed what the devils recited [c1]. The Arabic word for the pair can be read as angels or as kings in different recitations [c3]. The Arabic word ma can be read as what or as not, and the sense of the clause changes with it [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman did not disbelieve [c2]. The ayah says that Harut and Marut told anyone who came to them that they were only a trial, so that he should not disbelieve [c4]. It says that whoever buys what harms him has no share in the Hereafter [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah separates Sulayman from disbelief and puts the teaching of sorcery on the devils [c2]. Another is that it presents what people learned as harming them and not benefiting them [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the people are who followed what the devils recited, or when this happened.
- Not established: whether the Arabic is to be read as angels or kings, or whether what was sent down is affirmed or denied; the recitations and the readers differ, and this draft does not choose.
- Not established: where Babil was, or what the trial consisted of.
- Not established: anything about their nature, what they taught beyond the words of the ayah, or what became of them.

uncertainties_en: Many accounts about Harut and Marut circulate in later works; none is used here, and this draft adds nothing to what the one ayah states.
Hadith to add later: reports about Harut and Marut are numerous and graded differently; each would need a named grader, with the text of the ayah as the control; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God.
The disciples said that they were God's helpers, that they believed in God, and asked him to bear witness that they submit.
They said, our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and have followed the messenger, so write us down among the witnesses.

chapters.summary_md: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers and that they believed in God [c2]. They prayed to be written down among the witnesses [c3].
chapters.body_md: When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers, that they believed in God, and asked him to bear witness that they submit [c2]. They said, our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and have followed the messenger, so write us down among the witnesses [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the disciples' answer in parts, an address to Isa and a prayer to their Lord [c2][c3]. The word for submit, muslimun, is rendered by its general sense here [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Isa asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers [c2]. They prayed to be written down among the witnesses [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the disciples answer a call for help with a statement of belief and a prayer [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who they were, how many, or where this took place.
- Not established: from whom Isa sensed disbelief, beyond the word them.
- Not established: what the word hawariyyun means in its origin; the ayat use it without explaining it.

claims.statement_en: God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger, and that they said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger [c1]. They said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit [c1].
chapters.body_md: God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger, and that they said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit [c1].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah speaks of an inspiration to the disciples, and the verb is the one used for inspiration generally [c1]. It does not say how the inspiration came [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger [c1]. They said that they believed [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah presents the disciples' belief as something God inspired [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how the inspiration came to them.
- Not established in this ayah: who the messenger is; the ayah does not name him.

claims.statement_en: God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples, who are my helpers toward God, and the disciples said that they were God's helpers.
One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group disbelieved, and God supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became prevailing.

chapters.summary_md: God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another disbelieved [c2]. God supported those who believed against their enemy [c2].
chapters.body_md: God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples, who are my helpers toward God, and the disciples said that they were God's helpers [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group disbelieved, and God supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became prevailing [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah recalls the call of Isa as an example for the believers [c1]. The Arabic word rendered prevailing can also mean uppermost or manifest, and the ayah does not say in what way they prevailed [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Isa, son of Maryam, asked the disciples who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group did not [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah asks the believers to answer as the disciples answered [c1]. Another is that it ends by recording that God supported those who believed [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the enemy was, or when this support came.
- Not established: in what way those who believed prevailed.
- Not established: the numbers in the groups, or how they divided.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the disciples are numbered and named in later works, with their occupations and their travels.
Hadith to add later: reports about the disciples of Isa, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: The man who came from the farthest part of the city

chapters.title_en: The man from the farthest part of the city

claims.statement_en: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, my people, follow the messengers.
He told them to follow those who ask them for no payment and who are rightly guided.

He asked why he should not worship the One who created him and to whom they will be returned, and asked whether he should take gods besides Him, when, if the Merciful wished him harm, their intercession would not avail him at all and they could not rescue him, for then he would be in clear error.
He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him.
He was told to enter the Garden, and he said that he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honoured.

chapters.summary_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and told his people to follow the messengers [c1]. He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden, and he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him [c5].
chapters.body_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, my people, follow the messengers [c1]. He told them to follow those who ask them for no payment and who are rightly guided [c2]. He asked why he should not worship the One who created him and to whom they will be returned, and asked whether he should take gods besides Him, when, if the Merciful wished him harm, their intercession would not avail him at all and they could not rescue him, for then he would be in clear error [c3]. He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden, and he said that he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honoured [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not name the man, the city or the messengers [c1]. The ayah says that he was told to enter the Garden and does not say how or when he came to be there [c5].
chapters.kids_md: A man came running from the farthest part of the city [c1]. He told his people to follow the messengers [c1]. He said that he believed in their Lord [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the man argues from his own worship of the One who created him [c3]. Another is that the passage ends with his wish that his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the man's name, his age or his work.
- Not established: the name of the city, or who the messengers were; the ayat before this passage speak of them.
- Not established: how he came to be told to enter the Garden, or what his people did.
- Not established: whether he is related to any other man described with similar words in another passage; nothing in the ayat links them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is called Habib, and the city is identified in later works.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is called Habib, and later works give his trade, the name of the city and the manner of his death.
Hadith to add later: reports about the man of the city, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

stories.title_en: The man who passed by a ruined town

chapters.title_en: The town and the hundred years

claims.statement_en: The Quran gives the case of one who passed by a town that had fallen in ruins over its roofs, and he asked how God would give it life after its death.
God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him.
He was asked how long he had stayed, and he said a day or part of a day, and he was told that he had stayed a hundred years.

He was told to look at his food and drink, which had not spoiled, and at his donkey, so that God might make him a sign for the people, and to look at the bones, how God sets them together and then clothes them with flesh.
When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things.

chapters.summary_md: A man passed by a town that had fallen in ruins and asked how God would give it life after its death [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.body_md: The Quran gives the case of one who passed by a town that had fallen in ruins over its roofs, and he asked how God would give it life after its death [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. He was asked how long he had stayed, and he said a day or part of a day, and he was told that he had stayed a hundred years [c3].
