He was told to look at his food and drink, which had not spoiled, and at his donkey, so that God might make him a sign for the people, and to look at the bones, how God sets them together and then clothes them with flesh [c4]. When it became clear to him, he said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah does not name the man or the town [c1]. It does not say who asked him how long he had stayed [c3]. The Arabic for how God sets the bones together is read in more than one way in the recitations [c4].
chapters.kids_md: A man passed by a town that had fallen in ruins [c1]. God caused him to die for a hundred years and then raised him [c2]. He thought he had stayed a day or part of a day, and was told that it was a hundred years [c3]. He said that he knew that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the man's question about the town is answered by what happened to him [c1][c2]. Another is that his last words are a statement that God has power over all things [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the man's name, his faith or whether he was a prophet; the ayah calls him one who passed by a town.
- Not established: the name of the town, or who destroyed it.
- Not established: who asked him how long he had stayed; the ayah does not name the speaker.
- Not established: what the sign for the people was, beyond the words of the ayah.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man and the town are identified in later works.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is identified as Uzayr or as another figure, and the town as Jerusalem; the text itself names neither.
Hadith to add later: reports about the man who passed by the town, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished.
His wealth and what he earned did not avail him.
He will burn in a fire of flame.
His wife is mentioned as the carrier of firewood.
Her neck has a rope of palm fibre around it.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished [c1]. His wealth and what he earned did not avail him [c2]. It says that he will burn in a fire of flame, and it mentions his wife as the carrier of firewood [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that the hands of Abu Lahab have perished, and that he has perished [c1]. His wealth and what he earned did not avail him [c2]. He will burn in a fire of flame [c3]. His wife is mentioned as the carrier of firewood [c4]. Her neck has a rope of palm fibre around it [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage names him as Abu Lahab and gives no other name [c1]. It speaks of his wife in the last ayat, and the ayat do not say what the carrier of firewood refers to [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran says that Abu Lahab's wealth and what he earned did not help him [c2]. His wife is called the carrier of firewood [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage says wealth and earnings did not avail him [c2]. Another is that the passage speaks of his wife as well as of him [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established in these ayat: who Abu Lahab was, what his own name was, or why he is named in this way. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is identified as an uncle of Muhammad, and his own name is given as Abd al-Uzza.
- Not established: the wife's name, or what the carrier of firewood means; the phrase can be read literally or figuratively.
- Not established: the occasion on which the passage was revealed; it names no event.
- Not established: what the rope of palm fibre signifies.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man is identified with an uncle of Muhammad, his wife is given a name, and the occasion of the passage is told in later works.
Hadith to add later: reports about the occasion of the passage, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: God sent Hud to 'Ad; the ayat call Hud their brother, and 'Ad denied the messengers.
Hud told his people to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him.
Hud told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him.
Hud told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds.
Hud told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, and said that He would then send abundant rain from the sky on them and add strength to their strength.
Hud told them not to turn away as criminals.
Hud told them to remember that God had made them successors after the people of Nuh and had increased them abundantly in creation.
Hud told them to remember what God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs.
Hud asked them whether they built a sign on every high ground for amusement, took up strong buildings in the hope of living on, and seized people as tyrants.
Hud told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day.
Another passage speaks of the brother of 'Ad, who warned his people at al-Ahqaf, after warners had passed before him and after him, telling them to worship only God.

chapters.summary_md: God sent Hud to 'Ad, who called them to worship God alone and to fear Him [c1][c2][c3]. He asked no wage, reminded them of what God had given them and warned them of the punishment of a great day [c4][c8][c10].
chapters.body_md: God sent Hud to 'Ad; the ayat call Hud their brother, and 'Ad denied the messengers [c1]. Hud told his people to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him [c2]. Hud told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him [c3]. Hud told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds [c4]. Hud told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, and said that He would then send abundant rain from the sky on them and add strength to their strength [c5]. Hud told them not to turn away as criminals [c6]. Hud told them to remember that God had made them successors after the people of Nuh and had increased them abundantly in creation [c7]. Hud told them to remember what God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs [c8]. Hud asked them whether they built a sign on every high ground for amusement, took up strong buildings in the hope of living on, and seized people as tyrants [c9]. Hud told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day [c10]. Another passage speaks of the brother of 'Ad, who warned his people at al-Ahqaf, after warners had passed before him and after him, telling them to worship only God [c11].
chapters.deep_md:
- God sent Hud to 'Ad; the ayat call Hud their brother, and 'Ad denied the messengers (7:65, 26:123-124) [c1].
- Hud told his people to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him (7:65) [c2].
- Hud told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him (26:125-126) [c3].
- Hud told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds (26:127, 11:51) [c4].
- Hud told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, and said that He would then send abundant rain from the sky on them and add strength to their strength (11:52) [c5].
- Hud told them not to turn away as criminals (11:52) [c6].
- Hud told them to remember that God had made them successors after the people of Nuh and had increased them abundantly in creation (7:69) [c7].
- Hud told them to remember what God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs (26:132-134) [c8].
- Hud asked them whether they built a sign on every high ground for amusement, took up strong buildings in the hope of living on, and seized people as tyrants (26:128-130) [c9].
- Hud told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day (26:135) [c10].
- Another passage speaks of the brother of 'Ad, who warned his people at al-Ahqaf, after warners had passed before him and after him, telling them to worship only God (46:21) [c11].
chapters.kids_md: God sent Hud to his people, the people of 'Ad [c1]. Hud told them to worship God alone [c2]. He reminded them of the good things God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs [c8]. He also warned them of a great day of punishment [c10].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Hud's reminder joins the gifts God had given with the call to worship Him [c8][c2]. One reading is that the passage asks the listener to look at what they have been given and to ask what it is for [c8][c9].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the Quran does not say where 'Ad lived beyond the single mention of al-Ahqaf, nor when, nor how many they were.
- Not established: whether the brother of 'Ad in 46:21 is the same person as Hud is not stated in that ayah; the draft reads it that way because 'Ad and Hud are joined in 7:65 and 26:124.
- Not established: what exactly the high ground (a word read in more than one way) and the strong buildings of 26:128-129 were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the region where 'Ad lived, and any dates; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The chiefs of his people who disbelieved told Hud that they saw him in foolishness and thought him one of the liars.
Hud answered that there was no foolishness in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds who conveyed his Lord's messages and was a trustworthy adviser to them.
They asked Hud whether he had come so that they should worship God alone and leave what their fathers worshipped, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful.
They told Hud that he had brought no clear proof, that they would not leave their gods on his word, and that they did not believe in him.
They said that they could only say that some of their gods had struck Hud with evil.
Hud called God to witness, and told them to bear witness, that he was free of what they set up with God besides Him.
Hud told them that he had put his trust in God, his Lord and their Lord.
Hud told them that if they turned away he had already conveyed what he was sent with, and that his Lord would make another people successors in their place.

Hud told them that abomination and anger from their Lord had already fallen on them, and asked whether they disputed with him about names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority.
Hud told them to wait, saying that he was waiting with them.
They told Hud that it was the same to them whether he admonished them or was not one of those who admonish, that this was only the way of the earlier people, and that they would not be punished.

Another passage says that 'Ad were arrogant in the land without right and said who was stronger than they in strength, and it asks whether they did not see that God who created them was stronger than they in strength.
The same passage says that 'Ad used to reject the signs of God.

chapters.summary_md: The chiefs of 'Ad called Hud foolish and a liar, refused to leave their gods and told him to bring the punishment he threatened [c1][c3][c4]. Hud replied that he was a messenger, put his trust in God and told them to wait [c2][c7][c10].
chapters.body_md: The chiefs of his people who disbelieved told Hud that they saw him in foolishness and thought him one of the liars [c1]. Hud answered that there was no foolishness in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds who conveyed his Lord's messages and was a trustworthy adviser to them [c2]. They asked Hud whether he had come so that they should worship God alone and leave what their fathers worshipped, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful [c3]. They told Hud that he had brought no clear proof, that they would not leave their gods on his word, and that they did not believe in him [c4]. They said that they could only say that some of their gods had struck Hud with evil [c5]. Hud called God to witness, and told them to bear witness, that he was free of what they set up with God besides Him [c6]. Hud told them that he had put his trust in God, his Lord and their Lord [c7]. Hud told them that if they turned away he had already conveyed what he was sent with, and that his Lord would make another people successors in their place [c8]. Hud told them that abomination and anger from their Lord had already fallen on them, and asked whether they disputed with him about names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority [c9]. Hud told them to wait, saying that he was waiting with them [c10]. They told Hud that it was the same to them whether he admonished them or was not one of those who admonish, that this was only the way of the earlier people, and that they would not be punished [c11]. Another passage says that 'Ad were arrogant in the land without right and said who was stronger than they in strength, and it asks whether they did not see that God who created them was stronger than they in strength [c12]. The same passage says that 'Ad used to reject the signs of God [c13].
chapters.deep_md:
- The chiefs of his people who disbelieved told Hud that they saw him in foolishness and thought him one of the liars (7:66) [c1].
- Hud answered that there was no foolishness in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds who conveyed his Lord's messages and was a trustworthy adviser to them (7:67-68) [c2].
- They asked Hud whether he had come so that they should worship God alone and leave what their fathers worshipped, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful (7:70) [c3].
- They told Hud that he had brought no clear proof, that they would not leave their gods on his word, and that they did not believe in him (11:53) [c4].
- They said that they could only say that some of their gods had struck Hud with evil (11:54) [c5].
- Hud called God to witness, and told them to bear witness, that he was free of what they set up with God besides Him (11:54-55) [c6].
- Hud told them that he had put his trust in God, his Lord and their Lord (11:56) [c7].
- Hud told them that if they turned away he had already conveyed what he was sent with, and that his Lord would make another people successors in their place (11:57) [c8].
- Hud told them that abomination and anger from their Lord had already fallen on them, and asked whether they disputed with him about names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority (7:71) [c9].
- Hud told them to wait, saying that he was waiting with them (7:71) [c10].
- They told Hud that it was the same to them whether he admonished them or was not one of those who admonish, that this was only the way of the earlier people, and that they would not be punished (26:136-138) [c11].
- Another passage says that 'Ad were arrogant in the land without right and said who was stronger than they in strength, and it asks whether they did not see that God who created them was stronger than they in strength (41:15) [c12].
- The same passage says that 'Ad used to reject the signs of God (41:15) [c13].
chapters.kids_md: Some of the people of 'Ad would not listen to Hud [c1]. They said they would not leave their gods [c4]. Hud said that he was a messenger and that he trusted God [c2][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passages show a people who answered a call with insults and with loyalty to their fathers' ways [c1][c3]. One reading is that the same ayat show Hud answering without insult and returning to trust in God [c2][c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the speaker of the words 'rather it is what you sought to hasten' in 46:24 is not named; it is treated in the next chapter.
- Not established: the exact sense of the word translated abomination in 7:71 is read in more than one way, and the draft keeps the plain word.
- Not established: how long Hud spoke to them, how many believed, or who the chiefs were by name.
- Not established: the draft does not use 41:13-14, whose pronouns are not stated in those ayat; 41:15 names 'Ad.

claims.statement_en: God saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and saved them from a heavy punishment.
The Quran says that 'Ad rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every stubborn tyrant.
When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said it was a cloud that would give them rain.
The ayah answers that it was what they had asked to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment.
The wind destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and they became people of whom nothing could be seen except their dwellings.
God sent on them a furious wind in days of misfortune, to make them taste a punishment of disgrace in the life of this world.
The Quran calls the wind barren and says that it left nothing it came upon without making it like something decayed.
God made the wind work against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and the ayah says that the people lay overthrown in it like hollow trunks of palm trees.
The ayah then asks whether any remnant of them can be seen.
God had given them hearing, sight and hearts, but these were of no use to them because they used to reject the signs of God, and what they used to mock at surrounded them.
A curse followed them in this life and follows them on the Day of Resurrection, and the passage ends by saying away with 'Ad, the people of Hud.
The Quran says that God destroyed the first 'Ad.
Another passage asks whether the hearer has not seen how God dealt with 'Ad and names Iram, with pillars, the like of which was not created in the land.
The Quran says that in their destruction there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.

chapters.summary_md: God saved Hud and those who believed with him by His mercy [c1]. A wind sent against 'Ad destroyed what it came upon, and the Quran calls their end a sign [c6][c7][c14].
chapters.body_md: God saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and saved them from a heavy punishment [c1]. The Quran says that 'Ad rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every stubborn tyrant [c2]. When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said it was a cloud that would give them rain [c3]. The ayah answers that it was what they had asked to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment [c4]. The wind destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and they became people of whom nothing could be seen except their dwellings [c5]. God sent on them a furious wind in days of misfortune, to make them taste a punishment of disgrace in the life of this world [c6]. The Quran calls the wind barren and says that it left nothing it came upon without making it like something decayed [c7]. God made the wind work against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and the ayah says that the people lay overthrown in it like hollow trunks of palm trees [c8]. The ayah then asks whether any remnant of them can be seen [c9]. God had given them hearing, sight and hearts, but these were of no use to them because they used to reject the signs of God, and what they used to mock at surrounded them [c10]. A curse followed them in this life and follows them on the Day of Resurrection, and the passage ends by saying away with 'Ad, the people of Hud [c11]. The Quran says that God destroyed the first 'Ad [c12]. Another passage asks whether the hearer has not seen how God dealt with 'Ad and names Iram, with pillars, the like of which was not created in the land [c13]. The Quran says that in their destruction there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers [c14].
chapters.deep_md:
- God saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and saved them from a heavy punishment (11:58, 7:72) [c1].
- The Quran says that 'Ad rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every stubborn tyrant (11:59) [c2].
- When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said it was a cloud that would give them rain (46:24) [c3].
- The ayah answers that it was what they had asked to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment (46:24) [c4].
- The wind destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and they became people of whom nothing could be seen except their dwellings (46:25) [c5].
- God sent on them a furious wind in days of misfortune, to make them taste a punishment of disgrace in the life of this world (41:16, 54:19) [c6].
- The Quran calls the wind barren and says that it left nothing it came upon without making it like something decayed (51:41-42) [c7].
- God made the wind work against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and the ayah says that the people lay overthrown in it like hollow trunks of palm trees (69:7) [c8].
- The ayah then asks whether any remnant of them can be seen (69:8) [c9].
- God had given them hearing, sight and hearts, but these were of no use to them because they used to reject the signs of God, and what they used to mock at surrounded them (46:26) [c10].
- A curse followed them in this life and follows them on the Day of Resurrection, and the passage ends by saying away with 'Ad, the people of Hud (11:60) [c11].
- The Quran says that God destroyed the first 'Ad (53:50) [c12].
- Another passage asks whether the hearer has not seen how God dealt with 'Ad and names Iram, with pillars, the like of which was not created in the land (89:6-8) [c13].
- The Quran says that in their destruction there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers (26:139) [c14].
chapters.kids_md: God saved Hud and the people who believed with him [c1]. A strong wind came against 'Ad, and it did what God commanded [c5][c6]. The Quran calls what happened to them a sign [c14].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage joins the rescue of the believers with the end of those who rejected the signs [c1][c10]. One reading is that hearing and sight are gifts, and that the ayah asks what a person does with them [c10].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where this happened, how long ago, or how many people were saved.
- Not established: whether Iram in 89:7 names a people, a place or both, how it relates to 'Ad, and what the pillars were; the ayat leave this open.
- Not established: the exact meaning of the first 'Ad in 53:50 and of the word for the wind (a furious or violent wind, read in more than one way).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of Iram with a particular city or region, and any date for the event.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Hud and 'Ad. None is used in this draft.

Wording a scholar should check first: 41:16 and 54:19 (days of misfortune, or a day of continuing misfortune), 7:69 (increase in creation), 26:128-129 (high ground, strong buildings), 7:71 (abomination), 26:137 (the way of the earlier people), 89:7 (Iram), 53:50 (the first 'Ad), 11:52 (rain from the sky in abundance).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the location, size and date of 'Ad; none is used.

claims.statement_en: God sent Salih to Thamud, and the ayat call Salih their brother.
Salih told them to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him.
Salih told them that a clear proof had come to them from their Lord.
Salih told them that this was God's she-camel, a sign for them.
Salih told them to leave her to eat in God's land and not to touch her with harm, or punishment would seize them.
Salih told them that the she-camel had a drink and they had a drink, each on a known day.
Another passage has God say that He was sending the she-camel as a trial for them, and it tells the one addressed to watch them and be patient.
The same passage says that the water was divided between them, and that each drink was to be attended.
Another passage says that God gave Thamud the she-camel as a sign to see, that they did wrong with it, and that signs are sent only to warn.
Salih told them to remember that God had made them successors after 'Ad and settled them in the land, where they took palaces from its plains and carved houses from the mountains.
Salih told them to remember the favours of God and not to spread corruption in the land.
Salih told them that he was a trustworthy messenger, that they should fear God and obey him, and that he asked them for no wage.
Salih asked them whether they would be left secure in what was there: gardens and springs, fields and palm trees, and houses carved with skill from the mountains.
Salih told them not to obey the order of the transgressors, who spread corruption in the land and did not put things right.
Salih told them to ask forgiveness of God and turn back to Him, for his Lord is near and answers.

chapters.kids_md: God sent Salih to his people, Thamud [c1]. Salih told them to worship God [c2]. He showed them God's she-camel as a sign [c4]. He told them to let her eat in God's land and not to hurt her [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The reminders of Salih tie the favours his people enjoyed to the call not to spread corruption [c10][c11]. One reading is that the she-camel's drink and the people's drink on separate days put a shared resource in front of them as a test [c6][c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the Quran does not say where Thamud lived in these ayat, when, or how many they were.
- Not established: the speaker and the one addressed in 54:27-28 are not named; the draft reads the speaker as God, and the one addressed as a person told to watch them.
- Not established: what the dual-drink arrangement of 26:155 meant in practice, or how long the she-camel was among them.
- Not established: the sense of the word read here as did wrong with it in 17:59 is read in more than one way.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the region where Thamud lived, the manner in which the she-camel appeared, and any dates; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The chiefs who were arrogant asked those considered weak, who had believed, whether they knew that Salih was sent by his Lord, and the believers answered that they believed in what he was sent with.
Those who were arrogant said that they disbelieved in what the others believed.

They told Salih that he had been hoped for among them before this, asked whether he forbade them to worship what their fathers worshipped, and said they were in grave doubt about what he called them to.

Salih asked them to consider whether, if he was on a clear proof from his Lord and had mercy from Him, anyone could help him against God if he disobeyed Him, and said they would add nothing for him but loss.
They told Salih that he was only one of the bewitched, only a human like them, and told him to bring a sign if he was truthful.
Another passage says that Thamud denied the warnings, and asked whether they would follow one human from among them, saying that then they would be in error and madness.
They asked whether the reminder had been cast on him from among them, and said that he was an insolent liar.
The next ayah says that they will know tomorrow who the insolent liar is.
The Quran says that God guided Thamud, but they preferred blindness to guidance.
Another passage says that they became opposed groups disputing with each other.
Salih asked them why they hastened evil before good, and why they did not ask forgiveness of God so that they might receive mercy.
They told Salih that they took him and those with him as an ill omen, and he answered that their omen was with God and that they were a people being tested.
The ayat say that there were nine groups in the city who spread corruption and did not put things right.

They told one another to swear by God that they would attack him and his family by night, and then tell his guardian that they had not witnessed the destruction of his family and were telling the truth.
The Quran says that Thamud denied through their transgression, when the most wretched of them rose up.
The messenger sent by God told them: the she-camel of God and her drink.

chapters.summary_md: The chiefs who were arrogant refused to believe, and Thamud told Salih that he was only a human like them and asked for a sign [c1][c2][c5]. Salih answered that his Lord would not be disobeyed and asked them why they hastened evil before good [c4][c11].

chapters.kids_md: Some of the people of Thamud would not believe Salih [c2]. They said he was only a human like them [c5]. Salih asked them to ask forgiveness of God so that they might receive mercy [c11].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat show an argument between those who thought themselves strong and those they thought weak, about whether to believe a messenger [c1][c2]. One reading is that Salih answers a challenge with a question about asking forgiveness [c11].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the chiefs, the most wretched one, the guardian or the nine groups were by name, or whether the nine groups were the same people as the chiefs.
- Not established: in 27:49 the ayat do not name whose family is meant; the draft reads him as Salih.
- Not established: the pronoun of he is not named in 91:13; the ayah says the messenger of God, and the draft reads this as Salih.
- Not established: the sense of the word read here as bewitched in 26:153 is read in more than one way.

claims.statement_en: They hamstrung the she-camel, defied the command of their Lord, and told Salih to bring what he threatened if he was one of the messengers.
Another passage says that they called their companion, who took it up and hamstrung her.
Another passage says that they denied Salih and hamstrung her.
Salih told them to enjoy themselves in their home three days, saying that this was a promise not to be denied.
The Quran says that they were told to enjoy themselves for a while, but they defied the command of their Lord.
The Quran says that in the morning they were regretful.
The ayat word what seized them in different ways: a tremor, so that they lay fallen in their home.
The ayat also say that a cry seized the wrongdoers so that they lay fallen in their homes, and that God sent on them one cry and they became like dry twigs.
The ayat also say that a thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them, that it seized them while they looked on, and that they could not stand up and could not help themselves.
The Quran says that Thamud were destroyed by the overpowering one.
Their Lord crushed them for their sin and levelled it, and He does not fear its consequence.
Salih turned away from them and said that he had conveyed the message of his Lord and advised them, but that they did not love those who advise.
God saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and from the disgrace of that day.
God saved those who believed and feared Him.
They plotted a plot and God plotted a plot, and they did not perceive.
God destroyed them and their people all together, and their houses stand empty because of their wrongdoing.
The passage says that it was as if they had never lived there, and ends by saying away with Thamud.
The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.

chapters.summary_md: Thamud hamstrung the she-camel and defied their Lord's command [c1]. Salih told them to enjoy themselves in their home three days, and then punishment seized them; God saved Salih and those who believed with him [c4][c7][c8][c13].

chapters.kids_md: The people of Thamud hurt the she-camel, though they had been told not to [c1]. Salih told them they had only three days at home [c4]. Then God's punishment came, and God saved Salih and those who believed with him [c13].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat set the respite given to Thamud beside the warning that went unheeded [c4][c5]. One reading is that a warning given plainly and answered by defiance is the theme of this chapter [c1][c12].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the Quran does not say how long ago this was, where it happened, or how many were saved.
- Not established: whether the tremor, the cry, the thunderbolt and the overpowering one are one event described in different ways or different aspects of it; the draft does not decide.
- Not established: who the companion of 54:29 was, and whether one person or more than one hamstrung the she-camel (7:77 and 91:14 are worded in the plural).
- Not established: the three days of 11:65 are stated by Salih in the ayah; the ayat do not say when they began.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the people involved, the sign that marked the days, and the location of Thamud's dwellings.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that the Companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers.
God gave them His signs, but they turned away from them.
They used to carve houses from the mountains, in security.
The cry seized them in the morning.
What they used to earn did not help them.

chapters.summary_md: The Companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers and turned away from the signs God gave them [c1][c2]. The cry seized them, and what they had earned did not help them [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that the Companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers [c1]. God gave them His signs, but they turned away from them [c2]. They used to carve houses from the mountains, in security [c3]. The cry seized them in the morning [c4]. What they used to earn did not help them [c5].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran says that the Companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers (15:80) [c1].
- God gave them His signs, but they turned away from them (15:81) [c2].
- They used to carve houses from the mountains, in security (15:82) [c3].
- The cry seized them in the morning (15:83) [c4].
- What they used to earn did not help them (15:84) [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The Companions of al-Hijr turned away from God's signs [c2]. They had carved houses in the mountains and felt safe [c3]. But the cry came in the morning, and what they had earned did not help them [c4][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage sets security in houses against turning away from signs [c2][c3]. One reading is that earnings and safe houses did not decide the outcome [c3][c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the ayat do not say that the Companions of al-Hijr are Thamud; the inventory places this passage with Thamud.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the Companions of al-Hijr with Thamud, and of al-Hijr with a particular place.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Salih and Thamud. None is used in this draft.
Inventory refs not used: 85:17-18 (a single mention beside another people) and 69:4 (shared with 'Ad).

Wording a scholar should check first: 17:59 (the sense of the verb read as did wrong with it), 26:153 (bewitched), 54:29 (the companion), 27:48-49 (the nine groups and whose family), 91:13 (the messenger of God), 54:26 (the speaker), 69:5 (the overpowering one), 7:78 (tremor), 51:43 (for a while), 27:45 (the dual number of the opposed groups is rendered as groups).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the place, date and size of Thamud, and the identification of the Companions of al-Hijr with them; none is used.

claims.statement_en: God sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, and the ayat call Shu'ayb their brother.
Shu'ayb told them to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and that a clear proof had come to them from their Lord.
Shu'ayb told them to give full measure and weight, not to diminish people's things, and not to spread corruption in the land after it had been set right.
Shu'ayb told them that this was better for them if they were believers.
Shu'ayb told them that he saw them in good, and that he feared for them the punishment of an encompassing day.
Shu'ayb told them to give full measure and weight with justice and not to spread corruption in the land.
Shu'ayb told them that what God leaves is better for them if they were believers, and that he was not a guardian over them.
Shu'ayb told them not to sit on every path making threats, turning away from the way of God those who believed in Him and seeking to make it crooked.
Shu'ayb told them to remember that they had been few and that God had made them many, and to look at the end of those who spread corruption.
Shu'ayb told them that if a group of them believed in what he was sent with and a group did not, they should be patient until God judged between them, and that He is the best of judges.
Shu'ayb told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and turn back to Him, for his Lord is merciful and loving.
Shu'ayb told them that he wanted only to put things right as far as he was able, and that his success was only with God, in whom he trusted and to whom he turned.

Shu'ayb told them not to let their opposition to him bring on them the like of what struck the people of Nuh, the people of Hud or the people of Salih, and that the people of Lut were not far from them.
Shu'ayb told them to hope for the Last Day and not to spread corruption in the land.

chapters.summary_md: God sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, who told them to worship God alone and to give full measure and weight [c1][c2][c3]. He warned them of an encompassing day and told them to ask forgiveness and turn back to God [c5][c11].
chapters.body_md: God sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, and the ayat call Shu'ayb their brother [c1]. Shu'ayb told them to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and that a clear proof had come to them from their Lord [c2]. Shu'ayb told them to give full measure and weight, not to diminish people's things, and not to spread corruption in the land after it had been set right [c3]. Shu'ayb told them that this was better for them if they were believers [c4]. Shu'ayb told them that he saw them in good, and that he feared for them the punishment of an encompassing day [c5]. Shu'ayb told them to give full measure and weight with justice and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. Shu'ayb told them that what God leaves is better for them if they were believers, and that he was not a guardian over them [c7]. Shu'ayb told them not to sit on every path making threats, turning away from the way of God those who believed in Him and seeking to make it crooked [c8]. Shu'ayb told them to remember that they had been few and that God had made them many, and to look at the end of those who spread corruption [c9]. Shu'ayb told them that if a group of them believed in what he was sent with and a group did not, they should be patient until God judged between them, and that He is the best of judges [c10]. Shu'ayb told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and turn back to Him, for his Lord is merciful and loving [c11]. Shu'ayb told them that he wanted only to put things right as far as he was able, and that his success was only with God, in whom he trusted and to whom he turned [c12]. Shu'ayb told them not to let their opposition to him bring on them the like of what struck the people of Nuh, the people of Hud or the people of Salih, and that the people of Lut were not far from them [c13]. Shu'ayb told them to hope for the Last Day and not to spread corruption in the land [c14].
chapters.deep_md:
- God sent Shu'ayb to Madyan, and the ayat call Shu'ayb their brother (7:85, 11:84, 29:36) [c1].

- Shu'ayb told them to hope for the Last Day and not to spread corruption in the land (29:36) [c14].
chapters.kids_md: God sent Shu'ayb to the people of Madyan [c1]. Shu'ayb told them to worship God alone [c2]. He told them to give full measure and weight, and not to take away from people what belonged to them [c3]. He told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord [c11].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The call joins worship of God with honesty in measure and weight [c2][c3]. One reading is that the passage treats fair dealing between people as part of the same message as belief [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where Madyan was, when these things happened, or how many people Madyan numbered; the draft names no place.
- Not established: the exact meaning of the phrase read here as what God leaves in 11:86 is read in more than one way.
- Not established: the draft does not say what the paths of 7:86 were; the ayah does not describe them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the region of Madyan and any dates; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: The chiefs of his people who were arrogant told Shu'ayb that they would drive him and those who believed with him out of their town unless they returned to their religion.
Shu'ayb asked whether they would make them return even if they were unwilling.
Shu'ayb said that they would be inventing a lie against God if they returned to the religion of the chiefs after God had saved them from it.
Shu'ayb said that it was not for them to return to it unless God, their Lord, willed, that his Lord's knowledge encompassed everything, and that they put their trust in God.
Shu'ayb asked his Lord to judge between them and their people with truth, saying that He is the best of those who judge.
The chiefs who disbelieved told their people that if they followed Shu'ayb they would be losers.
They asked Shu'ayb whether his prayer told him that they should leave what their fathers worshipped or stop doing what they wished with their wealth, and called him the forbearing, the right-minded.
They told Shu'ayb that they did not understand much of what he said, that they saw him weak among them, and that but for his clan they would have stoned him.
Shu'ayb asked whether his clan was mightier with them than God, and said that they had cast Him behind their backs.
Shu'ayb told them that his Lord encompassed what they did.
Shu'ayb told them to act on their position, as he was acting, and that they would soon know who would receive a punishment that disgraces him and who was a liar.
Shu'ayb told them to watch, because he was watching with them.

chapters.summary_md: The arrogant chiefs of his people told Shu'ayb that they would drive him and the believers out unless they returned to their religion [c1]. Shu'ayb answered that it was not for them to return unless God willed, and that they put their trust in God [c3][c4].

Shu'ayb said that they would be inventing a lie against God if they returned to the religion of the chiefs after God had saved them from it [c3]. Shu'ayb told them to watch, because he was watching with them [c12].
chapters.deep_md:
- The chiefs of his people who were arrogant told Shu'ayb that they would drive him and those who believed with him out of their town unless they returned to their religion (7:88) [c1].
- Shu'ayb asked whether they would make them return even if they were unwilling (7:88) [c2].

- Shu'ayb said that it was not for them to return to it unless God, their Lord, willed, that his Lord's knowledge encompassed everything, and that they put their trust in God (7:89) [c4].
- Shu'ayb asked his Lord to judge between them and their people with truth, saying that He is the best of those who judge (7:89) [c5].
- The chiefs who disbelieved told their people that if they followed Shu'ayb they would be losers (7:90) [c6].

- Shu'ayb told them that his Lord encompassed what they did (11:92) [c10].

chapters.kids_md: The chiefs of the people told Shu'ayb that he and the believers must leave the town [c1]. Shu'ayb said they trusted God [c4]. He asked his Lord to judge between them with truth [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat show a threat of exile answered with trust and a request for God's judgement [c1][c4][c5]. One reading is that Shu'ayb ties his staying firm to what God wills, not to his own strength [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the chiefs were, how many believed with Shu'ayb, or whether the exile was carried out.
- Not established: the draft does not say what the clan of 11:91 was; the ayah does not describe it.
- Not established: whether the words forbearing and right-minded in 11:87 were meant seriously or mockingly; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: the speaker of the question even if they were unwilling is Shu'ayb in the draft's reading of 7:88; the ayah's grammar could be read as a question from either side.

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that a tremor seized them and they lay fallen in their home.
Another ayah says that when the command of God came, He saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Him.
The same ayah says that the cry seized the wrongdoers and they lay fallen in their homes.
It was as if they had never lived there, and the passage says away with Madyan, as Thamud was removed.
Those who denied Shu'ayb were as if they had never lived there, and the Quran calls them the losers.
Shu'ayb turned away from them and said that he had conveyed the messages of his Lord and advised them, and asked how he could grieve for a disbelieving people.

chapters.summary_md: A tremor and a cry seized the people of Madyan in their homes, and God saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him [c1][c2][c3]. The Quran calls those who denied Shu'ayb the losers [c5].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that a tremor seized them and they lay fallen in their home [c1]. Another ayah says that when the command of God came, He saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Him [c2]. The same ayah says that the cry seized the wrongdoers and they lay fallen in their homes [c3]. It was as if they had never lived there, and the passage says away with Madyan, as Thamud was removed [c4]. Those who denied Shu'ayb were as if they had never lived there, and the Quran calls them the losers [c5]. Shu'ayb turned away from them and said that he had conveyed the messages of his Lord and advised them, and asked how he could grieve for a disbelieving people [c6].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran says that a tremor seized them and they lay fallen in their home (7:91, 29:37) [c1].
- Another ayah says that when the command of God came, He saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Him (11:94) [c2].
- The same ayah says that the cry seized the wrongdoers and they lay fallen in their homes (11:94) [c3].
- It was as if they had never lived there, and the passage says away with Madyan, as Thamud was removed (11:95) [c4].
- Those who denied Shu'ayb were as if they had never lived there, and the Quran calls them the losers (7:92) [c5].
- Shu'ayb turned away from them and said that he had conveyed the messages of his Lord and advised them, and asked how he could grieve for a disbelieving people (7:93) [c6].
chapters.kids_md: God saved Shu'ayb and the people who believed with him [c2]. The people who would not believe were seized in their homes [c1][c3]. Shu'ayb said he had given them his Lord's message [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat set the safety of the believers beside the loss of those who denied Shu'ayb [c2][c5]. One reading is that Shu'ayb's last words are of a messenger who has delivered the message and turns away [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the ayat word what seized them as a tremor (7:91, 29:37) and as a cry (11:94); the draft does not decide whether these are one event.
- Not established: how long after the warning it happened, or how many were saved.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any account of the place of Madyan or of the manner of its end; none is used.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Shu'ayb and Madyan. None is used in this draft.
Inventory refs not used as chapters: none beyond the ayat cited; 29:36-37 is cited in the first and last chapters.

Wording a scholar should check first: 11:86 (what God leaves), 7:88 (the speaker of the question), 11:87 (the tone of forbearing and right-minded), 11:89 (the list of earlier peoples), 11:91 (weak, clan), 7:91 versus 11:94 (tremor and cry).

Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the people of Madyan with the Companions of the Thicket, or the separation of them; the ayat of Madyan do not mention the Thicket.

chapters.title_en: The call to the Companions of the Thicket

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.
Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God.
Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him.
Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds.
Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance.
Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land.
Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations.

chapters.summary_md: The Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers, and Shu'ayb called them to fear God and to obey him [c1][c2][c3]. He told them to give full measure, to weigh with the straight balance and not to spread corruption [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers [c1]. Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God [c2]. Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him [c3]. Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds [c4]. Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance [c5]. Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations [c7].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers (26:176) [c1].
- Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God (26:177) [c2].
- Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him (26:178-179) [c3].
- Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds (26:180) [c4].
- Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance (26:181-182) [c5].
- Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land (26:183) [c6].
- Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations (26:184) [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Shu'ayb spoke to the Companions of the Thicket [c2]. He told them to fear God [c3]. He told them to give full measure and not to take away from people what belonged to them [c5][c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The call joins fear of God with fairness in measure and weight [c3][c5]. One reading is that honest dealing appears here as part of what the messenger asks, together with a refusal of any wage [c4][c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the ayat of 26:177 name Shu'ayb but do not call him their brother, unlike other ayat that call a messenger their brother; the draft does not say whether this people is the same as another people.
- Not established: what the Thicket was, where it was, or how many Companions there were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the Thicket with a place, and any link to Madyan; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars.
They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful.
Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did.
They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them.
The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day.
The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.
Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them.
A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions.

chapters.summary_md: The Companions of the Thicket called Shu'ayb a liar and told him to make a piece of the sky fall on them [c1][c2]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them [c4].
chapters.body_md: They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars [c1]. They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful [c2]. Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did [c3]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them [c4]. The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day [c5]. The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers [c6]. Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them [c7]. A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions [c8].
chapters.deep_md:
- They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars (26:177, 26:185-186) [c1].
- They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful (26:187) [c2].
- Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did (26:188) [c3].
- They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them (26:189) [c4].
- The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day (26:189) [c5].
- The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers (26:190) [c6].
- Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them (15:78-79) [c7].
- A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions (38:13) [c8].
chapters.kids_md: The Companions of the Thicket did not believe Shu'ayb [c1]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow came [c4]. The Quran says that this is a sign [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat set a challenge to bring down the sky beside Shu'ayb's reply that his Lord knows best [c2][c3]. One reading is that the reply leaves the judgement with God [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the day of the shadow was, or what is meant by the shadow; the ayah gives only the name.
- Not established: 15:79 ends with a dual pronoun whose referents are not named in the ayah; the draft does not use that part.
- Not established: whether the factions of 38:13 are the same peoples as the Companions of the Thicket; the draft states only that the list names them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any link between the Companions of the Thicket and Madyan, and any date for the event.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Shu'ayb and the Companions of the Thicket. None is used in this draft.
Inventory refs: 50:14 (shared with the people of Tubba' and others) is not drafted here; it is used in the draft of Tubba'.
Wording a scholar should check first: 26:177 (named without the word brother), 26:185 (bewitched), 26:189 (the day of the shadow), 15:79 (the dual pronoun), 38:13 (factions).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the claim that the Companions of the Thicket and the people of Madyan are one people sent the same messenger; the draft keeps them apart.

claims.statement_en: God sent Lut to his people, and the ayat call Lut their brother; the Quran says they denied the messengers.
Lut told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him.
Lut told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds.
Lut asked them whether they committed the lewd act that no one in the worlds had done before them.
Lut said that they approached men with desire instead of women, and that they were a people who went beyond bounds.
Another passage has Lut ask whether they committed the lewd act while they saw, and say that they were a people who acted in ignorance.
Lut asked them whether they approached men, cut the road and committed the wrong in their gathering place.

chapters.summary_md: God sent Lut to his people, who called them to fear God and obey him [c1][c2]. Lut warned them about a deed that, he said, no one in the worlds had done before them [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md: God sent Lut to his people, and the ayat call Lut their brother; the Quran says they denied the messengers [c1]. Lut told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him [c2]. Lut told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds [c3]. Lut asked them whether they committed the lewd act that no one in the worlds had done before them [c4]. Lut said that they approached men with desire instead of women, and that they were a people who went beyond bounds [c5]. Another passage has Lut ask whether they committed the lewd act while they saw, and say that they were a people who acted in ignorance [c6]. Lut asked them whether they approached men, cut the road and committed the wrong in their gathering place [c7].
chapters.deep_md:
- God sent Lut to his people, and the ayat call Lut their brother; the Quran says they denied the messengers (26:160-161) [c1].
- Lut told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him (26:162-163) [c2].
- Lut told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds (26:164) [c3].
- Lut asked them whether they committed the lewd act that no one in the worlds had done before them (7:80, 29:28) [c4].
- Lut said that they approached men with desire instead of women, and that they were a people who went beyond bounds (7:81, 26:165-166) [c5].
- Another passage has Lut ask whether they committed the lewd act while they saw, and say that they were a people who acted in ignorance (27:54-55) [c6].
- Lut asked them whether they approached men, cut the road and committed the wrong in their gathering place (29:29) [c7].
chapters.kids_md: God sent Lut to his people [c1]. Lut told them to fear God [c2]. He told them that he asked no wage for it [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Lut's message begins with a call to fear God and a refusal of any wage before it names what he objects to [c2][c3][c4]. One reading is that the message is given as a messenger's duty and not as a personal gain [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where Lut's people lived, how many they were, or how long Lut spoke to them; the draft names no place.
- Not established: the draft says no more about the acts than the ayat say; it does not extend them.
- Not established: whether cutting the road in 29:29 describes a separate act, and what the gathering place was.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the towns of Lut's people and their location; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: Their only answer was to say: drive Lut's household out of your town, for they are people who keep themselves pure.
They told Lut that if he did not stop he would be among those driven out.
Lut said that he was one who hated what they did.
Lut asked his Lord to save him and his family from what they did.
Their answer was also to tell Lut to bring them the punishment of God if he was truthful, and Lut asked his Lord to help him against the people who spread corruption.
When Our messengers came to Lut, he was troubled for them, felt constrained and said that this was a hard day.
His people came rushing to him, and before that they had been doing evil deeds.
Lut told them to fear God and not to disgrace him in front of his guests, and asked whether there was no right-minded man among them.
In that passage Lut told them that his daughters were purer for them.
They told Lut that he knew they had no claim on his daughters and that he knew what they wanted.
Lut said that he wished he had strength against them or could take refuge in a strong support.
In another passage Lut told the messengers that they were a people he did not know, and the messengers said that they had come with what the people doubted and with the truth.
The people of the city came rejoicing, and Lut told them that these were his guests and that they should not shame him.
They answered by asking whether they had not forbidden him from receiving people of the worlds.
The ayah says that they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.

chapters.summary_md: Lut's people answered that Lut's household should be driven out [c1][c2]. Lut hated what they did and asked his Lord to save him and his family [c3][c4]. When the messengers came to him he was troubled, and he told his people to fear God and not to disgrace him in front of his guests [c6][c8].
chapters.body_md: Their only answer was to say: drive Lut's household out of your town, for they are people who keep themselves pure [c1]. They told Lut that if he did not stop he would be among those driven out [c2]. Lut said that he was one who hated what they did [c3]. Lut asked his Lord to save him and his family from what they did [c4]. Their answer was also to tell Lut to bring them the punishment of God if he was truthful, and Lut asked his Lord to help him against the people who spread corruption [c5]. When Our messengers came to Lut, he was troubled for them, felt constrained and said that this was a hard day [c6]. His people came rushing to him, and before that they had been doing evil deeds [c7]. Lut told them to fear God and not to disgrace him in front of his guests, and asked whether there was no right-minded man among them [c8]. In that passage Lut told them that his daughters were purer for them [c9]. They told Lut that he knew they had no claim on his daughters and that he knew what they wanted [c10]. Lut said that he wished he had strength against them or could take refuge in a strong support [c11]. In another passage Lut told the messengers that they were a people he did not know, and the messengers said that they had come with what the people doubted and with the truth [c12]. The people of the city came rejoicing, and Lut told them that these were his guests and that they should not shame him [c13]. claims.statement_en: The messengers told Lut that they were messengers of his Lord, who would never reach him, and told him to travel with his family in a part of the night.
They told him that none of them should look back except his wife, who would be struck by what struck the others, and that the appointed time was the morning.
God saved Lut and his family, except his wife, who was among those who stayed behind.
Another passage says that God saved him and his family all together, except an old woman among those who stayed behind.
When the command of God came, God made the town's upper part its lowest and rained on it stones of baked clay, layered one on another, marked with your Lord.
Another passage says that the cry seized them at sunrise, and that God made it upside down and rained on them stones of baked clay.
The Quran says that God rained a rain on them, and asks the hearer to see how the end of the criminals was.
The ayat say that God destroyed the others and rained a rain on them, and that the rain of those who were warned was evil.
Another passage says that God sent a stone-bearing wind against them, except the household of Lut whom He saved at dawn as a favour from Him.
That passage says that Lut had warned them of God's seizure, but they disputed the warnings, and that a lasting punishment came upon them early in the morning.
The messengers came to Ibrahim with good news and said that they were to destroy the people of that town because its people were wrongdoers.
Ibrahim said that Lut was in it, and they said that they knew best who was in it and would save him and his family, except his wife, who was among those who stayed behind.
When the messengers came to Lut, he was troubled for them, and they told him not to fear or grieve, as they would save him and his family except his wife.
They told Lut that they were to bring down on the people of that town a scourge from the sky because they had been disobedient.
The messengers said that they were sent to a criminal people to send down stones of clay marked with their Lord for the transgressors.
God brought out the believers who were there, and found there only a house of those who submitted.
The Quran says that God left a sign for those who fear the painful punishment, and a clear sign for people who use reason.
The Quran says that Lut was among the messengers, and that the hearers pass by them in the morning and at night, and asks whether they do not understand.
The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.

claims.statement_en: God sent Nuh to his people, and the ayat call Nuh their brother; the Quran says the people of Nuh denied the messengers.
Nuh told them to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him.
Nuh told them that he was a clear warner, and that he feared for them the punishment of a great day and of a painful day.
Nuh told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, that they should fear God and obey him, and that he asked them for no wage.
God told Nuh to warn his people before a painful punishment came to them.
Nuh told them to worship God, to fear Him and to obey him.
Nuh told them that He would forgive them some of their sins and give them time until a stated term, and that the term of God, when it comes, is not put back.

chapters.title_en: How the people of Nuh answered

claims.statement_en: The chiefs of his people told Nuh that they saw him in clear error, and Nuh answered that there was no error in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.
Nuh told them that he conveyed the messages of his Lord, advised them, and knew from God what they did not know.
The chiefs who disbelieved said that they saw in Nuh only a human like them, and that those who followed him were the lowest among them in their first judgement.
They said that they saw no merit in Nuh's followers over themselves, and that they thought them liars.
They said that he was only a human like them who wanted to raise himself above them, and that had God willed, He would have sent down angels.
They said that they had not heard of this among their fathers of old.
They said that he was only a man with madness, and told the others to wait on him for a time.
The Quran says that they denied God's servant, said he was mad, and that he was rebuffed.
They asked Nuh whether they should believe him when the lowest followed him.
Nuh said that he had no knowledge of what they had done, that their reckoning was only with his Lord, and that he would not drive away the believers.
Nuh said that he was only a clear warner.
Nuh asked them to consider that if he was on a clear proof from his Lord, who had given him mercy that was hidden from them, he could not force it on them while they disliked it.
Nuh said that he did not ask them for wealth, that his wage was only with God, and that he would not drive away those who believed, who would meet their Lord.
Nuh asked who would help him against God if he drove them away.
Nuh said that he did not claim to hold the treasuries of God, did not know the unseen, and did not claim to be an angel.
They told Nuh that he had disputed with them and had gone on disputing, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful.
Nuh answered that only God would bring it if He willed, and that they could not escape.
Nuh told them that his advice would not help them if God wished to lead them astray, since He was their Lord and they would return to Him.
They told Nuh that if he did not stop he would be among those stoned.

chapters.title_en: What Nuh said to his Lord about them

claims.statement_en: Nuh told his Lord that he had called his people night and day, and that his call only increased their flight.
Nuh said that whenever he called them for God to forgive them they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted and were very arrogant.
Nuh said that he then called them openly, and then spoke to them both publicly and in private.
Nuh told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord, who is ever forgiving, and that He would send abundant rain from the sky, supply them with wealth and sons, and give them gardens and rivers.
Nuh told his Lord that they had disobeyed him and followed one whose wealth and children only added to his loss, and that they had plotted a great plot.
They said not to leave their gods, and not to leave Wadd, Suwa, Yaghuth, Yauq and Nasr.
Nuh said that they had led many astray, and asked that the wrongdoers increase only in error.
Because of their wrongs they were drowned, then made to enter a fire, and found no helpers besides God.
Nuh asked his Lord not to leave on the earth any dwellers among the disbelievers, saying that if He left them they would lead His servants astray and beget only wicked, ungrateful children.
Nuh asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever entered his house as a believer, and the believing men and women.
Nuh called on his Lord that he was overcome, and asked for help.
Nuh said that his people had denied him, asked God to judge decisively between them and him, and to save him and the believers with him.
Nuh asked his Lord to help him because they had denied him.

- Nuh asked forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever entered his house as a believer, and the believing men and women (71:28) [c10].
- Nuh called on his Lord that he was overcome, and asked for help (54:10) [c11].
- Nuh said that his people had denied him, asked God to judge decisively between them and him, and to save him and the believers with him (26:117-118) [c12].
- Nuh asked his Lord to help him because they had denied him (23:26) [c13].
chapters.kids_md: Nuh called his people night and day [c1]. They would not listen [c2]. Nuh asked God to judge between them and him and to save him and the believers [c12].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat record a messenger who called by night and day, openly and in private, and then turned to his Lord in prayer [c1][c3][c12]. One reading is that persistence in calling and prayer for judgement are placed side by side [c3][c12].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how long Nuh called them before these prayers, or in what order the prayers were said.
- Not established: the draft names the names of 71:23 as the ayah gives them; the ayah does not say what they were, and the draft says no more.
- Not established: the sense of the word fingers in their ears and of covering themselves with garments is the ayah's picture of refusal; the draft states it as worded.
- Not established: 71:13-20 (a passage about creation) is not used in this chapter.

claims.statement_en: God told Nuh that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed.
God told Nuh to build the ship by His revelation, and not to address Him about the wrongdoers, since they would be drowned.
Whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him, and he said that if they mocked, he would mock them as they mocked.
Nuh told them that they would know who would receive a punishment that disgraces him and on whom a lasting punishment would fall.
When the command of God came and the tannur boiled over, God said to carry in it two of every kind, and Nuh's family, except those against whom the word had gone before, and whoever believed.
The ayah says that none believed with him except a few.
Nuh said to ride in it, and that in the name of God was its course and its mooring.
It ran with them on waves like mountains, and Nuh called to his son, who was apart, to ride with them and not to be with the disbelievers.
The son said that he would take refuge on a mountain to protect him from the water, and Nuh answered that there was no protector that day from the command of God except those on whom He had mercy.
The wave came between them, and the son was among the drowned.
The earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to stop, the water subsided, the matter was decided, the ship settled on al-Judi, and the call went out: away with the wrongdoing people.
Another passage says that God opened the gates of the sky with pouring water, made springs burst from the earth, and the waters met for a matter already decreed.
God carried Nuh on a vessel of planks and dusur, a word read in more than one way, which ran as a recompense for the one who had been rejected.
God left it as a sign.
God told Nuh, when the ship was settled with those with him, to say praise be to God who saved them from the wrongdoing people.
God told Nuh to say, my Lord, let me land at a blessed landing, for You are the best of those who bring to land.
The Quran says that in this there are signs and that God was testing.
God saved Nuh and those with him in the laden ship and afterward drowned the rest.
Nuh stayed among his people a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
God saved him and the companions of the ship and made it a sign for the worlds.
The people of Nuh denied the messengers, and God drowned them and made them a sign for people and prepared a painful punishment for the wrongdoers.
They denied him, and God saved him and those with him in the ship and drowned those who denied His signs, a blind people.
The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.
