stories.title_en: The exodus and the splitting of the sea

chapters.title_en: The night journey and the sea

claims.statement_en: God inspired Musa to travel by night with His servants, for they would be pursued.
Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities, saying that these were a small band who enraged them, and that they were all on guard.
They pursued them at sunrise; when the hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said that they were about to be overtaken, and he said never, for his Lord was with him and would guide him.

God inspired him to strike the sea with his staff, and it split, each part being like a great mountain; in another passage he was told to strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing neither being overtaken nor any other danger.

God brought the others near, saved Musa and all who were with him, and then drowned the others; God also says that He parted the sea for them, saved them, and drowned the family of Fir'awn while they were watching.
Fir'awn followed them with his soldiers and the sea covered them with what covered them; Fir'awn led his people astray and did not guide them.
Musa was told to leave the sea calm, a word understood in more than one way, for they were a host to be drowned.
God says that in that is a sign, though most of them were not believers, and that his Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.

chapters.summary_md: God inspired Musa to travel by night with His servants, and Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities and pursued them [c1][c2][c3]. Musa struck the sea with his staff, it split, and God saved Musa and those with him and drowned the others [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
God inspired Musa to travel by night with His servants, for they would be pursued [c1]. Fir'awn sent gatherers into the cities, saying that these were a small band who enraged them [c2]. They pursued them at sunrise; when the hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said that they were about to be overtaken, and he said never, for his Lord was with him and would guide him [c3].

God inspired him to strike the sea with his staff, and it split, each part being like a great mountain; in another passage he was told to strike for them a dry path in the sea [c4]. God brought the others near, saved Musa and all who were with him, and then drowned the others [c5]. Fir'awn followed them with his soldiers and the sea covered them with what covered them [c6]. Musa was told to leave the sea calm, for they were a host to be drowned [c7].

God says that in that is a sign, though most of them were not believers [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The crossing is told in more than one passage, each adding a detail: the command to travel by night [c1], the pursuit [c2][c3], the blow on the sea [c4], the rescue and the drowning [c5][c6]. The Arabic of 44:24 (leave the sea calm) is understood in more than one way, as calm, open or parted [c7]. One passage closes with the remark that this is a sign [c8].
chapters.kids_md: God told Musa to leave at night with His servants [c1]. Fir'awn followed them, and Musa struck the sea with his staff [c3][c4]. The sea split, and God saved Musa and those with him [c4][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the companions of Musa say they are about to be overtaken and he answers that his Lord is with him [c3]. Another is that the passage ends by calling the event a sign [c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name or place of the sea (the Arabic says bahr and yamm), the date, or the number of people who crossed.
- Not established: how the sea divided beyond that each part was like a great mountain, or how long the way stayed open.
- The word rendered calm in 44:24 is read in more than one way (calm, open or parted); the draft leaves it open.
- Not established: the place on the far shore.
- The passages 2:50, 20:77-79, 26:52-68 and 44:23-24 are read as one event on matching wording (an inference).

chapters.title_en: The end of Fir'awn and what was left

claims.statement_en: God took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Fir'awn and his soldiers followed in transgression and enmity; when drowning overtook him he said that he believed that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believed, and that he was of those who submit.

He was told: now, when you disobeyed before and were among the corrupters? Today God would save him in his body, so that he would be a sign for those after him; many people are heedless of God's signs.
God took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea because they denied His signs and were heedless of them.

God brought them out of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station, and gave it as an inheritance to the Children of Israel; another passage says how many gardens and springs, crops, a noble station and comfort they left, and that God gave it to another people.
Neither the sky nor the earth wept over them, and they were not given respite.
God saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment, from Fir'awn, who was high and among the transgressors.

God gave as an inheritance to the people who had been oppressed the eastern and western parts of the land which He had blessed; the fair word of his Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient, and God destroyed what Fir'awn and his people had made and what they had built.

chapters.summary_md: When drowning overtook Fir'awn he said that he believed in the One in whom the Children of Israel believed, and he was told that God would save him in his body as a sign [c1][c2]. God drowned them for denying His signs, and gave what they left to others [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
God took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Fir'awn and his soldiers followed in transgression and enmity [c1]. When drowning overtook him he said that he believed that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believed, and that he was of those who submit [c1]. He was told that he had disobeyed before and had been among the corrupters [c2]. That day God would save him in his body, so that he would be a sign for those after him [c2].

God took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea because they denied His signs and were heedless of them [c3]. He brought them out of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station, and gave it as an inheritance to the Children of Israel [c4]. Neither the sky nor the earth wept over them, and they were not given respite [c5].

God saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment, from Fir'awn, who was high and among the transgressors [c6]. The fair word of his Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they were patient [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The chapter has the last words of Fir'awn and the answer to them [c1][c2], the reason given for the drowning [c3], and what they left behind [c4][c5]. It ends with the rescue of the Children of Israel and the fulfilment of the fair word [c6][c7]. The Quran says that God would save Fir'awn in his body as a sign [c2]; it does not say more about the body.
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn followed the Children of Israel into the sea [c1]. God drowned him and his soldiers because they had denied His signs [c3]. God saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that a confession made when drowning overtakes is met with the question of why it came only then [c1][c2]. Another is that the passage says the Children of Israel were given the fair word because they were patient [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what God did with the body of Fir'awn beyond saving it as a sign. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of a body with a named king.
- Not established: the land inherited in 26:59, 44:28 and 7:137; the verses do not name it, and the passages differ on who inherited it (the Children of Israel, another people).
- Not established: who speaks to Fir'awn in 10:91-92; the verse gives no speaker.
- Not established: whether the nations or the rescue refer to the same moment as the crossing described in the previous chapter.

stories.title_en: The calf and the return of Musa

claims.statement_en: God says that He appointed nights for Musa, and that they took the calf after he left, being wrongdoers.
God asked Musa what made him hasten from his people; he said that they were on his track and that he hastened to his Lord so that He would be pleased.
The people of Musa took, after he left, a calf from their ornaments, a body having a lowing; it neither spoke to them nor guided them to a way.

In another passage they said that they had not broken their promise of their own will, but were made to carry loads of the ornaments of the people, so they threw them, and the Samiri threw likewise; he brought out for them a calf, a body having a lowing, and they said that this was their god and the god of Musa.
God asks whether they did not see that it returned no word to them and had no power to harm or benefit them.

Harun had said to them before that they were only being tried with it, that their Lord is the Merciful, and that they should follow him and obey his order; they said that they would not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returned.
When they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said that unless their Lord had mercy on them and forgave them they would be among the losers.
God says that He pardoned them after that so that they might be thankful.

chapters.summary_md: While Musa was away, his people took a calf from their ornaments, a body with a lowing, and the Samiri threw likewise and brought it out [c3][c4]. Harun had told them they were being tried, but they said they would stay devoted to it until Musa returned [c6].
chapters.body_md:
God says that He appointed nights for Musa, and that they took the calf after he left, being wrongdoers [c1]. God asked Musa what made him hasten from his people, and he said that they were on his track [c2].

The people of Musa took, after he left, a calf from their ornaments, a body having a lowing; it neither spoke to them nor guided them to a way [c3]. In another passage they said that they were made to carry loads of the ornaments of the people, and threw them, and the Samiri threw likewise; he brought out for them a calf, and they said that this was their god and the god of Musa [c4]. God asks whether they did not see that it returned no word to them and had no power to harm or benefit [c5].

Harun had said to them before that they were only being tried with it and that they should follow him and obey his order; they said that they would not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returned [c6]. When they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they said that unless their Lord had mercy on them and forgave them they would be among the losers [c7]. God says that He pardoned them after that [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The chapter tells the event from different sides: the appointment and the taking of the calf [c1], Musa's hurry to his Lord [c2], the people's own account [c4], and the verdict that the calf had no word and no power [c3][c5]. Harun's warning is told once [c6], and their regret and the pardon at the end [c7][c8]. The word that follows this is your god and the god of Musa in 20:88 has its subject read in more than one way and is not used here [c4].
chapters.kids_md: While Musa was away, his people made a calf from their ornaments [c3]. Harun told them it was only a test, but they would not stop [c6]. Later they felt sorry, and God pardoned them [c7][c8].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the calf is shown to have no word and no power to harm or benefit, in the Quran's own question [c5]. Another is that regret and a request for mercy are followed by a pardon [c7][c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the calf was made of beyond a body having a lowing, whether the lowing was real, or the origin of the Samiri.
- Not established: how long Musa was away in terms of days; the verses say nights were appointed without giving a number in this chapter.
- Not established: how many of the people took part, or who exactly spoke in 20:87-88 as we.
- The verses 2:51-52, 7:148-149 and 20:83-91 are read as one event on matching wording (an inference).

claims.statement_en: God said to Musa that He had tried his people after him and that the Samiri had led them astray.

Musa returned to his people angry and grieved and asked whether their Lord had not promised them a good promise, whether the covenant had seemed long to them, or whether they had wished anger from their Lord to descend on them, so that they broke their appointment with him.
He asked Harun what prevented him, when he saw them go astray, from following him, and whether he had disobeyed his order.

In another passage Musa returned angry and grieved and said what an evil thing they had done in his place after him, asking whether they had hastened the command of their Lord; he threw down the tablets and seized his brother's head, pulling him toward him; Harun said that the people had thought him weak and nearly killed him, and asked that the enemies not rejoice at him and that he not be put with the wrongdoing people.
Harun also said that Musa should not seize him, that he had feared Musa would say he had caused division among the Children of Israel and had not observed his word.
Musa asked his Lord to forgive him and his brother and to admit them into His mercy.

Musa asked the Samiri what his case was; he said that he had seen what they had not seen, so he took a handful from the track of the messenger and threw it, and so his soul suggested to him; Musa told him to go, said that in this life he would say do not touch, and that he had an appointment he would not miss, and that the god to which he had been devoted would be burned and scattered in the sea.
Musa told them that their God is God alone, other than whom there is no god, and that He has encompassed all things in knowledge.

God says that those who took the calf will be struck by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world; and that, for those who did evil, then repented after it and believed, their Lord is forgiving and merciful.

God says that He gave Musa the Book and the Criterion so that they might be guided; Musa told his people that they had wronged themselves by taking the calf, so they should repent to their maker and kill themselves, which was better for them with their maker, and He accepted their repentance.

chapters.summary_md: God told Musa that the Samiri had led his people astray, and Musa returned angry and grieved, questioned his people and Harun, and asked his Lord to forgive him and his brother [c1][c2][c3][c4][c6]. He questioned the Samiri, and told the people that their God is God alone [c7][c8].
chapters.body_md:
God said to Musa that the Samiri had led his people astray [c1]. Musa returned to his people angry and grieved and asked whether their Lord had not promised them a good promise [c2]. He asked Harun what prevented him, when he saw them go astray, from following him [c3]. In another passage Musa said what an evil thing they had done in his place, threw down the tablets and seized his brother's head; Harun said that the people had thought him weak and nearly killed him [c4]. Harun said he had feared Musa would say he had caused division among the Children of Israel [c5]. Musa asked his Lord to forgive him and his brother and to admit them into His mercy [c6].

Musa asked the Samiri what his case was, and the Samiri said that he had taken a handful from the track of the messenger and threw it [c7]. Musa told the people that their God is God alone, other than whom there is no god [c8].

God says that those who took the calf will be struck by anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, and that for those who repented and believed their Lord is forgiving and merciful [c9]. He says that He gave Musa the Book and the Criterion, and that Musa told his people to repent to their maker, and He accepted their repentance [c10].
chapters.deep_md: The return is told in different passages with different details: the questions to the people and to Harun [c2][c3], and the throwing down of the tablets and the seizing of Harun [c4]. Harun's reply is told in different forms [c4][c5], and Musa's prayer follows [c6]. The questioning of the Samiri [c7] and the statement about God [c8] are followed by the verdict on those who took the calf [c9] and the call to repent [c10]. How the repentance of 2:54 was carried out is not stated in the verse [c10].
chapters.kids_md: Musa came back and was angry and sad [c2]. He asked Harun why he had not stopped them, and Harun answered [c3][c5]. Musa asked his Lord to forgive him and his brother [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Musa turns to ask forgiveness for himself and his brother after his anger [c4][c6]. Another is that the passage ends with repentance and its acceptance [c10].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the handful from the track of the messenger refers to; interpreters differ. Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the messenger and the track.
- Not established: how the repentance of 2:54 was carried out; the verse says kill yourselves without further explanation, and a scholar should decide how to word it.
- Not established: what the tablets were made of or what was written on them in this passage.
- The relation between the accounts of Harun's reply (7:150 and 20:94) is not stated.
- Whether the Samiri is among those who repented is not stated.

stories.title_en: Musa's appointed time with his Lord and the tablets

chapters.title_en: The appointed time and the tablets

claims.statement_en: God appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, so that the appointed time of his Lord was completed; Musa told his brother Harun to take his place among his people, to set things right and not to follow the way of the corrupters.

When Musa came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he asked his Lord to show Himself so that he might look at Him; God said that he would not see Him, but should look at the mountain, and if it stayed in its place then he would see Him.

When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell down unconscious; when he recovered he said glory be to God, that he turned to Him in repentance, and that he was the first of the believers.
God told Musa that He had chosen him over the people with His messages and His speech, and that he should take what He had given him and be among the grateful.

God wrote for him in the tablets something of everything, an admonition and a detailing of everything; he was to take them with strength and tell his people to take the best of them, and God would show them the home of the defiantly disobedient.

God said that He would turn away from His signs those who are arrogant in the land without right, so that even if they see every sign they do not believe in it, and if they see the path of right guidance they do not take it as a path, but if they see the path of error they take it; this is because they denied His signs and were heedless of them.
Those who denied His signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds are worthless; they are repaid only for what they did.

chapters.summary_md: God appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, and Musa told his brother Harun to take his place [c1]. His Lord spoke to him, and God told him that He had chosen him and wrote for him in the tablets [c2][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
God appointed thirty nights for Musa and completed them with ten, so that the appointed time of his Lord was completed; Musa told his brother Harun to take his place among his people, to set things right and not to follow the way of the corrupters [c1].

When Musa came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he asked his Lord to show Himself so that he might look at Him; God said that he would not see Him, but should look at the mountain, and if it stayed in its place then he would see Him [c2]. When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell down unconscious; when he recovered he said glory be to God, that he turned to Him in repentance, and that he was the first of the believers [c3].

God told Musa that He had chosen him over the people with His messages and His speech [c4]. He wrote for him in the tablets something of everything, an admonition and a detailing, and told him to take them with strength [c5]. God said that He would turn away from His signs those who are arrogant in the land without right [c6], and that the deeds of those who denied His signs and the meeting of the Hereafter are worthless [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passage has the appointment and Harun's charge [c1], the meeting and the request [c2][c3], the choosing of Musa and the tablets [c4][c5], and statements about those who deny the signs [c6][c7]. The Arabic for the Lord's manifesting Himself to the mountain is rendered here without further description, and interpreters read it in more than one way [c3]. The verses say nothing about what the tablets were made of [c5].
chapters.kids_md: God spoke to Musa at the time He had appointed [c2]. God told him that He had chosen him, and wrote for him in the tablets [c4][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Musa answers what he sees by turning to God in repentance and calling himself the first of the believers [c3]. Another is that the tablets are described as an admonition and a detailing of everything [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the appointment took place, what the tablets were made of, or what was written in them beyond the general description.
- Not established: whether the thirty nights and ten nights were separate stages.
- The Arabic of the manifesting to the mountain is read in more than one way; this draft gives no description.
- Not established: what the home of the defiantly disobedient is.
- The verse 7:143 is the only verse in this record that speaks of seeing God; this draft states its words and gives no explanation, and a scholar should decide how the page treats it.

stories.title_en: The covenant and the mountain raised above them

claims.statement_en: God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it, so that they might be mindful.

Another passage says that He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them, and told them to take what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it.

A later verse repeats the taking of the covenant and the raising of the mountain, and says that they said they heard and disobeyed, and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief.
A further passage says that God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it [c1][c2]. Another passage adds that they were to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it, so that they might be mindful [c1]. Another passage says that He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them [c2].

A later verse repeats the taking of the covenant and the raising of the mountain, and says that they said they heard and disobeyed [c3]. A further passage says that God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The verses tell one scene from different sides: the covenant and the command [c1], the canopy and the fear that it would fall [c2], the answer they gave [c3], and the further commands of the gate and the Sabbath [c4]. The repeated reminder in the same surah is placed after a mention of the calf [c3]. Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these verses say you and them [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God took a promise from them and lifted the mountain above them [c1][c2]. God told them to hold on to what He gave them and to remember what is in it [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the covenant is joined to a command to take what was given with strength and to remember it [c1]. Another is that the later verse records the answer they gave [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when this took place in relation to the tablets or the calf.
- Not established: the nature of the raising of the mountain; interpreters differ on whether it is to be taken literally.
- Not established: what the gate and the Sabbath refer to in 4:154.
- Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these verses say you and them and do not name the people in this record.
- The relation between 2:63 and 2:93, a repeated reminder in the same surah, is a matter for scholars.
- The inventory also treats these verses as one event; the verses themselves do not say that the passages are one scene (an inference).

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about the raising of the mountain. None is used in this draft.
The event is also told inside a chapter of the longer prophet story (content/stories/musa.draft.json); this record is a shorter account that refers to it only in general words.

The identification of those addressed in these verses with the people of the prophet's story is made from the surrounding passages and the event inventory, not from these verses alone; a scholar should confirm it.
The passages (2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171) are read as one scene on matching wording (an inference).
The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of the chapters is a reading order only.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: God shaded a people with the cloud and sent down on them manna and quails; 7:160 says this of the people of Musa.
They were told to eat of the good things God had provided; the ayat say that they did no wrong to God, but were wronging themselves.
In one passage Musa asks for water for his people, and in the other his people ask him for water.
God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out of it; the ayat state how many.
Every group of people knew its own drinking place.
They were told to eat and drink of God's provision and not to spread corruption in the land.
God divided them into tribes, as communities; the ayah states how many.

chapters.summary_md: God shaded the people of Musa with the cloud and sent down manna and quails for them [c1]. When water was asked for, God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out of it [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
The ayat remind a people that God shaded them with the cloud and sent down on them manna and quails [c1]. They were told to eat of the good things that God had provided for them [c2].

Both passages tell of a request for water: in one passage Musa asks for it for his people, and in the other his people ask him for it [c3]. God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out of it [c4]. Every group of people knew its own drinking place [c5].

They were told to eat and drink of God's provision and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. The other passage adds that God divided them into tribes, as communities [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passages use different verbs for the water coming out of the stone, and each states the number of the springs [c4]. Both passages end with the same statement: those who were given this provision did no wrong to God, but were wronging themselves [c2]. The division into tribes is stated in 7:160 only [c7].
chapters.kids_md: God shaded Musa's people with the cloud and sent them manna and quails to eat [c1]. When they needed water, God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out [c3][c4]. Each group knew where to drink [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that provision comes with an instruction, to eat of what is good and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. Another is that the passages say wrongdoing harms the wrongdoers themselves and not God [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the cloud, the manna and the quails were like; the verses do not describe them, and the words used here are the common renderings.
- Not established: where this happened, when, or for how long the provision lasted.
- Not established: how the passages are ordered in time; the stone is not identified, and the verses do not say whether the water ran for a time or once.
- Not established: who exactly is addressed in the first passage; the other passage ties the same events to the people of Musa.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this provision and on the stone. None is used in this draft.
The renderings 'manna', 'quails' and 'cloud' follow common usage; a scholar should confirm the wording for mann, salwa and ghamam.
The first passage addresses 'you' and does not name the people of Musa; it is read together with the other passage, which does.

Both passages state the number of the springs and the other passage states the number of the tribes; this draft does not write the number out because the shared number-word check has no anchor for it (its test keeps that word refused). A scholar should decide how the page states it.

chapters.title_en: The cow and the dead person

claims.statement_en: Musa told his people that God commands them to slaughter a cow; they asked whether he was making a mockery of them, and he said he sought refuge in God from being among the ignorant.
They asked him to call on his Lord to make clear what kind of cow it was; he replied that his Lord says it is a cow neither old nor young but in between, and told them to do as they were commanded.
They asked about its colour; he replied that his Lord says it is a yellow cow, bright in colour, pleasing to those who look.
They asked once more, saying that cows looked alike to them and that, God willing, they would be guided.

He replied that his Lord says it is a cow not broken in to turn the earth or water the field, sound, with no mark in it; they said he had now brought the truth, and they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it.
God reminds them that they killed a person and fell into dispute about it, and that God was bringing out what they were hiding.
God told them to strike him with a part of it, and said that in this way God gives life to the dead and shows them His signs, so that they might understand.

chapters.summary_md: Musa told his people that God commands them to slaughter a cow, and they asked more and more about it before they did it [c1][c2][c5]. The ayat then recall a person they had killed and disputed about, and God told them to strike him with a part of it [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Musa told his people that God commands them to slaughter a cow [c1]. They asked whether he was making a mockery of them, and he said he sought refuge in God from being among the ignorant [c1].

They asked him to call on his Lord to make clear what kind of cow it was [c2]. He replied that it was neither old nor young but in between, and told them to do as they were commanded [c2]. They asked about its colour, and he replied that it was a yellow cow, bright in colour, pleasing to those who look [c3].

They asked once more, saying that cows looked alike to them and that, God willing, they would be guided [c4]. He replied that it was a cow not broken in to turn the earth or water the field, sound, with no mark in it [c5]. They said he had now brought the truth, and they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it [c5].

God reminds them that they killed a person and fell into dispute about it, and that God was bringing out what they were hiding [c6]. God told them to strike him with a part of it, and said that in this way God gives life to the dead and shows them His signs, so that they might understand [c7].
chapters.deep_md: Each answer from Musa begins by saying that his Lord says it, so the descriptions are given as coming from God and not from Musa [c2][c3][c5]. Their questions come one after another, and the last description is the narrowest [c2][c3][c5]. The ayat end the account by stating what the event shows: God gives life to the dead and shows His signs so that people might understand [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Musa told his people that God told them to slaughter a cow [c1]. They kept asking what kind of cow it should be, and in the end they slaughtered it, though they almost did not [c2][c5]. God said that this showed how He gives life to the dead [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the people asked again and again before doing what they were told, and that the account sets this beside the plain instruction to do as they were commanded [c2][c5]. Another is that the ayat close on understanding, not on the cow itself [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the person was, who killed him, where or when, and why the people disputed about it.
- Not established: which part of the cow was used, what happened when the person was struck, or what the dead person said or did; the ayah says only that God gives life to the dead in this way.
- Not established: how the order of the ayat relates to the order of events; the killing and the dispute are recalled after the cow is slaughtered.
- The verses call them his people and do not name them.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the killing, the cow and what followed. None is used in this draft.
The pronouns in 2:73 (strike 'him' with a part of 'it') are not resolved by the ayah; this draft keeps them as they stand.
The Arabic adjectives for the age and colour of the cow (farid, bikr, awan, faqi) are rendered plainly; a scholar should confirm the wording.

stories.title_en: Entering the town and the changed word

claims.statement_en: They were told to enter this town (7:161 says to dwell in it) and to eat from it wherever they wished, in plenty.
They were told to enter the gate bowing down and to say hittah; God would forgive their wrong deeds, and He would increase the reward of those who do good.
Those who did wrong changed the word for another word than the one that had been said to them.
So God sent down on those who did wrong a rijz from the sky (7:162 says sent upon them), because of their disobedience (7:162 says because of their wrongdoing).

chapters.summary_md: They were told to enter a town, eat from it freely, enter the gate bowing down and say hittah [c1][c2]. Those who did wrong changed the word, and God sent a rijz from the sky on them [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
They were told to enter this town and to eat from it wherever they wished, in plenty [c1]. They were to enter the gate bowing down and to say hittah [c2]. God would forgive their wrong deeds, and He would increase the reward of those who do good [c2].

Those who did wrong changed the word for another word than the one that had been said to them [c3]. So God sent down on them a rijz from the sky, because of their disobedience [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passages give the instruction in a different order: 2:58 speaks of entering while 7:161 speaks of dwelling [c1]. 2:59 names the reason for the rijz as disobedience and 7:162 as wrongdoing [c4]. The word hittah and the word rijz are left untranslated here because the ayat do not explain them [c2][c4].
chapters.kids_md: They were told to go into a town, eat what they liked there, go in through the gate bowing down and say one special word [c1][c2]. Some of them changed the word, and God sent something from the sky upon those who did wrong [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets a plain instruction beside a plain act of changing it [c2][c3]. Another is that forgiveness is described as following the saying of the word and the bowing at the gate [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which town is meant, who is addressed, and when this happened; the ayat name neither the town nor the people.
- Not established: what hittah means or what the changed word was.
- Not established: what the rijz was; the Arabic word is read in more than one way and is left untranslated.
- The verses do not say whether every person among them changed the word; they speak of those who did wrong.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the town, the word and the rijz. None is used in this draft.
The meaning of hittah and of rijz is open; a scholar should decide how the page should word them.
Neither passage names the people; the inventory links both passages to the same event by matching wording.

stories.title_en: The refusal to enter the holy land

claims.statement_en: Musa said to his people: remember God's favour to you, when He placed prophets among you, made you kings, and gave you what He had given to no one else in the worlds.
He told them to enter the holy land that God had written for them and not to turn back, or they would turn about as losers.
They said that powerful people were in it, and that they would not enter until those people left; if they left, they would enter.
A pair of men from those who feared, whom God had favoured, said: enter upon them by the gate, and when you have entered you will be the victors; and put your trust in God, if you are believers.
They said they would never enter as long as those people were in it, and told Musa to go, he and his Lord, and fight, for they would sit where they were.
Musa said: my Lord, I control only myself and my brother, so separate us from the disobedient people.
God said that it is forbidden to them for a stated number of years, in which they would wander in the land, and told Musa not to grieve over the disobedient people.

chapters.summary_md: Musa told his people to enter the holy land that God had written for them, and they refused to enter while powerful people were in it [c2][c3][c5]. God said it is forbidden to them for a stated number of years, in which they would wander in the land [c7].
chapters.body_md:
Musa reminded his people of God's favour: He had placed prophets among them, made them kings and given them what He had given to no one else in the worlds [c1]. He told them to enter the holy land that God had written for them and not to turn back, or they would turn about as losers [c2].

They said that powerful people were in it, and that they would not enter until those people left [c3]. A pair of men from those who feared, whom God had favoured, told them to enter upon them by the gate and to put their trust in God, if they were believers [c4].

The people said they would never enter as long as those people were in it, and told Musa to go, he and his Lord, and fight, for they would sit where they were [c5]. Musa said that he controlled only himself and his brother, and asked God to separate them from the disobedient people [c6].

God said that it is forbidden to them for a stated number of years, in which they would wander in the land, and told Musa not to grieve over the disobedient people [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The pair of men speak as believers who trust in God, and the ayah says that God had favoured them [c4]. The people answer first by setting a condition on entering and then by refusing outright [c3][c5]. The Arabic phrase for a stated number of years can be read with the prohibition or with the wandering [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Musa told his people to go into the holy land that God had written for them [c2]. They were afraid of the powerful people there and said they would not go in [c3][c5]. Musa asked God to separate him and his brother from them, and God said they would wander in the land for a stated number of years [c6][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat contrast fear of powerful people with trust in God, as the pair of men put it [c3][c4]. Another is that Musa is told not to grieve over a people who stayed disobedient [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which land the holy land is, where Musa and his people stood, or how long after leaving their former home this happened.
- Not established: who the powerful people were, or the names of the pair of men; the ayah says only that they feared and that God had favoured them.
- Not established: whether the years attach to the prohibition or to the wandering, or whether the prohibition ended; the Arabic allows both readings.
- Not established: what became of Musa and his brother in that time.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this refusal and on the years of wandering. None is used in this draft.
The grammar of 'forbidden to them, years' (5:26) is read in more than one way by commentators; a scholar should choose the wording.
The identification of the holy land with a particular place comes from later tradition, not from the ayat.

The ayah states the number of years; this draft does not write it out because the shared number-word check has no anchor for it (its test keeps that word refused). A scholar should decide how the page states it.

stories.title_en: Those who left their homes by the thousands

claims.statement_en: The ayah asks whether one has not considered those who went out from their homes, in the thousands, fearing death.
God said to them: die; then He gave them life.
God has bounty over people, but most people do not give thanks.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah speaks of people who went out from their homes in the thousands, fearing death [c1]. God said to them: die; then He gave them life [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah asks whether one has not considered those who went out from their homes, in the thousands, fearing death [c1]. God said to them: die; then He gave them life [c2]. God has bounty over people, but most people do not give thanks [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah is one sentence and carries a series of statements: the going out, the saying of God and then the giving of life, and the remark on thanks [c1][c2][c3]. It gives no names and no setting, so the account is as short as the verse [c1].
chapters.kids_md: Once some people left their homes, many thousands of them, because they were afraid of dying [c1]. God said to them: die; then He gave them life [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that fear of death is set beside God's power to give life [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayah ends by saying most people do not give thanks for God's bounty [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who these people were, where they lived, why they feared death, and when this was.
- Not established: how they died, how they were given life, or what they did afterwards.
- Not established: whether the words die and then He gave them life describe one event or a manner of speaking; the ayah gives no more.
- The ayah does not say how many thousands.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on who these people were. None is used in this draft.
Later commentators gave different accounts of the people and the place; none is in the ayah and none is used here.

stories.title_en: The staff and the creature of the earth

claims.statement_en: When God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff.
When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment.

chapters.summary_md: When God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah says that when God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives a pair of moments: the decree of death with the creature eating the staff, and the falling after which it became clear to the jinn [c1][c2]. The statement about the unseen is made of the jinn: knowing the unseen would have kept them from the punishment [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah says a small creature of the earth was eating a staff, and that was what showed his death [c1]. When he fell, the jinn saw that they did not know the unseen [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah teaches that knowledge of the unseen is not with the jinn [c2]. Another is that the ayah shows a death made known through an ordinary creature and an ordinary object [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who is meant; the ayah does not name him, and the inventory title identifies him from the verses before this one, which are outside the verses cited here.
- Not established: how long he remained as he was, what the staff was, or what the creature of the earth was.
- Not established: what work the jinn were doing, or how they came to know the matter; the ayah says only that it became clear to them when he fell.
- Not established: who is meant by them in the first clause; the ayah does not say who was not shown his death.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this event. None is used in this draft.
The ayah names no one; the link to the person named in the inventory title rests on the verses before it, which this draft does not cite. A scholar should confirm that link and its wording.
The word translated staff (minsa'ah) and the phrase creature of the earth are rendered plainly; a scholar should confirm.

stories.title_en: The disputants who came to Dawud

claims.statement_en: The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants has reached the hearer, when they climbed into the mihrab.

They entered upon Dawud and he was alarmed at them; they said: do not fear, we are a pair of disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path.
One of them said: this is my brother, he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; he said to entrust it to him, and he overcame me in speech.
Dawud said: he has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes; many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they.
Dawud thought that We had tested him; he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down bowing, and turned to God.
God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness to Us and a good place of return.

chapters.summary_md: A pair of disputants came to Dawud with a case about one ewe and ninety-nine ewes, and Dawud gave judgement [c2][c3][c4]. Dawud thought that he had been tested, asked forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned to God, and God forgave him [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah asks whether the news of the disputants has reached the hearer, when they climbed into the mihrab [c1]. They entered upon Dawud and he was alarmed at them [c2]. They said: do not fear, we are a pair of disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path [c2].

One of them said: this is my brother, he has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; he said to entrust it to him, and he overcame me in speech [c3]. Dawud said: he has wronged you by asking for your ewe to add to his ewes; many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they [c4].

Dawud thought that We had tested him; he asked forgiveness of his Lord, fell down bowing, and turned to God [c5]. God forgave him that, and said that he has nearness to Us and a good place of return [c6].
chapters.deep_md: Dawud's answer speaks of partners in general and then names the exceptions, those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4]. The ayah does not say what Dawud was forgiven; it says only that God forgave him that [c5][c6]. The same ayah that gives his judgement gives his turning to God, so the case and the test are told together [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: A pair of people came to Dawud with an argument about sheep: one had ninety-nine and the other had one [c2][c3]. Dawud gave his answer, then asked God to forgive him and bowed down, and God forgave him [c4][c5][c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the case teaches that many who share a thing wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds [c4]. Another is that the passage ends with turning to God and with forgiveness [c5][c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the disputants were, whether they were people or something else, or how they entered; the ayah says only that they climbed into the mihrab.
- Not established: what Dawud thought was the test, or what he was forgiven; the ayah says that without naming it.
- Not established: whether the case is a real dispute or a parable; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: where or when this was, or what Dawud did after the judgement.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this case and on the meaning of the test. None is used in this draft.

Later commentators gave many accounts of what the test was; none is in the ayat and none is used here. A scholar should decide how the page should word the phrase that Dawud thought We had tested him (zanna anna-ma fatannahu).
On etiquette, this draft gives no verdict on Dawud; it states what the ayat state, that he asked forgiveness and was forgiven.

claims.statement_en: Yunus was among the messengers.
He went away to the laden ship.
He cast lots and was among those who lost.
The fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.
Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the day they are raised.
God cast him on the open ground, and he was sick.
God caused a tree of yaqtin to grow over him.
God sent him to a hundred thousand or more; they believed, and God let them enjoy life for a time.

chapters.summary_md: Yunus, one of the messengers, went away to the laden ship, and the fish swallowed him [c1][c2][c4]. God cast him on the open ground, sent him to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed [c6][c8].
chapters.body_md:
The ayat say that Yunus was among the messengers [c1]. He went away to the laden ship, cast lots and was among those who lost [c2][c3].

The fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy [c4]. Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the day they are raised [c5].

God cast him on the open ground, and he was sick, and caused a tree of yaqtin to grow over him [c6][c7]. God sent him to a hundred thousand or more; they believed, and God let them enjoy life for a time [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give the cause of his rescue as his glorifying of God, and say what would otherwise have happened [c5]. The word for blameworthy describes him at the moment the fish swallowed him [c4]. The mission is told after the rescue: the number is given as a hundred thousand or more, and the result is that they believed [c8].
chapters.kids_md: Yunus was one of God's messengers, and he went away on a ship that was full [c1][c2]. A fish swallowed him, but he glorified God, and God cast him out on open ground and made a tree grow over him [c4][c5][c6][c7]. Then God sent him to a hundred thousand people or more, and they believed [c8].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie his rescue to his glorifying of God [c5]. Another is that the account ends with a whole people who believed and were allowed to enjoy life for a time [c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: why he went away, where he was sent first, where the ship sailed, or what the lots decided; the verses say only that he went away to the laden ship and cast lots.
- Not established: how long he stayed in the fish, where he was cast out, or what kind of tree the yaqtin was.
- Not established: the name of the people he was sent to, the place, or how long they were allowed to enjoy life.
- Not established: whether the sending to a hundred thousand or more happened before or after the events at sea; the verses tell it afterwards.

claims.statement_en: The man of the fish went away angry, thought that We would not constrain him, and called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers.
God answered him and saved him from distress, and said that He saves the believers in this way.
The hearer is told to be patient with the judgement of his Lord and not to be like the man of the fish when he cried out while choked with grief.
Had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast on the open ground while blameworthy.
His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: The man of the fish went away angry, and called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. God answered him and saved him from distress, chose him and made him among the righteous [c2][c5].
chapters.body_md:
The man of the fish went away angry, thought that We would not constrain him, and called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. God answered him and saved him from distress, and said that He saves the believers in this way [c2].

Another passage tells the hearer to be patient with the judgement of his Lord and not to be like the man of the fish when he cried out while choked with grief [c3]. It says that, had a favour from his Lord not reached him, he would have been cast on the open ground while blameworthy [c4]. His Lord chose him and made him among the righteous [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The cry has its parts in the ayah: that there is no god but God, glory to Him, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. The Arabic for constrain can also be read as having power over him, and the draft keeps it open [c1]. The ayat give God's answer as an answer to the cry and say the same is done for the believers [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The man of the fish called out in the darkness that there is no god but God, and that he had been among the wrongdoers [c1]. God answered him and saved him from his distress [c2]. God chose him and made him among the righteous [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat teach a prayer of praise and admission, and say that God answered it [c1][c2]. Another is that the hearer is told to be patient and not to be like him in his grief [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: that the man of the fish is the messenger named in the other chapter is read from the epithet and the matching events; the ayat here do not name him.
- Not established: what the darkness was, or where he was when he called; the Arabic word is plural and is not explained in the verses.
- Not established: what he was angry about, or what he thought of being constrained; the Arabic verb allows more than one rendering.
- Not established: how long the distress lasted.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the mission of Yunus, the fish and the people he was sent to. None is used in this draft.

The later chapter speaks of the man of the fish and of the one with the fish without naming Yunus; the link rests on the epithet and the matching events, as in the event inventory. A scholar should confirm.

The verb abaqa (37:140) is rendered 'went away' and is often rendered 'fled'. The Arabic naqdira (21:87) is rendered 'constrain'; it is read as having power over him by others. The words for blameworthy (muliim, madhmum) are rendered plainly.

stories.title_en: The glad tidings of Yahya to Zakariyya

chapters.title_en: The prayer and the glad tidings

claims.statement_en: Zakariyya called on his Lord, quietly, and asked for good offspring from Him; the ayah says that his Lord hears prayer.
He said that his bones had grown weak and that age had set its mark on his head, and that he had never been unfortunate in calling on his Lord.
He said he feared the ones who would follow him, and his wife was barren; he asked for an heir who would inherit from him and from the family of Yaqub, and asked that his Lord make him pleasing.
The angels called to him while he stood praying in the mihrab, saying that God gives him glad tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a sayyid and hasur, and a prophet among the righteous.
God said: O Zakariyya, We give you glad tidings of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not made anyone before him of that name.

He said: my Lord, how shall I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren; God said that this is how God does what He wills, that it is easy for Him, and that He had created him before when he was nothing.

He asked for a sign, and God said the sign was that he would not speak to people for three days, except by gesture, and that he should remember his Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and morning (19:10 says three nights).
He came out to his people from the mihrab and signalled to them to glorify God morning and evening.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya called quietly on his Lord for offspring, and the angels called to him with glad tidings of Yahya [c1][c4]. He asked how he could have a boy, and the sign given to him was that he would not speak to people for three days, except by gesture [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md:
Zakariyya called on his Lord, quietly, and asked for good offspring from Him [c1]. He said that his bones had grown weak and that age had set its mark on his head, and that he had never been unfortunate in calling on his Lord [c2]. He said he feared the ones who would follow him, and his wife was barren; he asked for an heir who would inherit from him and from the family of Yaqub [c3].

The angels called to him while he stood praying in the mihrab, saying that God gives him glad tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a sayyid and hasur, and a prophet among the righteous [c4]. God said: O Zakariyya, We give you glad tidings of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not made anyone before him of that name [c5].

He said: my Lord, how shall I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren [c6]. God said that this is how God does what He wills, that it is easy for Him, and that He had created him before when he was nothing [c6].

He asked for a sign, and God said the sign was that he would not speak to people for three days, except by gesture, and that he should remember his Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and morning [c7]. He came out to his people from the mihrab and signalled to them to glorify God morning and evening [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The passages tell the same event from different sides: one gives the angels' call in the mihrab and the other gives the quiet prayer and the wording of his request [c1][c4]. The sign is given as three days in one passage and three nights in the other [c7]. The words sayyid and hasur are left untranslated because the ayah does not explain them [c4].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya called quietly on his Lord and asked for a good child [c1]. The angels called to him and gave him glad tidings of a boy named Yahya [c4][c5]. As a sign he would not speak to people for three days, except by gesture, and he told his people to glorify God morning and evening [c7][c8].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show a prayer made quietly and answered [c1][c4]. Another is that the glad tidings are met with a question and answered with the statement that it is easy for God [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: his age, his wife's name, or the place of the mihrab; the ayat give only that his bones had grown weak and his wife was barren.
- Not established: who the ones who would follow him were, or what he feared from them.
- Not established: whether the silence was of tongue by a cause or a sign alone; the ayah says only that he would not speak to people except by gesture.
- Not established: the meaning of sayyid and hasur beyond the Arabic words; commentators differ and the draft leaves them untranslated.
- The ayat do not say how long it was between the prayer and the glad tidings.

claims.statement_en: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgement while he was a child.
God also gave him tenderness from Himself and purity, and he feared God.
He was dutiful to his parents and was not arrogant or disobedient.
Peace be on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.

chapters.summary_md: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgement while he was a child [c1]. He feared God and was dutiful to his parents, and peace was invoked on him on the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c2][c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgement while he was a child [c1]. God also gave him tenderness from Himself and purity, and he feared God [c2].

He was dutiful to his parents and was not arrogant or disobedient [c3]. Peace be on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat list what he was given and how he was: strength with the Book, judgement, tenderness, purity and fear of God [c1][c2]. The words about his parents come before the words of peace on him [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: Yahya was told to hold the Book firmly, and God gave him good judgement while he was still a child [c1]. He was kind to his parents and he feared God [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat link duty to parents with not being arrogant or disobedient [c3]. Another is that the passage ends with peace on his life, his death and his raising [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: his age when he was given judgement, or what the judgement was; the ayah says only that he was a child.
- Not established: which Book is meant; the ayah says the Book and does not say more.
- Not established: what became of Yahya, the manner of his death or where he lived.
- The ayat do not say what the words for tenderness and purity cover.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Zakariyya, Yahya and his life. None is used in this draft.
The image of the head in 19:4 is rendered loosely (age had set its mark) so that this draft does not describe a prophet; a scholar should decide the wording.
The words sayyid and hasur (3:39) and the Book (19:12) have more than one reading; a scholar should decide how the page should word them.
The passages (3:38-41 and 19:2-11) are read as the same event; the order of the angels' call and the quiet prayer is not stated in the ayat.

stories.title_en: The annunciation to Maryam and the birth of Isa

claims.statement_en: The angels said: O Maryam, God has chosen you, purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds.

The angels said that God gives her glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, held in honour in this world and the next and among those brought near; he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and will be among the righteous.
Maryam withdrew from her family to a place in the east and took a screen apart from them.
God sent Our spirit to her; she said: I seek refuge in the Merciful from you, if you fear God.
He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.

She said: how can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I am not unchaste; he said that this is what her Lord said, that it is easy for Him, that He would make him a sign for people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed.
God says that He creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be", and it is.

chapters.summary_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her and gave her glad tidings of a word from Him, the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam [c1][c2]. She asked how she could have a boy when no human had touched her, and the answer was that her Lord said it is easy for Him [c6].
chapters.body_md:
The angels said: O Maryam, God has chosen you, purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds [c1]. They said that God gives her glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, held in honour in this world and the next and among those brought near [c2]. He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and will be among the righteous [c2].

Maryam withdrew from her family to a place in the east and took a screen apart from them [c3]. God sent Our spirit to her; she said: I seek refuge in the Merciful from you, if you fear God [c4]. He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy [c5].

She said: how can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I am not unchaste [c6]. He said that this is what her Lord said, that it is easy for Him, that He would make him a sign for people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed [c6]. God says that He creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be", and it is [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passages give the same answer in different words: in one it is easy for God, and in the other God creates what He wills [c6][c7]. The ayat name him the Messiah and Isa son of Maryam, and say his place is held in honour in this world and the next [c2]. The form in which the spirit came to her is not described in this draft [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a son called Isa, who would speak to people even in the cradle [c2]. Maryam asked how it could be, and the answer was that it is easy for God [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the question of how beside the statement that God creates what He wills [c6][c7]. Another is that Maryam's first words to the spirit are words of refuge in the Merciful [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when or where the glad tidings came, or how old Maryam was; the ayat say only that she withdrew to a place in the east.
- Not established: the form in which the spirit came to her; the ayah speaks of it and this draft does not describe it.
- Not established: how the glad tidings of 3:45 and the message of 19:19 relate in order; the passages are read as one event.
- Not established: how the pregnancy began beyond what the ayat state.

claims.statement_en: She conceived him and withdrew with him to a place far away.
The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree; she said she wished she had died before this and been forgotten.
She was called from beneath her: do not grieve, your Lord has placed a stream beneath you; shake the trunk of the palm toward you and fresh ripe dates will fall; eat, drink and be content.
She was told that if she saw any human, she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak to any person that day.
She pointed to him; they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child; he said: I am a servant of God, He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.
He said that peace was on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive; this is Isa son of Maryam, a word of truth about which they doubt.
God made Maryam, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds; He breathed into her of Our spirit and sheltered them on elevated ground with a place for settlement and flowing water.
Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam conceived and withdrew to a place far away, and the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree [c1][c2]. The child spoke from the cradle, saying he was a servant of God, and God made Maryam and her son a sign for the worlds [c5][c7].
chapters.body_md:
She conceived him and withdrew with him to a place far away [c1]. The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree; she said she wished she had died before this and been forgotten [c2].

She was called from beneath her: do not grieve, your Lord has placed a stream beneath you; shake the trunk of the palm toward you and fresh ripe dates will fall; eat, drink and be content [c3]. She was told that if she saw any human, she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak to any person that day [c4].

She pointed to him; they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child; he said: I am a servant of God, He has given me the Book and made me a prophet [c5]. He said that peace was on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive; this is Isa son of Maryam, a word of truth about which they doubt [c6].

God made Maryam, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds; He breathed into her of Our spirit and sheltered them on elevated ground with a place for settlement and flowing water [c7]. Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat on the cradle speech are partly reported by the child and partly closed by the ayah calling him Isa son of Maryam and a word of truth [c5][c6]. The other passages describe Maryam and her son as a sign and speak of her as one who guarded her chastity, confirmed God's words and was among the devout [c7][c8]. The ayat do not say who called her from beneath her [c3].
chapters.kids_md: When Isa was born, Maryam was told to eat and drink and not to be sad [c3]. She pointed to the baby, and he spoke from the cradle and said he was a servant of God [c5]. God made Maryam and her son a sign for all the worlds [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the account sets her distress beside the words do not grieve [c2][c3]. Another is that the passages call Maryam devout and her son a sign for the worlds [c7][c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the place far away was, how long Maryam stayed there, or who was with her.
- Not established: who called to her from beneath her; the Arabic can be read as a person or as the one under her.
- Not established: how the people reacted beyond the words the ayat record, or how long after the birth they came.
- Not established: the date or the day of the birth.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the birth of Isa and on Maryam. None is used in this draft.
The event is told at greater length in the draft for Isa (content/stories); this event draft stays inside its own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state.

The caller in 19:24 (who called from beneath her) is read in more than one way in commentary; a scholar should decide whether the page names a reading. The words to be spoken to the people (19:26) are reported speech and nothing more.
The chapters omit 3:43-44, 19:27-28 and 19:31-32; 19:27-28 refers by name to another figure, which this draft does not repeat.

stories.title_en: The table sent down to the disciples

claims.statement_en: The disciples said: O Isa son of Maryam, can your Lord send down on us a table from the sky? He said: fear God, if you are believers.
They said they wanted to eat from it, that their hearts might be at rest, that they might know he had told them the truth, and that they might be witnesses to it.

Isa son of Maryam said: O God, our Lord, send down on us a table from the sky, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You, and provide for us; You are the best of providers.
God said: I am sending it down to you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish with a punishment I have not inflicted on anyone among the worlds.

chapters.summary_md: The disciples asked Isa son of Maryam whether his Lord could send down a table from the sky, and Isa asked God to send it down [c1][c3]. God said He was sending it down, and warned of a punishment for whoever disbelieved after that [c4].
chapters.body_md:
The disciples said: O Isa son of Maryam, can your Lord send down on us a table from the sky [c1]. He said: fear God, if you are believers [c1].

They said they wanted to eat from it, that their hearts might be at rest, that they might know he had told them the truth, and that they might be witnesses to it [c2].

Isa son of Maryam said: O God, our Lord, send down on us a table from the sky, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You, and provide for us; You are the best of providers [c3]. God said: I am sending it down to you; whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish with a punishment I have not inflicted on anyone among the worlds [c4].
chapters.deep_md: Isa first answers the request with a call to fear God, and then makes the request himself in his own prayer [c1][c3]. The disciples give their reasons: to eat, for their hearts to be at rest, to know the truth of what he told them, and to be witnesses [c2]. The ayah gives God's answer in the form I am sending it down, and joins to it a warning for those who disbelieve afterwards [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The disciples asked Isa if God could send down a table from the sky [c1]. Isa asked God to send it, as a sign and a festival, and God said He would [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the disciples' reasons for asking are set out in the ayah, and that Isa turns the request into a prayer [c2][c3]. Another is that the answer comes with a warning for whoever disbelieves afterwards [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether the table was in fact sent down; the ayah records God's saying that He is sending it, and the verses cited do not narrate its coming.
- Not established: what was on the table, when, where, or who ate from it.
- Not established: who the disciples were by name or how many; the ayah says only the disciples.
- Not established: how the warning in the last ayah was or was not carried out.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on what was on the table and what followed. None is used in this draft.
The ayah (5:112) can be read 'can your Lord' or 'would your Lord', with different readings of the first verb; a scholar should decide the wording.
The Arabic for sky (samaa) is rendered 'sky'; it is often rendered 'heaven', and a scholar should choose.

chapters.title_en: What God said of his raising

claims.statement_en: God said: O Isa, I am mutawaffika and raising you to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved, and I will place those who follow you above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me is your return and I will judge between you in what you differed.
The ayah reports their claim that they killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of God.

They did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them; those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge of it, and follow only conjecture; they did not kill him for certain.
Rather, God raised him to Himself; God is Mighty, Wise.

chapters.summary_md: God told Isa that He was raising him to Himself and placing those who follow him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection [c1]. The ayat say that they did not kill him or crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them, and that God raised him to Himself [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
God said: O Isa, I am mutawaffika and raising you to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved [c1]. He said that He would place those who follow him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection, and that then their return is to Him and He will judge between them in what they differed [c1].

The other passage reports their claim that they killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of God [c2]. It says that they did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them [c3]. Those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge of it, and follow only conjecture; they did not kill him for certain [c3].

Rather, God raised him to Himself; God is Mighty, Wise [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The word mutawaffika is read in more than one way and is left untranslated here [c1]. The ayat give God's raising of him in more than one form: as His address to Isa and as His statement of what is true against the claim [c1][c4]. The ayah on the claim speaks of doubt and conjecture among those who differ about it [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God told Isa that He would raise him to Himself [c1]. Some people claimed they had killed him, but the ayah says they did not, and that God raised him to Himself [c2][c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat answer a claim with what is certain, that God raised him to Himself [c3][c4]. Another is that the ayat set doubt and conjecture beside knowledge [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: how Isa was raised, where, when, or in what state; the ayat say that God raised him to Himself and no more.
- Not established: what it was that was made to appear so to them; the Arabic is open and the draft keeps it open.
- Not established: the meaning of mutawaffika beyond the Arabic word, which commentators read in more than one way.
- Not established: who the ones who claimed to have killed him are, beyond the ayah's report of their saying.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the raising and on any later return. None is used in this draft.
The word mutawaffika (3:55) and the phrase shubbiha lahum (4:157) are read in more than one way; a scholar must decide how the page words each, and this draft deliberately takes no side.
The order of 3:55 and 4:157-158 is a reading order; the ayat do not give a timeline between them.
