claims.statement_en: The ayah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant.
He made their plot go astray.
He sent birds in flocks upon them.
The birds struck them with stones of sijjil.
He made them like chaff that has been eaten.

chapters.summary_md: The surah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant, and says He made their plot go astray [c1][c2]. He sent birds in flocks upon them, which struck them with stones, and made them like chaff that has been eaten [c3][c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah asks whether one has not seen how the Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant [c1]. He made their plot go astray [c2].

He sent birds in flocks upon them [c3]. The birds struck them with stones of sijjil [c4]. He made them like chaff that has been eaten [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The account is a few short ayat and is built as questions followed by what God did [c1][c2]. The word sijjil is left untranslated here, and the word for flocks is read in more than one way [c3][c4]. The last ayah describes the result with a comparison to chaff that has been eaten [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat ask if you have seen what the Lord did to the companions of the elephant [c1]. He made their plot go wrong, sent flocks of birds with stones, and made them like eaten chaff [c2][c3][c4][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show a plot that went astray [c2]. Another is that the account is told as something the hearer is asked to consider [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the companions of the elephant were, where they went, what their plot was, or when this happened; the ayat give only the title and what God did.
- Not established: how many there were, how many elephants, or what became of them beyond the comparison to chaff.
- Not established: what the birds were, how many, or what the stones of sijjil were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leader, the kingdom he came from, the place he marched against and the year of the event.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, and early historical reports on who the companions of the elephant were and when. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leader Abraha, the land of Yemen, and the place they marched against.
The words sijjil and ababil are rendered plainly or left untranslated; a scholar should decide how the page should word them.

stories.title_en: The defeat and the promised victory of the Rum

claims.statement_en: The Rum have been defeated, in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will themselves be victorious, in several years.
The command belongs to God before and after; on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help.
God helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful.
It is the promise of God; God does not break His promise, but most people do not know.
They know an outward part of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that the Rum have been defeated in the nearest land and will be victorious after their defeat, in several years [c1]. They add that the command belongs to God before and after, and that God does not break His promise [c2][c4].
chapters.body_md:
The Rum have been defeated, in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will themselves be victorious, in several years [c1]. The command belongs to God before and after; on that day the believers will rejoice in God's help [c2].

God helps whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful [c3]. It is the promise of God; God does not break His promise, but most people do not know [c4]. They know an outward part of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat speak of the past and of the future: a defeat that has happened and a victory that will follow it [c1]. The Arabic for nearest land can also be read as the lowest land, and the draft keeps it open [c1]. The final ayat turn from the event to people's knowledge, saying they know the outward part of this life and are heedless of the Hereafter [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that the Rum had been defeated but would win after some years [c1]. They say that God keeps His promise, though most people do not know it [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places an event under God's command, before and after it [c2]. Another is that it sets the outward knowledge of this life beside heedlessness of the Hereafter [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which battle or war is meant, who defeated the Rum, where the nearest land was, or when the defeat happened.
- Not established: how many years several covers, or in what event the victory came; the ayat give only several years.
- Not established: what the believers rejoiced at beyond God's help, or what the connection of the believers to the Rum was.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the Rum with the Byzantines, of their opponents with the Persians, and the places and years of the war.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, and early historical reports on the war and on the believers' reaction. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the Byzantines, the Persians and the dating of the defeat and the victory.

The vowel reading of the verbs in 30:2-3 (defeated, will be victorious) is disputed in the readings tradition; a scholar of qira'at should decide how the page words it. The draft follows the common reading.
The phrase 'on that day the believers will rejoice' (30:4-5) is rendered closely and left open as to its cause.

chapters.title_en: Glory to Him who took His servant

claims.statement_en: Glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed.
The purpose given is to show him some of Our signs.
He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah gives glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed [c1]. It says the purpose was to show him some of Our signs [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah gives glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed [c1]. The purpose given is to show him some of Our signs [c2]. He is the Hearing, the Seeing [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah has one sentence of praise, one of purpose and one that names God as the Hearing and the Seeing, all around a journey told in a single clause [c1][c2][c3]. It names no person, no vehicle, no duration and no time of the night [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God took His servant by night from one mosque to a farthest mosque [c1]. It was to show him some of God's signs [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah begins with glory to God before it states the journey, as the wording of the ayah shows [c1]. Another is that the journey's purpose is stated as showing signs [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the servant is; the ayah does not name him.
- Not established: how the journey was made, how long it took, whether it was bodily or in vision, or what the signs were that he was shown.
- Not established: what the farthest mosque was or where, beyond the ayah's words about blessed surroundings.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the servant, the starting place and the farthest mosque by name, the vehicle, the ascent, the meetings with earlier prophets and the date.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the night journey and on the ascent that later tradition links with it. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names Jerusalem, Isra, Miraj and Buraq and the place of the farthest mosque.
The Arabic for the first mosque (a descriptive epithet) is rendered 'inviolable'; the common rendering is 'sacred'. A scholar should decide the wording.
Whether the journey was in body or in spirit was disputed by earlier scholars and the ayah does not settle it; this draft takes no side.

claims.statement_en: The ayah says that the Lord brought the one addressed out from his house with the truth, though a party of the believers disliked it; they disputed with him about the truth after it had become clear, as if they were being driven to death while looking on.

God promised them that one of the pair of parties would be theirs, and they wished that the one without sharp strength would be theirs; but God wished to establish the truth by His words and cut off the last of the disbelievers, to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even if the wrongdoers disliked it.

When they called on their Lord for help, He answered them: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another; God made it only glad tidings, so that their hearts would be at rest, and said that victory is only from God, who is Mighty, Wise.
God covered them with drowsiness as security from Him, and sent down water from the sky to purify them and remove the filth of Satan, to strengthen their hearts and make their feet firm.
Your Lord revealed to the angels: I am with you, so make firm those who believe; I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve.
God gave them victory at Badr when they were weak, so that they fear God and give thanks.

The ayah says: when you said to the believers, would it not suffice that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down; yes, if you are patient and fear God, and they come at you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels.

God made it only glad tidings, so that their hearts would be at rest, and said that victory is only from God, the Mighty, the Wise; and that He might cut off a part of those who disbelieved or subdue them, so that they turn back disappointed.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that a party of the believers disliked the going out, and that God promised them one of the pair of parties [c1][c2]. God answered their call for help by reinforcing them with angels, and said that victory is only from God and that He gave them victory at Badr [c3][c6][c8].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah says that the Lord brought the one addressed out from his house with the truth, though a party of the believers disliked it [c1]. They disputed with him about the truth after it had become clear, as if they were being driven to death while looking on [c1].

God promised them that one of the pair of parties would be theirs, and they wished that the one without sharp strength would be theirs [c2]. God wished to establish the truth by His words and cut off the last of the disbelievers, to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even if the wrongdoers disliked it [c2].

When they called on their Lord for help, He answered them: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another [c3]. God made it only glad tidings, so that their hearts would be at rest, and said that victory is only from God, who is Mighty, Wise [c3]. He covered them with drowsiness as security from Him, and sent down water from the sky to purify them and remove the filth of Satan, to strengthen their hearts and make their feet firm [c4].

Your Lord revealed to the angels: I am with you, so make firm those who believe; I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve [c5].

God gave them victory at Badr when they were weak, so that they fear God and give thanks [c6]. The ayah says: when you said to the believers, would it not suffice that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down; yes, if you are patient and fear God, and they come at you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels [c7]. God made it only glad tidings, so that their hearts would be at rest, and said that victory is only from God, the Mighty, the Wise [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give the angels' number differently in different places: a thousand in 8:9, and three thousand and five thousand in 3:124-125, and each is stated as a reinforcement and as glad tidings [c3][c7][c8]. In both places the ayat say the reinforcement was only glad tidings and a reassurance for hearts, and that victory is only from God [c3][c8]. The ayat of 3:123 name Badr, and the ayat that follow it are read with it [c6][c7].
chapters.kids_md: The believers called on their Lord for help, and He answered them [c3]. He reinforced them with angels, made them calm, and said that victory is only from God [c3][c4][c8]. God gave them victory at Badr when they were weak [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat say the reinforcement was glad tidings and a calming of hearts, and that victory is only from God [c3][c8]. Another is that they were told to fear God and give thanks for the victory [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the date, the place beyond the name Badr, the number of the believers or of their opponents, or the casualties; the ayat give none of these.
- Not established: who the pair of parties were, or what the party without sharp strength was; the ayah says only that one of the pair would be theirs.
- Not established: whether 3:124-125 speak of this day or of another; the ayah that precedes them names Badr, and they are read here with it. A scholar should decide.
- Not established: how the angels took part beyond what the ayat state, or how their number in one place relates to the numbers in the other.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the leaders, the caravan, the tribes involved and the names of the fighters. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

claims.statement_en: It was not they who killed them, but God killed them; and it was not the one addressed who threw when he threw, but God threw, so that He might try the believers with a good trial; God is Hearing, Knowing.
The ayah refers to the day of the Criterion, the day the pair of armies met.

They were on the nearer side and their opponents on the farther side, and the caravan was below them; had they made an appointment they would have differed about it, but God was to accomplish a matter already done, so that whoever perished would perish by clear evidence and whoever lived would live by clear evidence.

God showed them to the one addressed in his sleep as few; had He shown them as many, the believers would have lost courage and disputed over the matter, but God spared them; when they met, He showed them to the believers as few, and made the believers few in their sight, so that God might accomplish a matter already done.

The believers were told: when you meet a group, stand firm and remember God much, so that you may succeed; obey God and His Messenger and do not dispute, or you will lose heart and your strength will go; be patient, for God is with the patient.

They were told not to be like those who came out of their homes boastfully and to be seen by people, and who hinder others from God's way; Satan had made their deeds seem fair to them and said that no one could overcome them that day and that he was their protector; but when the pair of groups came in sight of each other he turned on his heels and said: I am free of you, I see what you do not see, I fear God.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat call the day the pair of armies met the day of the Criterion, and say that it was God who killed them and God who threw [c1][c2]. The believers were told to stand firm, remember God much, obey and not dispute [c5].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah says: it was not they who killed them, but God killed them; and it was not the one addressed who threw when he threw, but God threw, so that He might try the believers with a good trial [c1]. The ayah refers to the day of the Criterion, the day the pair of armies met [c2].

They were on the nearer side and their opponents on the farther side, and the caravan was below them [c3]. Had they made an appointment they would have differed about it, but God was to accomplish a matter already done, so that whoever perished would perish by clear evidence and whoever lived would live by clear evidence [c3].

God showed them to the one addressed in his sleep as few; had He shown them as many, the believers would have lost courage and disputed over the matter, but God spared them [c4]. When they met, He showed them to the believers as few, and made the believers few in their sight, so that God might accomplish a matter already done [c4].

The believers were told: when you meet a group, stand firm and remember God much, so that you may succeed [c5]. They were told to obey God and His Messenger and not to dispute, or they would lose heart and their strength would go; they were told to be patient, for God is with the patient [c5].

They were told not to be like those who came out of their homes boastfully and to be seen by people, and who hinder others from God's way [c6]. Satan had made their deeds seem fair to them and said that no one could overcome them that day and that he was their protector; but when the pair of groups came in sight of each other he turned on his heels and said: I am free of you, I see what you do not see, I fear God [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat say more than once that God was to accomplish a matter already done: about the meeting place and about the view each side had of the other [c3][c4]. The believers are given instructions in the same passage: stand firm, remember God, obey, do not dispute, be patient [c5]. The account of Satan's words speaks of what he said before the groups met and what he said when they came in sight of each other [c6].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that it was God who killed and God who threw [c1]. They tell the believers to stand firm, remember God much, obey and not to quarrel [c5]. Satan said he would protect some people, but he turned away when the groups met [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat give the believers a short list of conduct: stand firm, remember God much, obey, do not dispute and be patient [c5]. Another is that the ayat show Satan's promise failing when the groups met [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who killed whom, how many were on either side, what was thrown, or where the nearer and farther sides were.
- Not established: who the opponents were by name, or who the caravan was; the ayat speak of a caravan below the believers and do not name it.
- Not established: the date of the day of the Criterion; the ayah names the day and not its date.
- Not established: how the ayat on spoils in 8:41 relate to this account; this draft does not reproduce their legal content.

claims.statement_en: It was not for a prophet to hold captives until he had made the land secure; they wanted the goods of this world, while God wants the Hereafter; God is Mighty, Wise.
Had it not been for a decree from God already given, a great punishment would have touched them for what they took.
The Prophet was told to say to the captives in their hands: if God knows good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and forgive you; God is Forgiving, Merciful.
If they intend betrayal of him, they betrayed God before, and God gave him power over them; God is Knowing, Wise.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that a prophet should not hold captives until he has made the land secure, and that a great punishment would have touched them but for a decree from God [c1][c2]. The Prophet was told what to say to the captives, and God is Forgiving, Merciful [c3].
chapters.body_md:
It was not for a prophet to hold captives until he had made the land secure; they wanted the goods of this world, while God wants the Hereafter [c1]. Had it not been for a decree from God already given, a great punishment would have touched them for what they took [c2].

The Prophet was told to say to the captives in their hands: if God knows good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and forgive you [c3]. If they intend betrayal of him, they betrayed God before, and God gave him power over them [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passage speaks to the believers about what they wanted and then speaks to the Prophet about what to say to the captives [c1][c3]. It ends with a warning to the captives that betrayal has a history, and with God's knowledge and wisdom [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God told the believers what a prophet should do about captives [c1]. He told the Prophet to say to the captives that if God knows good in their hearts, He will give them better and forgive them [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets what people want of this world beside what God wants, the Hereafter [c1]. Another is that the captives are offered forgiveness if there is good in their hearts [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the captives were, how many, or what was taken from them; the ayat say only that something was taken from them.
- Not established: what the decree from God already given was, or what the believers did in the matter.
- Not established: when or where the captives were held.
- The ayah 8:69, on what was gained, is not drafted here because it is legal in kind.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the course of the battle, the numbers, the caravan, the captives and the individuals involved. None is used in this draft.
The ayat state no casualties, no dates and no commanders; none are given in this draft.

3:13 (the sign in the pair of groups that met) is not drafted: its Arabic wording of how each group saw the other is read in more than one way and carries a number that this draft cannot anchor safely.
Whether 3:124-125 belong to this day or to the day that the next event in the inventory covers is read in more than one way; a scholar should decide.
The prophet drafts in content/stories tell part of this at greater length; this event draft stays inside its own refs and does not repeat it.

claims.statement_en: The ayah says: when you went out at dawn from your family to settle the believers in positions for battle; God is Hearing, Knowing.
A pair of parties among them were about to lose heart, though God was their ally; on God let the believers rely.
The one addressed was told that none of the matter is his, whether God turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.
To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth; He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills; God is Forgiving, Merciful.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat speak of a going out at dawn to settle the believers in positions for battle, and of a pair of parties who were about to lose heart [c1][c2]. They also tell the one addressed that none of the matter is his, and that God forgives whom He wills [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah says: when you went out at dawn from your family to settle the believers in positions for battle; God is Hearing, Knowing [c1]. A pair of parties among them were about to lose heart, though God was their ally; on God let the believers rely [c2].

The one addressed was told that none of the matter is his, whether God turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers [c3]. To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth; He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat do not name the day or the place; they say only that someone went out at dawn from his family to set the believers in positions [c1]. They add that God was the ally of the pair of parties who were about to lose heart [c2]. The words that none of the matter is his are followed by a statement that all belongs to God [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that someone went out at dawn from his family and set the believers in their places for battle [c1]. God said that He is the ally of the believers, and that all belongs to God [c2][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the believers are told to rely on God even when a pair of parties among them were about to lose heart [c2]. Another is that the ayat close on God's forgiveness and mercy [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name of the day or the place; the ayat name neither. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.
- Not established: who the pair of parties were, or what made them about to lose heart.
- Not established: who they are in 3:128, the ones God may turn to or punish; the ayah says them and does not name them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Uhud for the day and the place, and the names of the commanders and groups.

claims.statement_en: They were told not to weaken or grieve, for they would be the uppermost if they were believers.

If a wound had touched them, a like wound had touched the others; God lets such days alternate among people, so that God knows those who believe and takes witnesses from among them; God does not love wrongdoers.
This was so that God might purify the believers and wipe out the disbelievers.
The ayah asks whether they thought they would enter the Garden before God knew those of them who strove and those who were patient.
They had wished for death before they met it; now they had seen it, looking on.

chapters.summary_md: The believers were told not to weaken or grieve, and that if a wound had touched them a like wound had touched the others [c1][c2]. The ayat say that God lets such days alternate among people, so that He knows the believers and purifies them [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
They were told not to weaken or grieve, for they would be the uppermost if they were believers [c1]. If a wound had touched them, a like wound had touched the others [c2].

God lets such days alternate among people, so that God knows those who believe and takes witnesses from among them; God does not love wrongdoers [c2]. This was so that God might purify the believers and wipe out the disbelievers [c3].

The ayah asks whether they thought they would enter the Garden before God knew those of them who strove and those who were patient [c4]. They had wished for death before they met it; now they had seen it, looking on [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat answer weakness and grief with a statement about the alternation of days among people and give its purposes [c1][c2][c3]. The question about entering the Garden is put to those who had wished for death before meeting it [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: The believers were told not to lose heart or be sad [c1]. God said that days go from one side to another among people, so that He knows who is patient and who strives [c2][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat answer a wound with the reminder that a like wound touched the others [c2]. Another is that the ayat set striving and patience before the entering of the Garden [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the wound was, how many were wounded or killed on either side, or when and where this was.
- Not established: who the witnesses are beyond the ayah's words that God takes witnesses from among the believers.
- Not established: how long the days alternate or how the alternation is counted.
- The ayat do not name the people who wished for death.

claims.statement_en: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed before him; the ayah asks whether, if he died or were killed, they would turn back on their heels; whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful.

No soul dies except by God's leave, at a written, fixed term; whoever wants the reward of this world, God gives him of it, and whoever wants the reward of the Hereafter, God gives him of it, and God will reward the grateful.
How many a prophet fought alongside many devoted followers, who did not lose heart for what befell them in God's way, did not weaken and did not give in; God loves the patient.

Their only words were to ask their Lord to forgive their sins and their excesses in their affair, to make their feet firm and to help them against the disbelieving people; so God gave them the reward of this world and the best reward of the Hereafter, and God loves the doers of good.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that Muhammad is only a messenger, that messengers have passed before him, and ask whether the believers would turn back if he died or were killed [c1]. They add that no soul dies except by God's leave, and tell of earlier followers of prophets who did not lose heart [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed before him [c1]. The ayah asks whether, if he died or were killed, they would turn back on their heels; whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful [c1].

No soul dies except by God's leave, at a written, fixed term [c2]. Whoever wants the reward of this world, God gives him of it, and whoever wants the reward of the Hereafter, God gives him of it, and God will reward the grateful [c2].

How many a prophet fought alongside many devoted followers, who did not lose heart for what befell them in God's way, did not weaken and did not give in; God loves the patient [c3]. Their only words were to ask their Lord to forgive their sins and their excesses in their affair, to make their feet firm and to help them against the disbelieving people [c4]. God gave them the reward of this world and the best reward of the Hereafter, and God loves the doers of good [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah puts the question of turning back in terms of death or being killed, and joins it to the statement that the messengers before him passed away [c1]. The ayat then give the example of earlier prophets and their followers, whose only words are quoted as a prayer for forgiveness, firmness and help [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat remind the believers that Muhammad is a messenger, as messengers came before him [c1]. They tell of followers of earlier prophets who did not lose heart and asked God to forgive them and help them [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat separate loyalty to God from the survival of any one person [c1]. Another is that the example of earlier followers is a prayer for forgiveness and firmness [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what prompted the question about his dying or being killed; the ayah states it as a question only.
- Not established: who the earlier prophets or their followers were, or how many.
- Not established: the date or place of any of these events.
- The ayat do not say how the believers answered.

chapters.title_en: What went wrong, and the pardon

claims.statement_en: God had fulfilled His promise to them when they were destroying their opponents by His leave, until they lost heart, disputed about the order and disobeyed after He had shown them what they love; some wanted this world and some the Hereafter; then He turned them away from them to test them, and He pardoned them; God is full of bounty to the believers.

They were climbing up, turning to no one, while the Messenger was calling them from behind; so He repaid them with distress upon distress, so that they would not grieve over what escaped them or what befell them; God is aware of what they do.

Then after the distress He sent down security, a drowsiness that covered a party of them, while another party were anxious for themselves and thought untruly of God, the thought of ignorance; they asked whether they had any share in the matter, and they were told that the matter is wholly God's.
Those of them who turned away on the day the pair of armies met, it was only Satan who made them slip, because of some of what they had earned; God has pardoned them; God is Forgiving, Forbearing.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that God fulfilled His promise until they lost heart, disputed the order and disobeyed, and that He then tested them and pardoned them [c1]. They say that Satan made those who turned away slip because of some of what they had earned, and that God has pardoned them [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God had fulfilled His promise to them when they were destroying their opponents by His leave, until they lost heart, disputed about the order and disobeyed after He had shown them what they love [c1]. Some wanted this world and some the Hereafter; then He turned them away from them to test them, and He pardoned them [c1].

They were climbing up, turning to no one, while the Messenger was calling them from behind [c2]. So He repaid them with distress upon distress, so that they would not grieve over what escaped them or what befell them [c2].

Then after the distress He sent down security, a drowsiness that covered a party of them, while another party were anxious for themselves and thought untruly of God, the thought of ignorance [c3]. They asked whether they had any share in the matter, and they were told that the matter is wholly God's [c3].

Those of them who turned away on the day the pair of armies met, it was only Satan who made them slip, because of some of what they had earned; God has pardoned them [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give the cause as a sequence: losing heart, disputing about the order and disobeying [c1]. In the same passage the ayat say that God tested them, that He pardoned them, and that He sent down security as drowsiness on a party of them [c1][c3]. The ayah on the day the pair of armies met ties the slip to Satan and to some of what they had earned, and then to God's pardon [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that the believers lost heart and disagreed about an order, and that God tested them [c1]. God then pardoned them and sent down calm on a party of them [c1][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat name the faults plainly and then name the pardon [c1][c4]. Another is that the calm is described as coming after the distress [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the order was, who gave it, who disobeyed it, or how many turned away.
- Not established: where the climbing up took place or who they were running from.
- Not established: who the party that was anxious for themselves were by name.
- The ayat give no casualties, names or commanders.

chapters.title_en: Mercy, the living, and the call

claims.statement_en: It was by a mercy from God that he was gentle with them; had he been harsh and hard-hearted they would have dispersed from around him; so pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, consult them in the matter, and when you have decided, rely on God; God loves those who rely on Him.
If God helps them none can overcome them, and if He forsakes them, no one can help them after Him; let the believers rely on God.

Do not think of those killed in God's way as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, provided for, rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them, that there is no fear on them and they will not grieve.
Those who answered God and the Messenger after the wound had touched them, those of them who did good and feared God, have a great reward.

People said to them that the people had gathered against them, so to fear them; it increased them in faith and they said that God is enough for them and an excellent Disposer of affairs; they returned with favour and bounty from God, no harm touching them, following God's approval.
It is only Satan who makes his allies fear; so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat tell the one addressed to pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, consult them, and rely on God [c1]. They say that those killed in God's way are alive with their Lord, and that those who answered God and the Messenger after the wound have a great reward [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
It was by a mercy from God that he was gentle with them; had he been harsh and hard-hearted they would have dispersed from around him [c1]. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, consult them in the matter, and when you have decided, rely on God; God loves those who rely on Him [c1]. If God helps them none can overcome them, and if He forsakes them, no one can help them after Him; let the believers rely on God [c2].

Do not think of those killed in God's way as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, provided for, rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty [c3]. They rejoice for those who have not yet joined them, that there is no fear on them and they will not grieve [c3].

Those who answered God and the Messenger after the wound had touched them, those of them who did good and feared God, have a great reward [c4]. People said to them that the people had gathered against them, so to fear them; it increased them in faith and they said that God is enough for them and an excellent Disposer of affairs [c5]. They returned with favour and bounty from God, no harm touching them, following God's approval [c5].

It is only Satan who makes his allies fear; so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah on gentleness says that it was a mercy from God, and gives a series of instructions: pardon, ask forgiveness, consult and rely [c1]. The ayat on the living are addressed to the hearer in the singular and speak of those killed in God's way as provided for and rejoicing [c3]. The passage ends by naming fear as the work of Satan upon his allies and telling the believers to fear God instead [c6].
chapters.kids_md: God told the one addressed to pardon them, ask forgiveness for them and rely on God [c1]. The ayat say that those killed in God's way are alive with their Lord [c3]. When people tried to frighten the believers, they said that God is enough for them [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie gentleness to God's mercy, and tie fear to Satan [c1][c6]. Another is that the reply of the believers to those who tried to frighten them was to say that God is enough for them [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the people were who said the people had gathered, or where and when this was said.
- Not established: the manner of the life of those killed in God's way, beyond the ayah's words that they are alive with their Lord and provided for.
- Not established: who he is in 3:159; the ayah speaks of him as gentle and does not name him.
- Not established: whether 3:172-174 speak of a later event or of this one; the ayat describe those who answered after the wound had touched them.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the course of the battle, the archers, the wounded and the individuals involved. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Uhud, and the names of the commanders, the groups and the place; the ayat name neither the day nor the place.
The ayat state no casualties, no dates and no commanders; none are given in this draft.
Not drafted: 3:149-151, 3:156-158 and 3:161-168, which cover warnings to the believers and the hypocrites; they are for a later pass. 3:123-127 are told in the draft for the battle of Badr.
The identification of this whole passage with a single day is from the event inventory and later tradition; the ayat refer to 'the day the pair of armies met' and do not name it.

chapters.title_en: The pledge and the near victory

claims.statement_en: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the one addressed under the tree; He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity on them, rewarded them with a near victory and with abundant gains that they would take; God is Mighty, Wise.

God had promised them abundant gains that they would take; He hastened this one for them and held back the hands of people from them, so that it would be a sign for the believers and guide them to a straight path; and there was another gain that they were not able to take, which God had encompassed; God has power over all things.
Had those who disbelieved fought them, they would have turned their backs and then found no ally or helper; this is God's way that passed before, and no change will be found in God's way.

chapters.summary_md: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance under the tree, and He sent down tranquillity on them and rewarded them with a near victory [c1]. He held back the hands of people from them, and said that no change will be found in His way [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the one addressed under the tree [c1]. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity on them, rewarded them with a near victory and with abundant gains that they would take [c1].

God had promised them abundant gains that they would take; He hastened this one for them and held back the hands of people from them [c2]. This was so that it would be a sign for the believers and guide them to a straight path; and there was another gain that they were not able to take, which God had encompassed [c2].

Had those who disbelieved fought them, they would have turned their backs and then found no ally or helper [c3]. This is God's way that passed before, and no change will be found in God's way [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat link the pledge, God's knowledge of what was in the hearts, the tranquillity and the near victory in one sentence [c1]. They speak of gains in more than one way: gains that are taken now, and another gain they were not able to take, which God had encompassed [c2]. The statement about God's way is given as something that passed before and does not change [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The believers pledged allegiance under a tree, and God was pleased with them [c1]. God sent calm into their hearts and gave them a victory that was near [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie God's pleasure to what He knew in their hearts [c1]. Another is that the ayat speak of God's way as one that does not change [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the tree was, when the pledge was given, or how many pledged; the ayat name neither the place nor the number.
- Not established: what the near victory was, or what the gains were; the ayat say only that they were near and abundant.
- Not established: who the people were whose hands were held back, or whether fighting had begun.
- Not established: whether these ayat describe a treaty; no treaty or its terms are mentioned in the verses cited.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Hudaybiyyah for the place, the treaty and its terms, and the number of those who pledged. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

claims.statement_en: They are those who disbelieved and barred the believers from the inviolable mosque and kept the offering from reaching its place; and had it not been for believing men and believing women whom the believers did not know, whom they might have trampled so that harm would have befallen them without knowing, God would have acted differently; this was so that God would admit into His mercy whom He wills; had they been distinct, God would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.

When those who disbelieved set zeal in their hearts, the zeal of ignorance, God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers and made them keep to the word of piety, of which they were more worthy and more deserving.

God made true the vision of His Messenger: you will enter the inviolable mosque, if God wills, in safety, with your heads shaved or cut short, not fearing; He knew what they did not know, and made, besides that, a near victory.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that those who disbelieved barred the believers from the inviolable mosque, and that God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers [c1][c2]. They say that God made true the vision of His Messenger and made, besides that, a near victory [c3].
chapters.body_md:
They are those who disbelieved and barred the believers from the inviolable mosque and kept the offering from reaching its place [c1]. Had it not been for believing men and believing women whom the believers did not know, whom they might have trampled so that harm would have befallen them without knowing, God would have acted differently [c1]. This was so that God would admit into His mercy whom He wills [c1].

When those who disbelieved set zeal in their hearts, the zeal of ignorance, God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers [c2]. He made them keep to the word of piety, of which they were more worthy and more deserving [c2].

God made true the vision of His Messenger: you will enter the inviolable mosque, if God wills, in safety, with your heads shaved or cut short, not fearing [c3]. He knew what they did not know, and made, besides that, a near victory [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat place a barrier and a reason for restraint side by side: those who barred the believers, and believers among them whom the believers did not know [c1]. The tranquillity is named for the Messenger and the believers together [c2]. The last ayah gives a vision made true, a promise of entering in safety, and a near victory made besides [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Some people kept the believers away from the mosque [c1]. God sent calm to His Messenger and the believers, and said that He made true the vision of His Messenger [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the zeal of ignorance beside the tranquillity God sent down [c2]. Another is that the vision is joined to the words if God wills [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who barred them, where, when, or for how long; the ayat describe the barring and do not name the people or the place.
- Not established: what the offering was or how many were with it, or who the believing men and women they did not know were.
- Not established: when the vision was seen or what it showed beyond the entering and the shaved or shortened heads.
- Not established: whether the entering mentioned in the vision happened in the same year; the ayah says that God made, besides that, a near victory.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the place, the date and the sequence of events that these ayat are linked with.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the pledge, the barring and what followed. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Hudaybiyyah, the treaty, and the names of those involved.

48:24 is not drafted because it names a town, and the town's name is listed as a name from later tradition in the shared fixtures of this repository; a scholar should decide whether the draft may name it.
The Arabic word translated inviolable (a descriptive epithet of the mosque) is often rendered 'sacred'; a scholar should decide. The word translated 'vision' (ru'ya) can also be rendered 'dream'.
The phrase translated 'the word of piety' (kalimat al-taqwa) is rendered closely; its meaning is left to commentary.

claims.statement_en: The ayah says: when those who disbelieved plotted against you to confine you, kill you or drive you out; they plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters.
If you do not help him, God has helped him when those who disbelieved drove him out, as second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: do not grieve, God is with us.
God sent down His tranquillity on him and supported him with forces you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest and the word of God the highest; God is Mighty, Wise.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that those who disbelieved plotted to confine, kill or drive out the one addressed, and that God is the best of plotters [c1]. They say that God helped him when he was in the cave as second of two, and said to his companion: do not grieve, God is with us [c2].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah says: when those who disbelieved plotted against you to confine you, kill you or drive you out; they plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters [c1].

If you do not help him, God has helped him when those who disbelieved drove him out, as second of two, when they were in the cave [c2]. He said to his companion: do not grieve, God is with us [c2].

God sent down His tranquillity on him and supported him with forces you did not see [c3]. He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest and the word of God the highest; God is Mighty, Wise [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The first ayah speaks of a plot with possible ends, to confine, kill or drive out, and puts God's plotting beside theirs [c1]. The second ayah is addressed to those who were told to help him, and reminds them that God helped him already [c2]. The comfort in the cave is spoken to a companion, and the ayah says that the tranquillity was sent down on him [c2][c3].
chapters.kids_md: Those who did not believe made a plan against him, but God is the best of planners [c1]. When he was in the cave he told his companion not to be sad, because God was with them [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah sets the plotting of people beside the plotting of God [c1]. Another is that the words to the companion are words of comfort, because God is with them [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the one driven out and his companion are; the ayah names neither of them.
- Not established: where the cave was, how long they stayed, where they went next or how they travelled.
- Not established: what the forces you did not see were, or what the plot was beyond the possible ends the ayah lists.
- Not established: whether the two ayat describe the same night; they are read here together as the inventory has them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the places, the companion, the route, the date and the details of the plot and the cave.

claims.statement_en: Those who believed, those who emigrated and those who strove in God's way, they hope for God's mercy; God is Forgiving, Merciful.

Those who believed, emigrated and strove with their wealth and themselves in God's way, and those who gave refuge and helped, are allies of one another; they are the believers in truth, and for them is forgiveness and generous provision.
Those who emigrated for God's sake after they were wronged: God will surely settle them in a good place in this world, and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.

A permission was given to those who are fought, because they have been wronged; God is able to help them; they are those who were driven out of their homes without right, only because they said our Lord is God.

Had God not repelled people by means of one another, cloisters, churches, synagogues and mosques in which God's name is often mentioned would have been demolished; God will surely help whoever helps Him; God is strong and mighty.
Those whom God establishes in the land establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong; with God is the outcome of all matters.
The poor emigrants were driven out of their homes and their wealth, seeking bounty and approval from God and helping God and His Messenger; they are the truthful.

Those who had settled in the home and in faith before them love those who emigrated to them and find no need in their hearts for what they were given, and prefer them over themselves even if they are in need; whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul, those are the successful.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat speak of those who believed, emigrated and strove in God's way, and say that they hope for God's mercy [c1]. They speak of the poor emigrants who were driven out of their homes, and of those who had settled in the home before them and loved them [c7][c8].
chapters.body_md:
Those who believed, those who emigrated and those who strove in God's way, they hope for God's mercy; God is Forgiving, Merciful [c1]. Those who believed, emigrated and strove with their wealth and themselves in God's way, and those who gave refuge and helped, are allies of one another [c2]. They are the believers in truth, and for them is forgiveness and generous provision [c2].

Those who emigrated for God's sake after they were wronged: God will surely settle them in a good place in this world, and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew [c3].

A permission was given to those who are fought, because they have been wronged; God is able to help them [c4]. They are those who were driven out of their homes without right, only because they said our Lord is God [c4]. Had God not repelled people by means of one another, cloisters, churches, synagogues and mosques in which God's name is often mentioned would have been demolished; God will surely help whoever helps Him [c5]. Those whom God establishes in the land establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong [c6].

The poor emigrants were driven out of their homes and their wealth, seeking bounty and approval from God and helping God and His Messenger; they are the truthful [c7]. Those who had settled in the home and in faith before them love those who emigrated to them and find no need in their hearts for what they were given, and prefer them over themselves even if they are in need [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The passages use the word for emigrating together with believing and striving, and in places pair it with being wronged or driven out [c1][c3][c7]. The ayat on those who gave refuge describe love for the emigrants and preferring them over themselves, even in need [c8]. The ayat on permission to those who are fought give the reason as wrong done to them and add that God repels some people by means of others [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: Some believers had to leave their homes because they were wronged [c3][c7]. Others who lived in the place they came to loved them and shared with them, even when they were in need themselves [c8]. God says that those who emigrated and strove hope for His mercy [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat praise those who gave refuge and shared, even when in need [c8]. Another is that the ayat set leaving home for God's sake beside the hope of God's mercy [c1][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the emigrants left from, where they went, when, or in what order; the ayat name no place.
- Not established: whether every ayah in this chapter speaks of the same emigration; they are grouped here because the event inventory groups them.
- Not established: who the people who gave refuge were, beyond the ayah's description that they had settled in the home and in faith before.
- Not established: what the permission in 22:39 was for in practice, or at what time it was given; the draft reports the ayat without a legal conclusion.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names of the places of departure and arrival, the groups and the dates.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the emigration, the cave, the route and the settlement. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Medina, and the names of the persons and groups.
The link of 8:30, 9:40, 16:41, 22:39-41, 59:8-9 and 2:218 to a single emigration comes from the event inventory and later tradition; the ayat do not say it.
The identity of the companion in 9:40 and of the one who spoke to him is not in the ayah; this draft does not name them.
The draft for the prophet's own story (content/stories) tells the cave in a chapter of its own; this event draft stays inside its own refs.

chapters.title_en: They came from above and below

claims.statement_en: The believers were told to remember God's favour to them when forces came against them, and God sent a wind upon them and forces they did not see; God sees what they do.
They came upon them from above and from below; the sight swerved, hearts reached the throats, and they thought wrong thoughts about God.
There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.

chapters.summary_md: The believers were told to remember God's favour when forces came, and God sent a wind and forces they did not see [c1]. They came from above and from below, and the believers were tested and shaken [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
The believers were told to remember God's favour to them when forces came against them, and God sent a wind upon them and forces they did not see; God sees what they do [c1].

They came upon them from above and from below; the sight swerved, hearts reached the throats, and they thought wrong thoughts about God [c2]. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah on the wind speaks of a favour to be remembered, and names what God sent: a wind and forces that were not seen [c1]. The next ayat describe the fear: the sight swerved and hearts reached the throats [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The forces came against the believers from above and below, and they were afraid and tested [c2][c3]. God sent a wind and forces they could not see [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat ask the believers to remember a favour at the very moment of fear [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayat do not hide the fear or the wrong thoughts about God [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the forces were, how many, where they came from or where they stood; the ayat say from above and from below and nothing more.
- Not established: what the wind was like, how long it lasted, or what the forces they did not see were.
- Not established: how long the test lasted or how it ended in detail.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the event as a siege, the defensive works, the groups and the dates.

claims.statement_en: The hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts said that God and His Messenger had promised them nothing but delusion.

A party of them said: people of Yathrib, there is no standing for you, so go back; and a group of them asked leave of the Prophet, saying that their houses were exposed, though they were not exposed; they only wanted to flee.

Had their city been entered from its sides and they been asked for sedition, they would have given it, hesitating little; they had made a covenant with God before not to turn their backs, and the covenant with God will be asked about.

They are told: flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will be enjoyed only briefly; who can protect you from God if He intends harm for you or intends mercy for you? They will find no ally or helper besides God.

God knows those among them who hinder others and say to their brothers: come to us; they join the fighting only a little, grudging toward you; when fear comes, they look at you as one overcome by death, and when fear goes, they scald you with sharp tongues, grudging toward good; God made their deeds fruitless.
They think the factions have not gone; if the factions came again, they would wish to be among the desert nomads asking for news of you, and if they were among you, they would fight only a little.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat tell of hypocrites who said that God and His Messenger had promised only delusion, and of a party who told the people of Yathrib to go back [c1][c2]. They say that flight will not benefit them, and that God made the deeds of those who hold back fruitless [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
The hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts said that God and His Messenger had promised them nothing but delusion [c1]. A party of them said: people of Yathrib, there is no standing for you, so go back [c2]. A group of them asked leave of the Prophet, saying that their houses were exposed, though they were not exposed; they only wanted to flee [c2].

Had their city been entered from its sides and they been asked for sedition, they would have given it, hesitating little [c3]. They had made a covenant with God before not to turn their backs, and the covenant with God will be asked about [c3].

They are told: flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will be enjoyed only briefly [c4]. They will find no ally or helper besides God [c4].

God knows those among them who hinder others and say to their brothers: come to us; they join the fighting only a little, grudging toward you [c5]. When fear comes, they look at you as one overcome by death, and when fear goes, they scald you with sharp tongues, grudging toward good; God made their deeds fruitless [c5]. They think the factions have not gone; if the factions came again, they would wish to be among the desert nomads asking for news of you, and if they were among you, they would fight only a little [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat set the words of the hypocrites, their excuse of exposed houses and their earlier covenant side by side [c1][c2][c3]. They answer with a reminder that flight cannot protect from death and that no one can shield from God [c4]. The last ayat describe their conduct in fear and after fear, and give the verdict that God made their deeds fruitless [c5][c6].
chapters.kids_md: Some people who were not sincere said the promise was only a delusion, and tried to leave [c1][c2]. The ayat say that running away cannot save anyone from death, and that no one can shield them from God [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show how fear brings out words that were not believed in the heart [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayat remind them that flight cannot protect from death [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the hypocrites and the party were by name, or how many; the ayat do not name them.
- Not established: which houses were exposed, or whether any attempt to leave was made; the ayah says only what they asked.
- Not established: what covenant they had made before; the ayah says they had pledged not to turn their backs.
- Not established: how long the fear lasted or when the factions went.

claims.statement_en: There is a good example for you in the Messenger of God, for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God much.
When the believers saw the factions, they said: this is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth; it only increased them in faith and submission.
There are men among the believers who were true to what they pledged to God; some have fulfilled their vow and some are still waiting, and they have not changed at all.
This was so that God may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in mercy; God is Forgiving, Merciful.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that there is a good example in the Messenger of God, and that the believers, when they saw the factions, said that this was what God and His Messenger had promised [c1][c2]. They say that it only increased them in faith and submission, and that some were true to what they pledged [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
There is a good example for you in the Messenger of God, for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God much [c1].

When the believers saw the factions, they said: this is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth; it only increased them in faith and submission [c2].

There are men among the believers who were true to what they pledged to God; some have fulfilled their vow and some are still waiting, and they have not changed at all [c3]. This was so that God may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in mercy [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The same sight, the factions, is met with fear in one group of ayat and with increased faith in these [c2]. The ayat distinguish between those who have fulfilled their vow and those who still wait [c3]. They end with the purpose: to reward the truthful and to leave the hypocrites to God's will to punish them or turn to them [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The believers saw the factions and said that this was what God and His Messenger had promised [c2]. It only made them believe more and submit more [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show one sight meeting different hearts [c2]. Another is that the ayat praise men who were true to their pledge to God [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the men who fulfilled their vow are by name, or what the vow was; the ayah says only that they were true to what they pledged.
- Not established: what the promise they recalled was; the ayah says only that it was what God and His Messenger promised.
- Not established: who the ones waiting are, or for what.
- The ayat do not say how the example of the Messenger applies in detail.

claims.statement_en: God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good; and God spared the believers from fighting; God is strong and mighty.
He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them, and cast terror into their hearts; some you killed and some you took captive.
He made them inherit their land, homes and wealth, and a land they had not trodden; God has power over all things.

chapters.summary_md: God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage, and spared the believers from fighting [c1]. He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them, and the ayat say that some were killed and some taken captive [c2].
chapters.body_md:
God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good; and God spared the believers from fighting; God is strong and mighty [c1].

He brought down from their strongholds those of the People of the Book who had backed them, and cast terror into their hearts; some you killed and some you took captive [c2]. He made them inherit their land, homes and wealth, and a land they had not trodden; God has power over all things [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat go from the turning back of the forces to the fate of those who had backed them, and end with what was inherited [c1][c2][c3]. The description of the People of the Book is by what they did, backing the forces, and not by name [c2].
chapters.kids_md: God turned back those who came against the believers, and they gained nothing [c1]. He also dealt with those who had backed them, and made the believers inherit their land [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat end the account with statements about God's strength and power [c1][c3]. Another is that the ayat describe a group by what it did, backing the forces, and then by what befell it [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the People of the Book who backed the forces were, how many were killed or taken captive, or where the strongholds were.
- Not established: what land they had not trodden, or what became of it.
- Not established: the date or the length of the events.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the group, the place and the details of the events that these ayat are linked with; no names are given in the ayat.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the siege, the defences, the groups involved and what followed. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Khandaq for the defensive works, the name Qurayza for the group in 33:26, and the dates.
The ayat give no casualties, no dates and no commanders; none are given in this draft.
The sentence on sedition in 33:14 and the clause on those of the People of the Book in 33:26 are sensitive; a scholar should confirm that the wording stays within what the ayat say.
The prophet drafts (content/stories) are separate; this event draft stays inside its own refs.

stories.title_en: The expulsion of a party of the People of the Book

claims.statement_en: God drove out those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes at the first gathering; the believers did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; take a lesson, you who have sight.
Had God not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
That was because they opposed God and His Messenger; whoever opposes God, God is severe in punishment.
Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.

chapters.summary_md: God drove out those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes, and they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers [c1]. The ayat say that they opposed God and His Messenger, and that God had decreed exile for them [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
God drove out those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes at the first gathering [c1]. The believers did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts [c1]. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers; take a lesson, you who have sight [c1].

Had God not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire [c2]. That was because they opposed God and His Messenger; whoever opposes God, God is severe in punishment [c3].

Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God's leave, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give the believers' view and the expelled party's view of the same event: the believers did not expect them to leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them [c1]. The expulsion is called exile, a thing decreed, and the alternative is stated as punishment in this world [c2]. The ayah on the palm trees says that what was cut or left standing was by God's leave [c4].
chapters.kids_md: A group of the People of the Book had to leave their homes, though they thought their fortresses would protect them [c1]. God said that He had decreed exile for them [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat say that fortresses did not protect them from God, and ask the hearer to take a lesson [c1]. Another is that the ayat give the reason as opposing God and His Messenger [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the party of the People of the Book was by name, where they lived, when they left, or where they went; the ayat describe them and do not name them.
- Not established: what the first gathering was, or how it relates to a later gathering.
- Not established: which palm trees these were, or how many.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the party, the place and the date. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

chapters.title_en: What was returned, and the prayer of those who came after

claims.statement_en: What God returned to His Messenger from them was not something for which the believers had urged horse or camel, but God gives His messengers power over whom He wills; God has power over all things.

Those who came after them say: our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place any resentment in our hearts toward those who believe; our Lord, You are kind and merciful.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that what God returned to His Messenger from them was not gained by the believers urging horse or camel, but that God gives His messengers power over whom He wills [c1]. They record the prayer of those who came after: to forgive them and their brothers who preceded them in faith and to place no resentment in their hearts [c2].
chapters.body_md:
What God returned to His Messenger from them was not something for which the believers had urged horse or camel, but God gives His messengers power over whom He wills; God has power over all things [c1].

Those who came after them say: our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place any resentment in our hearts toward those who believe; our Lord, You are kind and merciful [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The first ayah explains how the matter came about by saying that it was not by urging horse or camel [c1]. The next ayah is a prayer spoken by later believers for those who preceded them in faith [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that God gives His messengers power over whom He wills [c1]. Later believers pray for their brothers who came before them and ask for no resentment in their hearts [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the prayer asks for forgiveness for those who came earlier and for freedom from resentment [c2]. Another is that the first ayah ties the matter to God's power over all things [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what exactly was returned, how it was used, or who received it; the allocation (59:7) is legal in kind and is not drafted here.
- Not established: who those who came after are by name, or when they came.
- Not established: how this prayer relates in time to the expulsion.
- The ayat do not say how much was returned.

claims.statement_en: Those who showed hypocrisy said to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieved: if you are driven out, we will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you; and if you are fought, we will help you; God testifies that they are liars.
If they were driven out, they would not go out with them; if they were fought, they would not help them; and if they helped them, they would turn their backs and then not be helped.
They have more fear of the believers in their hearts than of God, because they are a people who do not understand.

They will not fight the believers all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls; their violence among themselves is severe; you think them united while their hearts are divided, because they are a people who do not reason.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that the hypocrites promised their brothers among the People of the Book to go out with them and to help them, and that God testifies they are liars [c1]. They say that if driven out they would not go out with them, and that if fought they would not help them [c2].
chapters.body_md:
Those who showed hypocrisy said to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieved: if you are driven out, we will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you; and if you are fought, we will help you; God testifies that they are liars [c1].

If they were driven out, they would not go out with them; if they were fought, they would not help them; and if they helped them, they would turn their backs and then not be helped [c2]. They have more fear of the believers in their hearts than of God, because they are a people who do not understand [c3].

They will not fight the believers all together except in fortified towns or from behind walls; their violence among themselves is severe; you think them united while their hearts are divided, because they are a people who do not reason [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat quote the hypocrites' promise and then answer it with God's testimony that they are liars [c1]. They give the answer in a series of conditions: driven out, fought, and helping [c2]. The last ayat explain the failure by what is in the hearts: fear of the believers more than of God, and divided hearts [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: Some people who were not sincere promised their friends to help them, but God said they were not telling the truth [c1]. The ayat say that their hearts were divided [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat show a promise made without sincerity and what happens to it [c1][c2]. Another is that the ayat find the cause in hearts that are divided and do not understand [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the hypocrites were by name, or when and to whom they spoke; the ayat describe them and do not name them.
- Not established: whether the promise was ever put to the test, beyond what the ayat say would happen.
- Not established: where the fortified towns were.
- The ayat do not say how many they were.

chapters.title_en: Like those before, and like Satan

claims.statement_en: They are like those shortly before them who tasted the evil result of their conduct; for them is a painful punishment.
They are like Satan when he said to the human being: disbelieve; then when he disbelieved, he said: I am free of you, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.
The end of both is that they are in the Fire, abiding in it; that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat compare them to those shortly before them who tasted the evil result of their conduct, and to Satan, who said to the human being: disbelieve [c1][c2]. The end of both is the Fire, which is the recompense of the wrongdoers [c3].
chapters.body_md:
They are like those shortly before them who tasted the evil result of their conduct; for them is a painful punishment [c1].

They are like Satan when he said to the human being: disbelieve; then when he disbelieved, he said: I am free of you, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds [c2]. The end of both is that they are in the Fire, abiding in it; that is the recompense of the wrongdoers [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat give comparisons, one with people shortly before them and one with Satan, and draw one ending for both [c1][c2][c3]. The words of Satan are recorded in stages: his saying disbelieve and then his saying that he is free of the one who disbelieved [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that Satan told a human being to disbelieve, and then said he was free of him [c2].
