- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the earlier direction, the occasion of the change and the people who objected. None is used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: God says that He sees the turning of the face of the one addressed toward the sky, and that He will turn him to a qibla that pleases him.
The one addressed is told to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque, and the believers are told to turn their faces in its direction wherever they are.
Those who were given the book know that it is the truth from their Lord, and God is not unaware of what they do.
Even if the one addressed brought to those who were given the book every sign, they would not follow his qibla; nor would he follow theirs; nor do they follow one another's.
If he followed their desires after the knowledge that came to him, he would then be among the wrongdoers.
Those to whom God gave the book recognise it as they recognise their sons, yet a party of them conceal the truth while they know.
The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He sees the one addressed turning his face toward the sky, and that He will turn him to a qibla that pleases him [c1]. The one addressed is told to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque [c2], and the verses say that those who were given the book know that it is the truth from their Lord [c3]. They also say that a party of them conceal the truth while they know [c6].
chapters.body_md:
God says that He sees the turning of the face of the one addressed toward the sky, and that He will turn him to a qibla that pleases him [c1]. The one addressed is told to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque, and the believers are told to turn their faces in its direction wherever they are [c2].

Those who were given the book know that it is the truth from their Lord, and God is not unaware of what they do [c3]. Even if the one addressed brought to them every sign, they would not follow his qibla; nor would he follow theirs; nor do they follow one another's [c4]. If he followed their desires after the knowledge that came to him, he would then be among the wrongdoers [c5].

Those to whom God gave the book recognise it as they recognise their sons, yet a party of them conceal the truth while they know [c6]. The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The verse at 2:144 joins a statement about what God sees to an address to the one addressed and then to the believers [c1][c2]. The pronoun in 'recognise it' in 2:146 is not resolved in the verse [c6]. The verses speak of disagreement about the qibla among those who were given the book, and say that the one addressed is not to follow their desires [c4][c5]. They end with the truth being from the Lord [c7].
chapters.kids_md: God says that He sees the one addressed turning his face toward the sky, and that He will turn him to a direction that pleases him [c1]. He is told to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque [c2]. God says that the truth is from his Lord [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents the direction as the truth from the Lord and warns against following the desires of others after knowledge has come [c5][c7]. Another is that it tells of God seeing the turning of the face of the one addressed and answering it [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which qibla 'a qibla that pleases him' is, where the sacred mosque is, or whether the face was turned in prayer. The word prayer is not in these verses.
- Not established: who 'those who were given the book' are. The verses do not name them.
- Not established: what 'it' is that they recognise (2:146): the Arabic pronoun can be read as the truth, the qibla or a person, and the draft does not decide.
- The Arabic word shatr, rendered 'in the direction of', is read in more than one way.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the people given the book, the place of the sacred mosque, and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: For each there is a direction that he turns toward; so they are to race one another to good things.
God will bring them all together wherever they are; God has power over everything.
From wherever the one addressed goes out he is to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque; it is the truth from his Lord, and God is not unaware of what they do.
The same instruction is given again, with the reason that the people may have no argument against them, except those of them who did wrong; they are not to fear them but to fear God.
A further aim is stated: that God may complete His favour upon them and that they may be guided.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say that for each there is a direction he turns toward, and that they are to race one another to good things [c1]. They repeat that the one addressed is to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque from wherever he goes out [c3][c4]. They give as aims that the people have no argument against them and that God completes His favour upon them [c4][c5].
chapters.body_md:
For each there is a direction that he turns toward; so they are to race one another to good things [c1]. God will bring them all together wherever they are; God has power over everything [c2].

From wherever the one addressed goes out he is to turn his face in the direction of the sacred mosque; it is the truth from his Lord, and God is not unaware of what they do [c3]. The same instruction is given again, with the reason that the people may have no argument against them, except those of them who did wrong; they are not to fear them but to fear God [c4]. A further aim is stated: that God may complete His favour upon them and that they may be guided [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage first says that every one has a direction, then turns that into a call to race to good things [c1]. It says that God will bring them all together wherever they are [c2]. It restates the instruction about the sacred mosque and gives its reasons: truth from the Lord [c3], no argument for the people against them [c4], and the completion of favour and guidance [c5].
chapters.kids_md: God says that for each there is a direction he turns toward, so they are to race to good things [c1]. God says that wherever they are, He will bring them all together [c2]. He says that He will complete His favour upon them [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage answers differences of direction with a call to race to good things [c1]. Another is that it ends by naming the completion of favour and guidance as the aim [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what 'each' (2:148) refers to, or whether 'a direction' there means a qibla or something wider; the Arabic word can be read both ways.
- Not established: who 'those of them who did wrong' are, or what argument they might make.
- Not established: how the repeated instruction in 2:149 and 2:150 relates to the first (2:144); the draft states each as the verse says it.
- The word prayer is not in these verses, and the draft does not add it.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion, the people who argued and the place. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of the change, on the earlier and the later direction and on the people who objected, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
The word prayer is not in 2:142-150; the draft says qibla (the direction faced). How the page links the passage to prayer is for the reviewer.
The Arabic shatr and the pronoun in 2:146 are left open; see the unknowns of the chapters.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: The likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam: God created him from dust, then said to him "Be", and he was.
The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters.

The one addressed is told that if anyone argues with him about him after the knowledge that has come to him, he is to say: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves.
Then let them earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say that the likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam [c1], and that the truth is from the Lord of the one addressed [c2]. They tell him what to say to anyone who argues with him: let each side call their sons, their women and themselves, and earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
The likeness of Isa with God is like the likeness of Adam: God created him from dust, then said to him "Be", and he was [c1]. The truth is from the Lord of the one addressed, so he is not to be among the doubters [c2].

The one addressed is told that if anyone argues with him about him after the knowledge that has come to him, he is to say: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves [c3]. Then let them earnestly supplicate, and put the curse of God upon the liars [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passage begins with a likeness and ends with an invitation [c1][c3]. The pronoun in 'about him' is not resolved in the verse; it can be read as Isa or as the truth stated before it [c3]. The invitation names groups to be called, sons, women and ourselves, and leaves the persons unnamed [c3]. What follows the supplication is a curse upon the liars, and the verse says no more [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The verses say that God made Isa like He made Adam: from dust, then He said "Be", and he was [c1]. They say that the truth is from the Lord [c2]. They tell what to say to those who argue: come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage meets an argument with an invitation to turn together to God [c3][c4]. Another is that it begins from a likeness, Isa and Adam, before it turns to the invitation [c1][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who argued, where, or when. The verse says 'anyone who argues with you about him'.
- Not established: whether the invitation was carried out, who came, or how it ended; the verses do not say.
- Not established: who 'our sons', 'our women' and 'ourselves' refer to.
- The pronoun in 'about him' (3:61) is read in more than one way; the draft does not decide.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the people who argued, the people called, the place and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of the invitation, on those who argued and on those who were called, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
The inventory title calls the passage the invitation to mutual invocation; the verses state the invitation and say nothing of its outcome.
The pronoun in 'about him' (3:61) is left open; see the unknowns.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: God has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God.
God hears the exchange that took place, for God is hearing and seeing.

Of those among them who make this declaration about their wives, God says that the wives are not their mothers, that their mothers are only those who bore them, and that they say an objectionable word and a falsehood.
God is pardoning and forgiving.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God [c1]. God hears the exchange, and is hearing and seeing [c2]. Of those who make this declaration about their wives, He says that the wives are not their mothers [c3], and that God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God [c1]. God hears the exchange that took place, for God is hearing and seeing [c2].

Of those among them who make this declaration about their wives, God says that the wives are not their mothers, that their mothers are only those who bore them, and that they say an objectionable word and a falsehood [c3]. God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The first verse says what God has heard and that He is hearing and seeing [c1][c2]. The woman is not named and her words are not given [c1]. The verse at 58:2 speaks of a declaration by men about their wives, and names it by the Arabic verb yuzahirun; the verse does not spell out the words of the declaration [c3]. It ends with God's names pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God says that He has heard the woman who disputes about her husband and complains to Him [c1]. God hears and sees everything that is said [c2]. God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage begins with God hearing a complaint made to Him [c1][c2]. Another is that it calls an objectionable word an objectionable word, and ends with pardon and forgiveness [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the woman is, who her husband is, what she said, or when and where it happened. The verse says 'the woman who disputes' and names no one.
- Not established: who the one addressed is. The verse says 'you' and does not name him.
- Not established: what the declaration of 58:2 consisted of in words. The verb is yuzahirun and the verse does not spell it out.
- This chapter does not restate 58:3-4, which set out what follows for those who make the declaration. They are left to a scholar to present or not, in the verses' own words; the draft states no judgement on them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the woman, of her husband, and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of these ayat, on who the woman was and on what was said, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

The verses 58:3-4 are inside the inventory refs but are not drafted: they set out provisions for those who made the declaration, and the draft leaves any statement of them to a scholar. This is reported, not hidden.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the woman and of her husband.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: Those who brought the ifk, a grave falsehood, were a group among those addressed.
They are told not to think it bad for them; rather it is good for them.
Each of them will have what he earned of sin, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself has a great punishment.
The verse asks why, when they heard it, the believing men and women did not think well of themselves and say that this is a clear lie.
The verse asks why they did not bring four witnesses for it; since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in God's sight, are the liars.
Were it not for the favour of God upon them and His mercy, in this world and the hereafter, a great punishment would have touched them for what they plunged into.
They received it with their tongues and said with their mouths what they had no knowledge of, and counted it light, while with God it is grave.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say that a group among those addressed brought a grave falsehood, the ifk [c1]. They say that the believing men and women should have thought well and said that it is a clear lie [c4], and that, since the witnesses were not brought, those are the liars in God's sight [c5]. They say that without God's favour and mercy a great punishment would have touched them [c6].
chapters.body_md:
Those who brought the ifk, a grave falsehood, were a group among those addressed [c1]. They are told not to think it bad for them; rather it is good for them [c2]. Each of them will have what he earned of sin, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself has a great punishment [c3].

The verse asks why, when they heard it, the believing men and women did not think well of themselves and say that this is a clear lie [c4]. It asks why they did not bring four witnesses for it; since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in God's sight, are the liars [c5].

Were it not for the favour of God upon them and His mercy, in this world and the hereafter, a great punishment would have touched them for what they plunged into [c6]. They received it with their tongues and said with their mouths what they had no knowledge of, and counted it light, while with God it is grave [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The verses name no person and give no content of the falsehood; they speak of a group, of each one's share, and of the one who took the greater part [c1][c3]. The passage turns from those who brought it to those who heard it, and asks what the hearers should have done [c4][c5]. It states in its own words that those who did not bring the witnesses are the liars in God's sight [c5]. It also speaks of passing on, with the tongue and the mouth, what one has no knowledge of, and of counting light what is grave with God [c7].
chapters.kids_md: The verses say that a group brought a grave falsehood [c1]. They say that when the believers heard it they should have thought well and said that it is a clear lie [c4]. They say that what one has no knowledge of is grave with God, even if people count it light [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage turns attention from those who spread a falsehood to what those who hear it should do [c4]. Another is that it names saying what one has no knowledge of as grave with God [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the falsehood said, whom it concerned, who the group was, who took the greater part of it, or when and where it happened. The verses name no one, and this draft names no one.
- Not established: what 'think well of themselves' covers; the Arabic says 'of their own selves', and the verse does not say more.
- The verse about the witnesses (24:13) is stated here as it is written, and the draft draws no further conclusion from it.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an occasion for these verses, the person the falsehood concerned and the persons given as having spread it. None is used, and this draft names no one.

claims.statement_en: The verse asks why, when they heard it, they did not say that it is not for them to speak of this, glory be to God, this is a great slander.
God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers.
God makes the signs clear to them, and God is knowing and wise.
Those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe have a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter; God knows and they do not know.
The verse repeats 'were it not for the favour of God upon you and His mercy', and says that God is kind and merciful.

chapters.summary_md: The verses ask why the hearers did not say that it is not for them to speak of this, and that it is a great slander [c1]. God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers [c2]. They end with God's favour and mercy [c5].
chapters.body_md:
The verse asks why, when they heard it, they did not say that it is not for them to speak of this, glory be to God, this is a great slander [c1].

God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers [c2]. God makes the signs clear to them, and God is knowing and wise [c3].

Those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe have a painful punishment in this world and the hereafter; God knows and they do not know [c4]. The passage ends by repeating that it is by the favour of God upon them and His mercy, and that God is kind and merciful [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage gives words that the hearers might have said, and calls the falsehood a great slander [c1]. It then admonishes and turns to a wider warning about those who love that indecency should spread [c2][c4]. The verse about those who love that it spread speaks of them and not of those who brought the falsehood [c4]. The passage closes with favour and mercy, as it did in the earlier verses [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The verses ask why the hearers did not say that it is not for them to speak of this [c1]. God admonishes them never to return to the like of it, if they are believers [c2]. God makes the signs clear, and God is knowing and wise [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage gives the hearers words to say as well as a warning [c1][c2]. Another is that it ends, as it began, by pointing to God's favour and mercy [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what 'indecency' refers to here, or how it relates to the falsehood of the previous chapter; the verse speaks of those who love that it spread.
- Not established: who 'they' are who are admonished, beyond those addressed in the passage.
- Not established: which 'signs' God makes clear.
- Not established: how the punishment in this world and the hereafter is carried out; the verse says only that it is painful.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion and the persons concerned. None is used, and this draft names no one.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of these ayat, each with a named grader, to be added by an editor after review. None is used in this draft, and no name is given in it.

This story is drafted with the greatest restraint. It states what the verses say and the Quran's declaration in its own words (24:13), names no one, gives no content to the falsehood and draws no conclusion from the verses.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion of the passage, the person the falsehood concerned and the persons given as having spread it.
The sense of the Arabic ifk (a grave falsehood), of 'think well of themselves' (24:12) and of the word rendered 'indecency' (24:19) is for the reviewer.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

stories.title_en: The matter of Zayd and adoptive sonship

chapters.title_en: When God and His messenger decide

claims.statement_en: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His messenger have decided a matter, to have the choice in their affair.
Whoever disobeys God and His messenger has clearly gone astray.
The verse recalls what the one addressed said to the man on whom God had bestowed favour and on whom the one addressed had bestowed favour: keep your wife for yourself, and fear God.
The one addressed was concealing within himself what God was going to bring to light, and was fearing the people, though God has more right to be feared.
When Zayd had accomplished a need from her, God gave her to the one addressed in marriage.
The reason given is that there should be no blame on the believers regarding the wives of those they have adopted as sons, when these have accomplished a need from them.
The command of God is carried out.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say that when God and His messenger have decided a matter, a believing man or woman has no choice in their affair [c1]. They recall what the one addressed said to a man who had been favoured, and say that when Zayd had accomplished a need from her, God gave her to the one addressed in marriage [c3][c5]. They give as the reason that there should be no blame on the believers regarding the wives of those they have adopted as sons [c6].
chapters.body_md:
It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His messenger have decided a matter, to have the choice in their affair [c1]. Whoever disobeys God and His messenger has clearly gone astray [c2].

The next verse recalls what the one addressed said to the man on whom God had bestowed favour and on whom the one addressed had bestowed favour: keep your wife for yourself, and fear God [c3]. The one addressed was concealing within himself what God was going to bring to light, and was fearing the people, though God has more right to be feared [c4].

When Zayd had accomplished a need from her, God gave her to the one addressed in marriage [c5]. The reason given is that there should be no blame on the believers regarding the wives of those they have adopted as sons, when these have accomplished a need from them [c6]. The command of God is carried out [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passage opens with a statement about God's decision and the choice of believers, and moves to a particular matter without saying that they are connected [c1][c3]. The verse names Zayd only in its later sentence; the man to whom the words were said is first described by the favours he received [c3][c5]. The woman is not named [c3][c5]. The verse does not say what the one addressed was concealing, and does not spell out what the 'need' (watar) was [c4][c5]. The reason it gives concerns the believers and the wives of those they have adopted as sons [c6].
chapters.kids_md: The verses say that when God and His messenger have decided a matter, believers have no choice in it [c1]. They say that God has more right to be feared than the people [c4]. They say that the command of God is carried out [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets the fear of God above the fear of the people [c4]. Another is that it begins from the decision of God and His messenger and ends with the command of God being carried out [c1][c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the one addressed is; the verse says 'you' and does not name him.
- Not established: who the man is on whom God and the one addressed had bestowed favour. The verse names Zayd only in its later sentence; that he is the same man is the natural reading, but the Arabic leaves it to the context.
- Not established: whose wife is meant by 'your wife' and 'her'. The verses name no woman.
- Not established: what the one addressed was concealing; the verse says 'what God was going to bring to light' and does not say what it was.
- Not established: what 'accomplished a need' covers. The verse does not say in words what took place between Zayd and his wife, and the draft keeps the verse's wording.
- Not established: when or where this took place, or whether the decision in 33:36 is about the same matter as 33:37.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names and circumstances of the persons in 33:36-37 and the occasion of the passage. This draft names no one beyond the name the verse itself gives, and states no conclusion about adoption beyond the words of 33:37.

chapters.title_en: No blame, and the seal of the prophets

claims.statement_en: There is no blame on the prophet in what God has ordained for him; this is the way of God among those who passed before, and the command of God is a decree decreed.
Those who convey the messages of God, fear Him and fear no one but God are described; God suffices as one who takes account.
Muhammad was not the father of any of the men among those addressed, but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets; God has knowledge of all things.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say that there is no blame on the prophet in what God has ordained for him, and that this is the way of God among those who passed before [c1]. They describe those who convey the messages of God and fear none but Him [c2]. They say that Muhammad was not the father of any of the men among those addressed, but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets [c3].
chapters.body_md:
There is no blame on the prophet in what God has ordained for him; this is the way of God among those who passed before, and the command of God is a decree decreed [c1].

The next verse describes those who convey the messages of God, fear Him and fear no one but God; God suffices as one who takes account [c2].

The passage ends by saying that Muhammad was not the father of any of the men among those addressed, but the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets, and that God has knowledge of all things [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The verse at 33:38 speaks of what God has ordained for the prophet and ties it to the way of God among those who passed before [c1]. The verse at 33:39 describes a kind of person by what they convey and whom they fear [c2]. The last states what Muhammad was not and what he was, in the words of the verse [c3]. The word rendered 'seal' is read in more than one way in the recitations, and the draft keeps the rendering of the verse [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The verses say that there is no blame on the prophet in what God has ordained for him [c1]. They say that those who convey the messages of God fear Him and fear no one but God [c2]. They say that God has knowledge of all things [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins conveying the messages of God with fearing none but Him [c2]. Another is that it ends by naming the messenger of God and the seal of the prophets and by placing all knowledge with God [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what 'what God has ordained for him' (33:38) refers to; the verse does not say.
- Not established: how 33:38-40 relate to the matter of 33:36-37 beyond standing in the same passage. The draft places them together because they are in one passage and does not say that one explains the other.
- Not established: who the prophet of 33:38 is, beyond the name given in 33:40; the verses use the title and the name in different places.
- The Arabic word rendered 'seal' is read in more than one way; a scholar should decide how the page words it.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion of these verses. It is not used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of 33:36-37, on the persons concerned and on how the passage was understood, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

This story is drafted with the greatest restraint. It states only what the verses say, names no one except Zayd and Muhammad, whom the verses name, and states no legal conclusion about adoption or marriage; the verses are given in their own words and the page should not add to them without review.
The Arabic word watar ('need', 33:37) is kept general. The verse does not say in so many words what took place, and the draft says nothing that the verse does not.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the woman and of the one addressed, and the circumstances of the passage.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

claims.statement_en: There are those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of lying in wait for one who had fought God and His messenger before.
They will swear that they wanted only the best, and God bears witness that they are liars.
The one addressed is told never to stand in it.
A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy of his standing in it; in it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.

The verse asks whether one who founded his building on fear of God and His approval is better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, which collapsed with him into the fire of Hell; God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts, until their hearts are cut into pieces; God is knowing and wise.

chapters.summary_md: The verses speak of those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief and for dividing the believers [c1]. They say that God bears witness that these people are liars when they swear that they wanted only the best [c2]. The one addressed is told never to stand in it [c3], and the verses speak of a mosque founded on piety from the first day [c4].
chapters.body_md:
There are those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of lying in wait for one who had fought God and His messenger before [c1]. They will swear that they wanted only the best, and God bears witness that they are liars [c2].

The one addressed is told never to stand in it [c3]. A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy of his standing in it; in it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves [c4].

The verse asks whether one who founded his building on fear of God and His approval is better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, which collapsed with him into the fire of Hell; God does not guide the wrongdoing people [c5]. The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts, until their hearts are cut into pieces; God is knowing and wise [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The passage names the purposes of those who built it: harm, disbelief, division and lying in wait [c1]. It reports what they will swear and God's witness against it [c2]. It then sets buildings side by side, one founded on piety and one on the edge of a crumbling bank [c4][c5]. It does not name the builders, the place, or the one they lay in wait for [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The verses speak of people who took a mosque for harm and to divide the believers [c1]. They say that a mosque founded on piety is more worthy [c4]. They say that in it are men who love to purify themselves, and that God loves those who purify themselves [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage judges a building by what it was founded on: piety and God's approval on one side, harm and division on the other [c1][c5]. Another is that it speaks of purifying oneself as something God loves [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the mosque stood, who built it, when, or what became of it. The verses give none of this.
- Not established: who 'one who had fought God and His messenger before' is.
- Not established: which mosque is 'founded on piety from the first day', or who the men are who love to purify themselves.
- Not established: whether 'stand in it' refers to prayer; the verse says only 'stand'.
- Not established: what the 'doubt in their hearts' refers to beyond the words of 9:110.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the builders, the place, the occasion and what followed. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of these ayat, on the builders and the place and on what was done with the building, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
The statement about those who built it (9:107) and the image of 9:109 are stated in the verses' own words; a scholar should decide whether the kids text should keep them.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the builders, of the one they lay in wait for and of the mosque founded on piety.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

stories.title_en: The declaration of release from the treaties

claims.statement_en: A release from God and His messenger to those among the ones who associate partners with God with whom treaties were made.

A command is given to travel freely in the land for four months, with the words 'know that you cannot frustrate God and that God will disgrace the disbelievers'; the verse does not name who is addressed.
A proclamation from God and His messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage says that God is free of those who associate partners, and so is His messenger.
If they repent it is better for them, and if they turn away they are to know that they cannot frustrate God; good news of a painful punishment is to be given to those who disbelieved.

The exception is for those among them with whom a treaty was made, who then did not diminish anything toward those addressed and did not support anyone against them: their treaty is to be completed to its term; God loves those who are mindful of Him.

chapters.summary_md: The verses open with a release from God and His messenger to those among the ones who associate partners with whom treaties were made [c1]. They give a command to travel freely in the land for four months [c2], and a proclamation on the day of the greater pilgrimage [c3]. They except those who kept their treaty, and say that it is to be completed to its term [c5].
chapters.body_md:
The passage opens with a release from God and His messenger to those among the ones who associate partners with God with whom treaties were made [c1].

A command is given to travel freely in the land for four months, with the words know that you cannot frustrate God and that God will disgrace the disbelievers; the verse does not name who is addressed [c2]. A proclamation from God and His messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage says that God is free of those who associate partners, and so is His messenger [c3]. If they repent it is better for them, and if they turn away they are to know that they cannot frustrate God; good news of a painful punishment is to be given to those who disbelieved [c4].

The exception is for those among them with whom a treaty was made, who then did not diminish anything toward those addressed and did not support anyone against them: their treaty is to be completed to its term; God loves those who are mindful of Him [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage has a release [c1], a period of four months [c2], a proclamation [c3], a call to repent [c4] and an exception [c5]. The verse that gives the four months does not name who is addressed [c2]. The exception is for those who kept their treaty and did not support anyone against those addressed, and for them the treaty is to be completed to its term [c5]. The verse ends with God loving those who are mindful of Him [c5].
chapters.kids_md: The passage opens with a release from treaties, from God and His messenger [c1]. It gives four months to travel freely in the land [c2]. It says that those who kept their treaty are to have it completed to its term, and that God loves those who are mindful of Him [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage separates those who kept a treaty from those who did not, and gives the first a treaty completed to its term [c5]. Another is that it ends with God's love for those who are mindful of Him [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which treaties are meant, with which groups, or when and where the proclamation was made. The verses say 'those among the ones who associate partners with whom treaties were made'.
- Not established: who is addressed in 9:2 and from when the four months run.
- Not established: what 'the day of the greater pilgrimage' is; the verse names it and does not date it.
- Not established: who the people are who did not diminish anything and did not support anyone; the verse says 'those among them'.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion, the year, the groups and the persons concerned. None is used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: When the sacred months have passed, those addressed are told to kill those who associate partners wherever they find them, to seize them, to besiege them and to sit in wait for them at every place of ambush.
If they repent, establish the prayer and give the zakat, those addressed are to let them go on their way; God is forgiving and merciful.

If any one of those who associate partners asks the one addressed for protection, he is to give him protection until he hears the word of God, then convey him to his place of safety; that is because they are a people who do not know.

chapters.summary_md: The verses say what is to be done when the sacred months have passed [c1], and that those who repent, establish the prayer and give the zakat are to be let go on their way [c2]. They also say that if any one of them asks for protection, he is to be given protection until he hears the word of God, and then conveyed to his place of safety [c3].
chapters.body_md:
When the sacred months have passed, those addressed are told to kill those who associate partners wherever they find them, to seize them, to besiege them and to sit in wait for them at every place of ambush [c1]. If they repent, establish the prayer and give the zakat, those addressed are to let them go on their way; God is forgiving and merciful [c2].

If any one of those who associate partners asks the one addressed for protection, he is to give him protection until he hears the word of God, then convey him to his place of safety; that is because they are a people who do not know [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The passage gives a time, the passing of the sacred months, and what is to be done after it [c1]. It names what ends the matter for those who repent: they are let go on their way [c2]. The verse that follows at once speaks of a different case, one who asks for protection, and gives the reason in the words that they are a people who do not know [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The passage says that if one of them asks for protection, he is to be given protection until he hears the word of God [c3]. Then he is to be taken to his place of safety [c3]. The passage ends by saying that God is forgiving and merciful [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage includes, beside its commands, a verse about protection for one who asks for it, until he hears the word of God [c3]. Another is that the passage speaks of repenting and of God as forgiving and merciful [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which groups the verses apply to, beyond the phrase 'those who associate partners', or when the sacred months are counted from; the verses do not say.
- Not established: how the verses are to be applied, by whom or in what circumstances. This draft states what the verses say and no conclusion from them.
- Not established: what repenting consists of beyond the words of 9:5.
- 9:5 and 9:6 stand beside 9:4, which excepts those who kept their treaty, and beside 9:1-3; a scholar should decide how the page shows the verses together, and whether the verses after 9:6 should be added.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the occasion, the year, the groups and the persons concerned. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion and the year of the declaration, on the groups and the treaties concerned and on the application of the verses, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

This story is drafted with restraint. 9:5 is stated in its own words and is kept beside the verses on either side of it; it must not be shown alone, and a scholar should check first how the page words it and how it is placed.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the groups, the treaties, the date and the persons concerned.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

stories.title_en: The announcement that the religion is completed

claims.statement_en: The verse says that today those who disbelieved have despaired of the religion of those addressed.
Those addressed are told not to fear them but to fear God.
God says that today He has completed their religion for them, has completed His favour upon them, and has approved Islam as their religion.

chapters.summary_md: The verse says that today those who disbelieved have despaired of the religion of those addressed [c1]. They are told not to fear them but to fear God [c2]. God says that today He has completed their religion, completed His favour upon them, and approved Islam as their religion [c3].
chapters.body_md:
The verse says that today those who disbelieved have despaired of the religion of those addressed [c1]. Those addressed are told not to fear them but to fear God [c2].

God says that today He has completed their religion for them, has completed His favour upon them, and has approved Islam as their religion [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The statement has parts: what those who disbelieved have done, what those addressed are told, and what God says He has done [c1][c2][c3]. The verse says 'today' and does not give a date [c1][c3]. It does not say what was completed or in what way, only that the religion and the favour were completed [c3]. The same verse contains other matters, which this draft does not restate [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God says that today He has completed their religion for them [c3]. God says that today He has completed His favour upon them [c3]. God says that He has approved Islam as their religion, and they are told to fear God [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verse sets the fear of God against the fear of those who disbelieved [c2]. Another is that it speaks of completion and favour together and puts both with God [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which day 'today' is, or where it was. The verse gives no date or place.
- Not established: what was completed or how, or what 'despaired of your religion' says about what those who disbelieved had hoped for.
- The same verse also names things made forbidden and a case of need. They are not restated in this chapter, whose subject is the announcement; a scholar should decide whether the page shows the verse whole.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the day, the place and the occasion of the announcement. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the day, the place and the occasion of the announcement, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

This chapter quotes only the announcement within 5:3 and leaves out the rest of the verse (the provisions on what is forbidden and the case of need). A scholar should decide whether partial citation of the verse is acceptable on the page.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the day and place of the announcement.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
